Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 12, verse 7–18:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, in Joseph and his brothers there are signs for those who inquire﴾. That is, in his story and the story of his brothers. Their names: Ruben, who was the eldest of them; Simeon; Levi; Judah; Zebulun; and Issachar. Their mother was Leah, daughter of Ayan, who was the paternal cousin of Jacob. He had four more sons from two concubines, one named Zad and the other Milda: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. Then Leah died, and Jacob married her sister Rachel, who bore him Joseph and Benjamin. The sons of Jacob were twelve men.

﴿Signs﴾: the people of Mecca read "āyah" in the singular, meaning admonition and lesson. It was also said that it means wonder, as one says, "So-and-so is an āyah in beauty and knowledge," meaning a marvel. The rest read ﴿āyāt﴾ in the plural. ﴿For those who inquire﴾: this is because the Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the story of Joseph, and he informed them of it as it is in the Torah. They were amazed by it and said: "From where do you have this, O Muhammad?" He said: "My Lord taught it to me." [109]

It was also said that its meaning is "for those who inquire and for those who do not inquire," like His saying: ﴿alike to those who ask﴾.

﴿When they said: "Joseph and his brother Benjamin are dearer to our father than we are, though we are a band (ʿuṣbah)."﴾ The lam in ﴿la-Yūsufu﴾ is the answer to an oath; its sense is: "By Allah, Joseph and his brother..." ʿUṣbah means a group. It has been said it ranges from one to ten, and it was said up to fifteen, and it was said from ten to forty. It has no singular from its own root, like nafar and raht. ﴿Indeed our father is in manifest error﴾: a clear mistake in his preference of Joseph and his brother over us.

﴿Kill Joseph, or cast him out to some land, so that your father's face will be turned to you alone, and after that you will be a righteous people.﴾ The scholars differed about the speaker of this statement. Wahb said: Simeon said it. Kaʿb said: Dan. Muqatil said: Ruben. ﴿So that your father's face will be turned to you﴾: away from preoccupation with Joseph, for he has occupied him away from us and turned his face toward him instead of us. ﴿And after him you will be a righteous people﴾: after killing Joseph, repentant. Muqatil said: he will set right your affairs between yourselves and your father.

A speaker from among them said — he was Ruben; al-Suddi said it was Judah, and he was the greatest of them and was Joseph's maternal cousin, and he was the best of them in his opinion. He forbade them from killing him and said: ﴿Do not kill Joseph; but if you must act, cast him into the bottom of the well﴾: that is, into the depth and darkness of the well where his news will be hidden. Qatadah said: at its bottom. The ghayabah is everything that conceals something, and its root is from ghaybubah (concealment). The people of Medina read ﴿ghayabāt al-jubb﴾ in the plural; the rest read ﴿ghayabat﴾ in the singular. The jubb is a well that is not lined with stones. Qatadah said it is the well of Jerusalem. Wahb said it is in the land of Jordan. Kaʿb said: between Midian and Egypt. Muqatil said: three farsakhs from Jacob's dwelling.

﴿Some travellers will pick him up﴾: they will take him. The common reading uses the yāʾ because the subject is "some" (baʿḍ). Al-Hasan read ﴿taltaqiṭhu﴾ with the tāʾ because of ﴿al-sayyārah﴾ (the caravan). The Arabs do this in every report where the subject is a part of a feminine noun-phrase, so that the verb agrees with the whole, as the poet says:

"I see the passing years have taken from me
as the crescent loses its light to the moon."
[Lisan al-ʿArab: 8/73; Sharh Ibn ʿAqil: 1/64.]

He did not say "akhadhat"... Another poet says:

"When one of them dies, a chief arises,
and the people of the villages and churches submit to him."
[Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/205.]

﴿Some of the travellers﴾: some passers-by on the road who would take him to another region, and his news would be concealed. ﴿If you are going to do [anything]﴾ what I tell you.

It was said to al-Hasan: "Can a believer envy?" He said: "What makes you forget the sons of Jacob?" That is why it is said: "The father is a bringer-in, and the brother is a plunderer." Then they agreed upon separating him from his father by some kind of trickery. They said to Jacob: ﴿O our father, what is wrong with you that you do not entrust us with Joseph, though we are indeed his sincere well-wishers?﴾ Abu Jaʿfar read the nūn (tāmannā-na), and the rest read it with ishmām of the nūn toward the ḍammah (a faint rounding), which was chosen by Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Ḥātim, because its origin is ta'mannunā with two nūns, one of which was assimilated into the other.

﴿And indeed we are his sincere well-wishers﴾: we will protect him and guard him until we return him to you. Muqatil said: there is inversion and transposition in the speech, for Joseph's brothers said to their father: ﴿Send him with us tomorrow; he will enjoy himself and play, and indeed we will surely guard him.﴾ Their father said: ﴿Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him away, and I fear that the wolf will devour him while you are heedless of him.﴾ Then they said: ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not entrust us with Joseph, though we are indeed his sincere well-wishers? Send him with us tomorrow to the open country, to enjoy himself and play.﴾

Abu ʿAmr read the nūn in both, and so did Ibn ʿAmir. Hārūn said: I said to Abu ʿAmr, "How do you read nartaʿ and nalʿab when they were prophets?" He said: "They were not prophets at that time." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/206.] The people of Kufa read both with the yāʾ, meaning "he will enjoy himself, eat, be active and play." It is said: "ratiʿa fulān fī mālih" when he enjoys his wealth and spends it on his desires. Al-Qaṭṭāmi said:

"Do you disbelieve after the death was turned back from me,
and after your gift of the hundred camels of the herd?"
[Lisan al-ʿArab: 15/69.]

Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is that he herds his sheep, observes and understands, so that he knows what a man knows. [Ibid.]

Yaʿqub read ﴿narta' ﴾ with the nūn and ﴿yalʿab﴾ with the yāʾ, returning the play to Joseph and the enjoyment to his brothers. The people of the Hijaz read ﴿nartaʿi﴾ with the kasrah on the ʿayn, from al-irtiʿāʾ, meaning: we keep watch, and each protects the other. ﴿And indeed we are his guardians.﴾

Jacob said to them: ﴿Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him away﴾: that is, your going. ﴿And I fear that the wolf will devour him while you are heedless of him﴾: you are not aware. He had seen in a dream that the wolf had attacked Joseph, and he had been wary of this. Hence he said this, and so he gave them the reason, but they did not realize it. They said: ﴿If the wolf devours him while we are a band﴾: ten men, ﴿then indeed we would be losers﴾: weak, incapable, defrauded.

﴿So when they had taken him away﴾: there is an omission and abbreviation in the speech; its sense is: so he sent him with them, and when they had taken him away, ﴿and agreed﴾: resolved ﴿to put him into the bottom of the well﴾. ﴿And We revealed to him﴾: this waw is superfluous and inserted; the sense is: "We revealed," as in His saying: ﴿So when they both submitted, and He threw him down upon his forehead, We called out to him﴾, meaning: We called out to him. Imru' al-Qays said:

"When we passed the courtyard of the tribe and it veered
with us into the valley of the sandy hills of ʿaqanqal..."
[Gharib al-Hadith: 2/188.]

He meant "veered" (intaḥā).

﴿You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs, while they do not perceive﴾: that is, We revealed to Joseph, "Your dream will come true, and you will surely inform your brothers of their deed and of what they did to you, while they do not perceive the revelation of Allah to him or His informing him of that." This is the meaning of Mujahid's statement. It was also said [by Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas, Zad al-Masir: 4/147]: its meaning is ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ that you are Joseph.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: When Joseph's brothers entered upon Joseph, ﴿he recognized them, but they did not recognize him﴾, he called for the drinking-cup, placed it on his hand, then struck it and it resonated. He said: "This cup informs me that you had a brother from your father called Joseph, whom he favoured over you, and that you took him and cast him into the bottom of the well, then came to your father and said: 'The wolf has eaten him,' and sold him ﴿for a paltry price﴾. That is His saying: ﴿You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs, while they do not perceive.﴾"

Al-Suddi said: Jacob sent Joseph with them, and they took him out, and he had honour over them. When they went out into the wilderness they showed him enmity. His brother began to strike him, and he would call for help to the other, who would strike him too. He found no mercy from them, and they beat him until they nearly killed him. He began to cry out and say: "O father, O Jacob! If you knew what these sons are doing to your son!"

When they were nearly about to kill him, Judah said: "Did we not take from our father a covenant that you would not kill him?" So they took him to the well to cast him down. They began to lower him into the well, and he clung to its edge. They tied his hands and stripped off his shirt. He said: "O my brothers, return my shirt to me, that I may cover myself with it in the well." They said: "Call upon the sun, the moon, and the eleven stars, and they will keep you company." He said: "Indeed, I see nothing."

They lowered him into the well until he reached halfway down, then let him fall, intending that he would die. There was water in the well, and he fell into it, then he took refuge on a rock in it and stood upon it. When they cast him into the well, he began to weep, and they called to him. He thought it was mercy that had come to them, so he answered them. They wanted to crush him with a rock to kill him, but Judah stood up and prevented them and said: "You have given me a covenant that you would not kill him." Judah used to bring him food. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/209.]

It is said: Allah the Exalted commanded a rock to rise from the bottom of the well, and Joseph stood upon it while he was naked. When Abraham the Friend (ﷺ) was cast into the fire, he was stripped of his garments and thrown into the fire naked, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) brought him a shirt of Paradisal silk and clothed him in it. That [shirt] was with Abraham; when he died it passed to Isaac, and when Isaac died it passed to Jacob. When Joseph grew up, Jacob put that shirt in an amulet and hung it on his neck, and he never parted from it. When he was cast into the well naked, Gabriel came, and that amulet was on him; he took the shirt out of it and clothed him with it. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Then they slaughtered a young goat and smeared its blood on Joseph's shirt.

﴿And they came to their father in the evening, weeping﴾: so that they would be bolder in the darkness to make their excuse and to pass off what they had plotted. It has been said: "Do not seek a need at night, for modesty is in the eyes," and one does not make an excuse for a sin in daytime, lest he stammer in the excuse and be unable to complete it. It was also said: they delayed their coming until the time of the late night prayer ('ishāʾ), in order to deceive their father.

Al-Suddi said: When he heard their voices he was alarmed and said: "What is the matter with you, my sons? Has something befallen your flock?" They said: "No." He said: "Then what has befallen you? And where is Joseph?" They said: ﴿O our father, we went off racing one another﴾: that is, we were shooting arrows at targets. Its evidence is the saying of ʿAbd Allah: "We were competing in archery." Al-Suddi and Ibn Hayyan said: we were running. ﴿And we left Joseph by our belongings, and the wolf devoured him; but you will not believe us, even though we are truthful﴾: because of your bad opinion of us and your accusing us. ﴿And they brought his shirt stained with false blood﴾: that is His saying ﴿with false blood﴾, meaning with false blood. It was also said: with blood that carried a lie, because it was not Joseph's blood but the blood of a sheep. This is like saying "the night is the crescent." It was also said: its meaning is with blood that was falsified in it, so the verbal noun was placed in the position of the noun, as one says: "He has no intellect nor is he intellectual."

ʿAʾishah read: ﴿bi-damin kadhib﴾ with an unpointed dāl, meaning fresh. Then Jacob wept at that, and said to his sons: "Show me his shirt," and they showed him. He said: "By Allah, I have never seen a wolf more gentle than this one: it devoured my son and did not tear his shirt!" Then he said: ﴿Rather, your souls have made a matter attractive to you; so patience is fitting.﴾ That is: "My patience" or "my duty is patience," and it was said: "My patience is beautiful patience." Al-Ashhab and al-ʿUqayli read ﴿fa-ṣabrun﴾ as the verbal noun, meaning: "I will surely be patient with a beautiful patience," which is the patience without complaint or grievance.

It was also said: its meaning is: I will not keep company with you in sorrowful face and imprisoned grief, but I will be in your company in a beautiful way, as I was before.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from al-Thawri, from Habib ibn Thabit, that the Prophet Jacob (peace be upon him) had his eyebrows fall over his eyes, and he would raise them with a cloth. It was asked of him: "What is this?" He said: "The length of time and the abundance of sorrows." Then Allah revealed to him: "O Jacob, do you complain to Me?" He said: "O Lord, it is a sin I committed, so forgive me for it."

﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾, namely the lie. They said: Joseph was eighteen years old when he was cast into the well. It was also said: seventeen years. It was also said: he was ten. He remained in it three days.

with us into the valley of the sandy hills of ʿaqanqal..."
[Gharib al-Hadith: 2/188.]

He meant "veered" (intaḥā).

﴿You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs, while they do not perceive﴾: that is, We revealed to Joseph, "Your dream will come true, and you will surely inform your brothers of their deed and of what they did to you, while they do not perceive the revelation of Allah to him or His informing him of that." He said: "This cup informs me that you had a brother from your father called Joseph, whom he favoured over you, and that you took him and cast him into the bottom of the well, then came to your father and said: 'The wolf has eaten him,' and sold him ﴿for a paltry price﴾. That is His saying: ﴿You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs, while they do not perceive.﴾"

Al-Suddi said: Jacob sent Joseph with them, and they took him out, and he had honour over them. When they went out into the wilderness they showed him enmity. His brother began to strike him, and he would call for help to the other, who would strike him too. He found no mercy from them, and they beat him until they nearly killed him. He began to cry out and say: "O father, O Jacob! If you knew what these sons are doing to your son!"

When they were nearly about to kill him, Judah said: "Did we not take from our father a covenant that you would not kill him?" So they took him to the well to cast him down. They began to lower him into the well, and he clung to its edge. They tied his hands and stripped off his shirt. He said: "O my brothers, return my shirt to me, that I may cover myself with it in the well." They said: "Call upon the sun, the moon, and the eleven stars, and they will keep you company." He said: "Indeed, I see nothing."

They lowered him into the well until he reached halfway down, then let him fall, intending that he would die. There was water in the well, and he fell into it, then he took refuge on a rock in it and stood upon it. When they cast him into the well, he began to weep, and they called to him. He thought it was mercy that had come to them, so he answered them. They wanted to crush him with a rock to kill him, but Judah stood up and prevented them and said: "You have given me a covenant that you would not kill him." Judah used to bring him food. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/209.]

It is said: Allah the Exalted commanded a rock to rise from the bottom of the well, and Joseph stood upon it while he was naked. When Abraham the Friend (ﷺ) was cast into the fire, he was stripped of his garments and thrown into the fire naked, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) brought him a shirt of Paradisal silk and clothed him in it. That [shirt] was with Abraham; when he died it passed to Isaac, and when Isaac died it passed to Jacob. When Joseph grew up, Jacob put that shirt in an amulet and hung it on his neck, and he never parted from it. When he was cast into the well naked, Gabriel came, and that amulet was on him; he took the shirt out of it and clothed him with it. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Then they slaughtered a young goat and smeared its blood on Joseph's shirt.

﴿And they came to their father in the evening, weeping﴾: so that they would be bolder in the darkness to make their excuse and to pass off what they had plotted. It has been said: "Do not seek a need at night, for modesty is in the eyes," and one does not make an excuse for a sin in daytime, lest he stammer in the excuse and be unable to complete it. It was also said: they delayed their coming until the time of the late night prayer ('ishāʾ), in order to deceive their father.

Al-Suddi said: When he heard their voices he was alarmed and said: "What is the matter with you, my sons? Has something befallen your flock?" They said: "No." He said: "Then what has befallen you? And where is Joseph?" They said: ﴿O our father, we went off racing one another﴾: that is, we were shooting arrows at targets. Its evidence is the saying of ʿAbd Allah: "We were competing in archery." Al-Suddi and Ibn Hayyan said: we were running. ﴿And we left Joseph by our belongings, and the wolf devoured him; but you will not believe us, even though we are truthful﴾: because of your bad opinion of us and your accusing us. ﴿And they brought his shirt stained with false blood﴾: that is His saying ﴿with false blood﴾, meaning with false blood. It was also said: with blood that carried a lie, because it was not Joseph's blood but the blood of a sheep. This is like saying "the night is the crescent." It was also said: its meaning is with blood that was falsified in it, so the verbal noun was placed in the position of the noun, as one says: "He has no intellect nor is he intellectual."

ʿAʾishah read: ﴿bi-damin kadhib﴾ with an unpointed dāl, meaning fresh. Then Jacob wept at that, and said to his sons: "Show me his shirt," and they showed him. He said: "By Allah, I have never seen a wolf more gentle than this one: it devoured my son and did not tear his shirt!" Then he said: ﴿Rather, your souls have made a matter attractive to you; so patience is fitting.﴾ That is: "My patience" or "my duty is patience," and it was said: "My patience is beautiful patience." Al-Ashhab and al-ʿUqayli read ﴿fa-ṣabrun﴾ as the verbal noun, meaning: "I will surely be patient with a beautiful patience," which is the patience without complaint or grievance.

It was also said: its meaning is: I will not keep company with you in sorrowful face and imprisoned grief, but I will be in your company in a beautiful way, as I was before.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from al-Thawri, from Habib ibn Thabit, that the Prophet Jacob (peace be upon him) had his eyebrows fall over his eyes, and he would raise them with a cloth. It was asked of him: "What is this?" He said: "The length of time and the abundance of sorrows." Then Allah revealed to him: "O Jacob, do you complain to Me?" He said: "O Lord, it is a sin I committed, so forgive me for it."

﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾, namely the lie. They said: Joseph was eighteen years old when he was cast into the well. It was also said: seventeen years. It was also said: he was ten. He remained in it three days.

And a caravan came; it was a company passing by from the direction of Madyan, heading for Egypt. They lost the way and set off walking off the track until they came to a place near the well. The well was in a desolate spot far from settlements; it was used only by shepherds and travellers passing through. Its water was brackish, but it became sweet when Yusuf was thrown into it. When they had camped there, they sent a man from the people of Madyan called Malik ibn Dhu'r to seek water for them. This is the meaning of ﴿they sent their water-drawer﴾. The *warid* (water-drawer) is the one who goes ahead of the caravan to the water and prepares the ropes and buckets. He reached the well and ﴿let down his bucket﴾, meaning he lowered it. It is said: "I let down the bucket into the water" when you lower it into it, and "I drew the bucket" when you bring it out of it. Yusuf (ʿalayhi al-salam) took hold of the rope, and when he came up, behold, there was a boy more beautiful than any boy.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yusuf was given half of beauty, and the other half was given to all other people."

[110] Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said: Yusuf had a handsome face and curly hair, large eyes, a well-proportioned frame, fair complexion, thick calves, forearms and upper arms, a slender belly, and a small navel. When he smiled, one saw light in his cheeks, and when he spoke, one saw a ray of light in his speech, flashing between his front teeth. No one could describe him. His beauty was like the light of day at night. He resembled Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) on the day God created him, shaped him, and breathed into him of His spirit, before he committed the sin. It is said that he inherited that beauty from his grandmother Sarah, who had been given a sixth of beauty.

When Malik ibn Dhu'r saw him he said: ﴿O good news! This is a boy.﴾ The readers differed over his words "O good news" (*yā bushrā*). The people of Kufa read it with a silent yāʾ, and said: Malik called out to a man among his companions whose name was Bushr, saying: "O Bushr," as one says "O Zayd." This is in the position of nominative as a direct address, and this is the view of al-Suddi.

The rest read *yā bushrāya*, with an alif and a fatha on the yāʾ, as a possessive construction, and they said: the water-drawer gave his companions the good news that he had found a slave.

﴿And they concealed him﴾, i.e., they hid him, ﴿as merchandise﴾, which is an accusative of circumstance. Malik ibn Dhu'r and his companions among the merchants who were with him said, and they told them: he is merchandise that we have been entrusted with by some people of the water to take to Egypt, for fear that they would ask them for a share in him if they knew his price. ʿAṭiyya reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: this refers to Yusuf's brothers, who concealed the matter of Yusuf, that he was their brother, and said: he is a slave of ours who ran away from us.

God the Exalted said: ﴿And God knows what they do.﴾ Yahuda brought food to Yusuf, but did not find him in the well. He informed his brothers of this, and they searched for him. Behold, they found Malik and his companions camped, so they came to them, and behold, they had Yusuf. They said: this is a slave who ran away from us. Wahb said: Yahuda had been standing at a distance, watching what would happen to Yusuf. When they drew him out, he saw him and informed the others. They came to Malik and said: this is our slave. Yusuf concealed his own matter, for fear that his brothers would kill him. Malik said: I will buy him from you. So they sold him to him. This is the meaning of God's words: ﴿and they sold him﴾, i.e., they sold him. Ibn Mufarrigh al-Ḥimyarī said:

*"I sold a cloak, would that I had..."
"...after the cloak I had been a lord of a company"*

That is, he sold a cloak, and it was his slave.

﴿For a paltry price﴾, i.e., deficient. It is a verbal noun placed in the position of a noun. Qatada said: it is injustice. al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: it is forbidden, because the price of a free person is unlawful. ʿIkrima and al-Shaʿbi said: little. Ibn Ḥayyan said: counterfeit. ﴿Dirhams﴾ is a substitute for the price. ﴿Counted﴾: mentioning a number is an expression of paucity; that is, they sold him for a few counted dirhams, not weighed, deficient and not full. Some people said: He said ﴿counted﴾ because in that time they did not weigh what weighed less than forty dirhams; they counted it by counting. When it reached an ounce they weighed it, because the smallest and least of their weights at that time was an ounce, and an ounce is forty dirhams.

The scholars differed over the amount of dirhams for which they sold him. Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Qatada and al-Suddi said: twenty dirhams, and they divided them, two dirhams each. Mujahid said: twenty-two dirhams. ʿIkrima said: forty dirhams.

﴿And they were of those who had no interest in him﴾, i.e., Yusuf's brothers were of those who had no interest in Yusuf; they did not know his honour with God nor his station with Him.

Then Malik ibn Dhu'r and his companions set off with Yusuf, and his brothers followed them, saying to them: take a firm hold of him so that he does not run away. They went until they brought him to Egypt, and Qiṭfīr bought him. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas. It is also said: Iṭfīr ibn Rawjīt, and he was the *ʿAzīz*, and he was in charge of the treasuries of Egypt.

The king of Egypt and its regions at that time was al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid ibn Thawrān ibn Irāma ibn Fāwun ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿImlāq ibn Lāwad ibn Sām ibn Nūḥ. It is also said that this king did not die until he believed and followed Yusuf in his religion, then he died, and Yusuf lived on after him. After him reigned Qābūs ibn Muṣʿab ibn Muʿāwiya ibn Numayr ibn al-Yiblawās ibn Fārān ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿImlāq ibn Lāwī ibn Sām ibn Nūḥ, and he was an unbeliever. Yusuf invited him to Islam, but he refused to accept it.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: When they entered Egypt, Qiṭfīr met Malik ibn Dhu'r, and bought Yusuf from him for twenty dinars, a pair of sandals, and two white garments. Ibn Munabbih said: The caravan brought Yusuf to Egypt and displayed him for sale; people competed for his price and bid against one another until his price reached his weight in musk and silver, and Qiṭfīr ibn Mālik bought him at this price. This is God's words: ﴿And the one who bought him from Egypt said﴾.

If it is said: How did he affirm buying in the words ﴿and they sold him﴾ and ﴿who bought him﴾, when no contract was concluded over him? The answer: buying means exchange. When he equalled him with money from his own possession, it was permissible to say "he bought him," by extension, as in God's words: ﴿Indeed God has bought from the believers their souls﴾, and the verse continues.

When Qiṭfīr came and brought him to his house, he said to his wife, whose name was Rāḥīl, daughter of Raʿābīl; this was said by Muḥammad ibn Isḥaq ibn Yasar.

al-Thaʿlabi said: Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Munabbih narrated to us, saying: Abu Ḥāmid al-Mustamli narrated to us, Abu Hisham al-Rifaʿi narrated to us, saying: the name of the wife of the *ʿAzīz* who embraced Yusuf was Zulaykhā, daughter of Mūsā.

﴿Honour his lodging﴾, i.e., his dwelling and his stay. Qatada and Ibn Jurayj said: his station. ﴿Perhaps he will benefit us﴾, meaning he will suffice us when he reaches maturity, understands matters, and handles some of the affairs we face.

﴿Or we may take him as a son﴾, i.e., adopt him. Ibn Isḥaq said: Qiṭfīr did not approach women, and his wife Rāḥīl (in al-Ṭabari, Rāʿīl, and it is Iṭfīr) was beautiful, pampered, and well-provided, living in wealth and worldly comfort.

al-Thaʿlabi said: Abu Bakr al-Jawqi informed us, Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Daghuli informed us, ʿAli ibn al-Ḥasan al-Hilali narrated to us, Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abu Isḥaq, from Abu ʿUbayd, from ʿAbdullah, who said:

The most perceptive of people are three: the *ʿAzīz* when he discerned in Yusuf and said: ﴿Honour his lodging﴾; the woman who came to Musa and said to her father: ﴿O father, hire him﴾; and Abu Bakr when he appointed ʿUmar as successor.

﴿And thus﴾, i.e., just as We rescued Yusuf from the hands of his brothers, who had resolved to kill him, and brought him out of the well after he had been thrown into it, so We brought him to honour and an exalted station with the *ʿAzīz* of Egypt. ﴿We established Yusuf in the land﴾, meaning the land of Egypt; We made him in charge of its treasuries. The People of the Book said: When Yusuf (ʿalayhi al-salam) had completed thirty years, Pharaoh made him his minister.

﴿And that We may teach him the interpretation of events﴾, i.e., so that We may teach him the interpretation of dreams. ﴿And God is dominant over His affair﴾: they differed over this pronoun. Some said: it refers back to God, the Mighty and Majestic, and the sense of the sentence is: nothing overpowers God, rather He is dominant over His affair, doing what He wills and knowing what He intends. Others said: it refers to Yusuf, and the meaning of the verse is: God is in charge of Yusuf's affair, governing him, protecting him, arranging his affair, and not leaving it to anyone else.

﴿But most people do not know﴾ what God is doing with Yusuf, and that to Him Yusuf's affair will return. They are those who had no interest in him and sold him for a paltry price and did to him what they did. [Tafsir al-Ṭabari, with variations: 12/230.]

The wise said regarding this: ﴿God is dominant over His affair.﴾ When Yaʿqub commanded Yusuf (ʿalayhima al-salam) not to recount his dream to his brothers, God's command prevailed, and he recounted it. Then Yaʿqub wanted them not to plot against him, and God's command prevailed until they plotted. Then Yusuf's brothers wanted to kill him, and God's command prevailed so that they did not kill him. Then they wanted to throw him into the well so that some caravan would pick him up and his name would be erased, but God's command prevailed so that his name was not erased and he became mentioned and famous. Then they sold him so that he would be a slave, and God's command prevailed until he became a king with slaves before him. Then they wanted to clear their father's attention for themselves, and God's command prevailed until their father's heart was constricted for them. Then they resolved that after him they would be righteous, repentant people, and God's command prevailed until they forgot the sin, and persisted, until they confessed before Yusuf at the end, after forty years, and said: ﴿And indeed we were sinners﴾, and they said to their father: ﴿Indeed we were sinners.﴾

Then they wanted to deceive him with the shirt's name, the blood and the weeping, and God's command prevailed so that he was not deceived; he said: ﴿Rather, your souls have enticed you to something﴾. Then they plotted to remove his love from his father's heart, and God's command prevailed until love and longing increased in his heart. Then Yusuf resolved to free himself from prison by mentioning the cupbearer, and God's command prevailed so that the cupbearer forgot to mention him, and he remained in prison for several years. Then the wife of the *ʿAzīz* plotted to cease her solicitation of him, until she said: ﴿What is the recompense for one who intended harm to your family?﴾ and the verse continues. God's command prevailed until a witness from her own family testified.

﴿And when he reached his full strength﴾, i.e., the end of his youth and the height of his power. Mujahid said: thirty-three years. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: twenty years. Ibn ʿAbbas reported that it is between eighteen and thirty years; it was also said: up to forty; it was also said: up to sixty. The word *ashudd* (full strength) is the plural of *shadd*, like *qadd* and *aqudd*, *sharr* and *ashirr*, *ḍarr* and *aḍirr*. Ḥumayd said:

*"The blamers may tire, for he has come of age, four complete [years] after the ashall..."*

The poet said:

*"Is it not that the ashall has multiplied, and the war of kings has destroyed the vast wealth?"*

﴿We gave him judgment and knowledge﴾. Mujahid said: intellect, understanding, and knowledge before prophethood. The people of meanings said: that is, correctness in speech, and knowledge of the interpretation of dreams, and of the sources and destinations of affairs.

﴿And thus We reward the good-doers﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: the believers; and from him also: the guided. al-[Ṣadūq] reported from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: that is, those who are patient in calamities as Yusuf was patient. Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said:

Although the outward sense of this is general to every good-doer, the intended meaning is Muhammad, the Prophet of God ﷺ. It says: As I did to Yusuf after what he met from his brothers and endured the trials he endured, I established him in the land, I settled him in the country, and gave him judgment and knowledge; so I will do with you. I will deliver you from the polytheists of your people who aim at you with enmity, I will establish you in the land, and increase you in judgment and knowledge, because that is My recompense for the good-doers in My command and My prohibition.

﴿Honour his lodging﴾, i.e., his dwelling and his stay. Qatada and Ibn Jurayj said: his station. ﴿Perhaps he will benefit us﴾, meaning he will suffice us when he reaches maturity, understands matters, and handles some of the affairs we face.

﴿Or we may take him as a son﴾, i.e., adopt him. Ibn Isḥaq said: Qiṭfīr did not approach women, and his wife Rāḥīl (in al-Ṭabari, Rāʿīl, and it is Iṭfīr) was beautiful, pampered, and well-provided, living in wealth and worldly comfort.

al-Thaʿlabi said: Abu Bakr al-Jawqi informed us, Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Daghuli informed us, ʿAli ibn al-Ḥasan al-Hilali narrated to us, Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abu Isḥaq, from Abu ʿUbayd, from ʿAbdullah, who said:

The most perceptive of people are three: the *ʿAzīz* when he discerned in Yusuf and said: ﴿Honour his lodging﴾; the woman who came to Musa and said to her father: ﴿O father, hire him﴾; and Abu Bakr when he appointed ʿUmar as successor.

﴿And thus﴾, i.e., just as We rescued Yusuf from the hands of his brothers, who had resolved to kill him, and brought him out of the well after he had been thrown into it, so We brought him to honour and an exalted station with the *ʿAzīz* of Egypt. ﴿We established Yusuf in the land﴾, meaning the land of Egypt; We made him in charge of its treasuries. The People of the Book said: When Yusuf (ʿalayhi al-salam) had completed thirty years, Pharaoh made him his minister.

﴿And that We may teach him the interpretation of events﴾, i.e., so that We may teach him the interpretation of dreams. ﴿And God is dominant over His affair﴾: they differed over this pronoun. Some said: it refers back to God, the Mighty and Majestic, and the sense of the sentence is: nothing overpowers God, rather He is dominant over His affair, doing what He wills and knowing what He intends. Others said: it refers to Yusuf, and the meaning of the verse is: God is in charge of Yusuf's affair, governing him, protecting him, arranging his affair, and not leaving it to anyone else.

﴿But most people do not know﴾ what God is doing with Yusuf, and that to Him Yusuf's affair will return. They are those who had no interest in him and sold him for a paltry price and did to him what they did. [Tafsir al-Ṭabari, with variations: 12/230.]

The wise said regarding this: ﴿God is dominant over His affair.﴾ When Yaʿqub commanded Yusuf (ʿalayhima al-salam) not to recount his dream to his brothers, God's command prevailed, and he recounted it. Then Yaʿqub wanted them not to plot against him, and God's command prevailed until they plotted. Then Yusuf's brothers wanted to kill him, and God's command prevailed so that they did not kill him. Then they wanted to throw him into the well so that some caravan would pick him up and his name would be erased, but God's command prevailed so that his name was not erased and he became mentioned and famous. Then they sold him so that he would be a slave, and God's command prevailed until he became a king with slaves before him. Then they wanted to clear their father's attention for themselves, and God's command prevailed until their father's heart was constricted for them. Then they resolved that after him they would be righteous, repentant people, and God's command prevailed until they forgot the sin, and persisted, until they confessed before Yusuf at the end, after forty years, and said: ﴿And indeed we were sinners﴾, and they said to their father: ﴿Indeed we were sinners.﴾

Then they wanted to deceive him with the shirt's name, the blood and the weeping, and God's command prevailed so that he was not deceived; he said: ﴿Rather, your souls have enticed you to something﴾. Then they plotted to remove his love from his father's heart, and God's command prevailed until love and longing increased in his heart. Then Yusuf resolved to free himself from prison by mentioning the cupbearer, and God's command prevailed so that the cupbearer forgot to mention him, and he remained in prison for several years. Then the wife of the *ʿAzīz* plotted to cease her solicitation of him, until she said: ﴿What is the recompense for one who intended harm to your family?﴾ and the verse continues. God's command prevailed until a witness from her own family testified.

﴿And when he reached his full strength﴾, i.e., the end of his youth and the height of his power. Mujahid said: thirty-three years. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: twenty years. Ibn ʿAbbas reported that it is between eighteen and thirty years; it was also said: up to forty; it was also said: up to sixty. The word *ashudd* (full strength) is the plural of *shadd*, like *qadd* and *aqudd*, *sharr* and *ashirr*, *ḍarr* and *aḍirr*. Ḥumayd said:

*"The blamers may tire, for he has come of age, four complete [years] after the ashall..."*

The poet said:

*"Is it not that the ashall has multiplied, and the war of kings has destroyed the vast wealth?"*

﴿We gave him judgment and knowledge﴾. Mujahid said: intellect, understanding, and knowledge before prophethood. The people of meanings said: that is, correctness in speech, and knowledge of the interpretation of dreams, and of the sources and destinations of affairs.

﴿And thus We reward the good-doers﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: the believers; and from him also: the guided. al-[Ṣadūq] reported from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: that is, those who are patient in calamities as Yusuf was patient. Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said:

Although the outward sense of this is general to every good-doer, the intended meaning is Muhammad, the Prophet of God ﷺ. It says: As I did to Yusuf after what he met from his brothers and endured the trials he endured, I established him in the land, I settled him in the country, and gave him judgment and knowledge; so I will do with you. I will deliver you from the polytheists of your people who aim at you with enmity, I will establish you in the land, and increase you in judgment and knowledge, because that is My recompense for the good-doers in My command and My prohibition.

And she in whose house he was, meaning the wife of the Chief (al-'Aziz), sought to seduce him, and she asked him to have intercourse with her. ﴿And she locked the doors﴾, and they were seven.

﴿And she said: "Come, you."﴾ The readers differed concerning it. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Sulami, Abu Wa'il and Qatadah read *hi'ta lak* (هئت لك) with a kasra on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*, with a hamza, meaning "I have prepared myself for you." Abu 'Amr rejected this reading. Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna said: I heard Abu 'Amr being asked about the reading of one who reads *hi'ta lak* with a kasra on the *ha'* and a hamza on the *ya'*, and Abu 'Amr said: "It is false. He has taken it from *tahayya'tu* (I prepared myself). Go and survey the Arabs until you reach Yemen; do you know anyone who says this?" Al-Kisa'i also said: "*Hi'ta* has not been transmitted from the Arabs." 'Ikrimah said: *hi'ta lak* means "she adorned herself for you and beautified herself," and this reading is not approved.

Nasr ibn 'Asim, Yahya ibn Ya'mar and Abdullah ibn Abi Ishaq read *hayta lak* (هيت لك) with a fatha on the *ha'* and a kasra on the *ta'*. Yahya ibn Wathhab read *hayt* (هِيتُ) with a kasra on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*. Ibn Kathir read it with a fatha on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*. Tarafah recited:

"My people are not the most distant when one calls from the clan, *hayt*,
They respond swiftly, like flocks of birds, leaving no house behind."

The people of Medina and Syria read it with a kasra on the *ha'* and a fatha on the *ta'*, and the rest read it with a fatha on both the *ha'* and the *ta'*. This is the dialect of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the well-known usage among the Arabs.

Al-Sha'bi reported from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "The Prophet (ﷺ) recited to me *hayta lak*."

Al-A'mash reported from Abu Wa'il from Ibn Mas'ud that he recited *hi'ta lak*, and it was said to him, "*Hayta lak*," and Ibn Mas'ud said: "We only recite it as we were taught it and as we heard it, all together: *hallumma*, come, and approach." A poet, addressing the Commander of the Faithful Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), said:

"Convey to the Commander of the Faithful, the people of Iraq, when you arrive,
That Iraq and its people are yours, so *hayta*, *hayta*."

Al-Suddi said: "In Coptic it means *halumma lak*" (come to you). Al-Husayn said: "*Hayta lak* is a word in Syriac meaning 'upon you'." Abu 'Ubayd said: "Al-Kisa'i used to say it is the dialect of the people of Hawran that reached the Hijaz, and its meaning is 'come'." Abu 'Ubayd said: "I asked a learned elder from Hawran, and he mentioned that it is their dialect." 'Ikrimah said likewise.

Mujahid and others said: "It is an Arabic dialect by which she invited him to herself. It is a word of urging and of turning toward something." The root of both is the calling and shouting. The Arabs say, "*Hayyata* so-and-so with so-and-so," when he called him and shouted at him. A poet said:

"The silence of the camel-driver has troubled me;
Had he been addressed by it, he would have shouted *hayyata*."

That is, he shouted at him. *Al-Kari* means the camel-driver.

Our teacher Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: "I saw in some exegeses, *hayta lak*, which says: 'Do you have a desire for my beauty and my comeliness?'" Abu 'Ubaydah mentioned that the Arabs do not form the dual of *hayta*, nor its plural, nor its feminine; it is in one form in every case, and it is distinguished only by what follows it and what precedes it.

Yusuf (peace be upon him) said at that: ﴿"Allah forbid! I seek refuge and protection in Allah from what you invite me to."﴾ *Ma'adha Allah* is a verbal noun, its estimated form being *'iyadhan billah* (seeking refuge in Allah).

﴿"Indeed, he is my lord; he has made my dwelling good."﴾ That is, your husband Qatafir, my master. This is the view of most exegetes. Some said: it refers back to Allah, ﴿"he has made my dwelling good"﴾, meaning He sheltered me and saved me from the trial of love.

﴿"Indeed, the wrongdoers will not prosper."﴾ That is, if I did it, after he honored me and entrusted me, I would have betrayed him regarding his family, and "he has made my dwelling good," so I would be a wrongdoer, and ﴿the wrongdoers will not prosper﴾. It was also said: the adulterers.

﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her.﴾ The meaning of desire (*hamm*) for a thing is that a person speaks to himself about it without doing it. A poet said:

"I desired, and did not act; I nearly did, and would that I had not,
Leaving the wives of 'Uthman weeping over him."

As for the desire that Yusuf (peace be upon him) had for the woman, and her desire for him, the scholars differed concerning it. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah reported from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: "I heard Ibn 'Abbas asked: 'How far did the desire of Yusuf go?' He said: 'He untied the drawstring and sat between her legs like a man sits with his wife.'"

Ibn Jurayj reported from Ibn Abi 'Atiyyah, who said: "I asked Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) how far the desire of Yusuf went. He said: 'She lay on her back, and he sat between her legs to take off his clothes.'"

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "He loosened the cord of his trousers." Mujahid said: "He untied the trousers until they reached the ankles, and he sat with her as a man sits with his wife."

Al-Dahhak said: "Satan ran between them; he struck with his hand at Yusuf's collar and with the other hand at the woman's collar until he joined them together."

Al-Suddi and Ibn Ishaq said: "When the wife of the Chief wanted to seduce Yusuf, she began to mention to him the excellence of his person and to express her longing for herself. She said to him: 'O Yusuf, how beautiful is your hair!' He said: 'It is the first thing to fall from my body.' She said: 'O Yusuf, how beautiful is your eye!' He said: 'It is the first thing to flow to the earth from my body.' She said: 'How beautiful is your face!' He said: 'It is for the dust to eat.' She kept obeying him once and frightening him another time, and inviting him to pleasure, while he was a young man in the full vigor of youth, with such desire as a man has, and she was a beautiful, lovely woman, until he softened toward her because of what he saw of her passion for him, and he was no longer wary of her, until they were left alone in some room, and he desired her." These are the sayings of the exegetes from the righteous predecessors.

A group of later scholars said: "This does not befit the prophets," so they interpreted the verse in various ways. Some said: "He desired to flee from her." This is not correct, because the fleeing is mentioned, and there is no mention of it in the verse. It was said: "He desired to strike her and push her away." It was said: "He desired to dispute with her and bring her case before her husband." It was said: "*Wa-hamma bihā* is a reference to something not mentioned." It was said: "The statement is complete at His saying: ﴿And she certainly desired him﴾, then the report about Yusuf begins: ﴿and he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾." This is with inversion (*taqdim wa ta'khir*), its estimate being: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have desired her, but he saw the proof and did not desire her," like His saying: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan﴾. This is corrupt according to the linguists, because the Arabs do not place the answer of *law-la* (had it not been) before it. One does not say: "I stood up had it not been for Zayd," meaning: "Had it not been for Zayd, I would have stood up."

Juwaybir reported from al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "She desired Yusuf that he should lie with her, and ﴿and he would have desired her﴾ means he wished her to be his wife."

These interpretations that we have related are all weak and not acceptable, because they contradict the sayings of the earlier scholars from whom interpretation is taken, and they took it from those who witnessed the revelation.

It has been reported in a sound report that when Yusuf entered upon the king and the woman confessed, Yusuf said: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence.﴾ Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: "Nor when you desired her, O Yusuf?" Yusuf then said: ﴿"And I do not acquit myself; indeed, the soul is most commanding of evil, except what my Lord has mercy upon."﴾

As for the people of realities (*ahl al-haqa'iq*), they said regarding this verse: "Desire is of two kinds: a settled desire (*hamm muqim*, lasting), which is when it is accompanied by determination, resolve, intention and consent, like the desire of the wife of the Chief, and in that case the covenant is taken. And a passing desire (*hamm 'arid*), which is a passing thought, a fancy and a self-talk without choice or determination, like the desire of Yusuf (peace be upon him), and the covenant is not taken as long as one does not speak it or do it." This is shown by what was reported from Ibn al-Mubarak, who said: "I said to Sufyan: 'Is one held accountable for a mere desire?' He said: 'If it is a determination, one is held accountable for it.'"

It was reported from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'When My servant desires a good deed and does not do it, I write it for him as a good deed; and if he does it, I write it for him as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times. And when My servant desires an evil deed and does not do it, I do not write it against him; if he does it, I write it against him as one evil deed; and if he leaves it for My sake, I write it for him as a good deed.'"

The affirmation of such slips and minor sins in the case of the prophets (peace be upon them) is not forbidden, for a kind of wisdom:
First: that they may be in awe of Allah, Exalted, when they recall them, so they strive in His obedience out of fear, and do not rely on the vastness of Allah's mercy.
Second: to make them know the position of His blessing and His favor upon them in turning it away from them.
Third: to make them leaders for the sinners in hope of Allah's mercy and in not despairing of His pardon and bounty.

'Ikrimah reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one meets Allah, Mighty and Majestic, without having desired a sin or committed it, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya, for he did not desire it and did not commit it."

It was reported from Mus'ab ibn Abd Allah, who said: Mus'ab ibn 'Uthman told me: "Sulayman ibn Yasar was among the most handsome of people. A woman came in to him seeking a fatwa, and she tempted him with herself, but he refused her and admonished her. She said to him: 'If you do not do it, I will certainly spread word against you and I will cry out against you.' He went out and left her, and he saw in his dream Yusuf the Prophet (peace be upon him), who said to him: 'Are you Yusuf?' He said: 'I am Yusuf the Prophet. I desired, and you are Sulayman, who did not desire.'"

As for the proof that Yusuf (peace be upon him) saw, the scholars differed concerning it. Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Husayn ibn 'Atiyyah, from Isra'il, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: "A likeness of Ya'qub appeared to him and struck his chest with his hand, and his desire came out through his fingertips."

Al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Ibn Sirin, Abu Salih, Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah and al-Dahhak said: "The ceiling of the room opened for him, and he saw Ya'qub biting his finger."

Ibn Jubayr said: "Every son of Ya'qub had twelve sons, except Yusuf, who had eleven sons, because some of his desire was reduced when he saw the image of his father, and so he felt shame."

Qatadah said: "He saw the image of Ya'qub, and said: 'O Yusuf, will you do the deed of fools while you are written among the prophets?'"

Ibn Abi Mulaykah reported from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "It was called out: 'O Yusuf, will you commit adultery, and be like a bird whose feathers have fallen, and it tries to fly but has no feathers?'"

Al-Suddi said: "It was called out: 'O Yusuf, will you lie with her? Your likeness, so long as you do not lie with her, is like a bird in the air of the sky that is not released; and your likeness if you lie with her is like a [bird] that dies and falls to the earth, unable to ward off itself. And your likeness, so long as you do not lie with her, is like the difficult bull on which no work is done; and your likeness if you lie with her is like the bull when it dies, and ants enter the base of its horns, and it cannot ward them off from itself.'"

Abu Mardud reported from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: "Yusuf raised his head to the ceiling of the room when he desired, and he saw a writing on the wall of the room: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way.﴾"

Abu Ma'shar reported from him: "Had he not seen what was in the Qur'an of the magnification and prohibition of adultery." Al-Qurazi added: "in the Qur'an and the scrolls of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)."

Layth reported from Mujahid from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: "He untied his trousers and sat between her thighs as a man sits with his wife, and behold, a palm was extended between them, with no arm and no wrist, on which was written: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do.﴾"

He said: "So he stood up fleeing, and she stood up. When the terror left them, she returned and he returned. When he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, behold, a palm was extended between them, with no arm and no wrist, on which was written: ﴿And fear a day when you will be returned to Allah, then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ So he stood up fleeing, and she stood up. When the terror left them, she returned and he returned. When he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, Allah, exalted is He, said to Jibril (peace be upon him): 'O Jibril, overtake My servant before he commits the sin.' Jibril saw him biting his finger or his palm, and he was saying: 'O Yusuf, will you do the deed of fools while you are written with Allah among the prophets?'"

That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil and immorality.﴾

Qatadah reported from 'Atiyyah from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: "When Yusuf and the wife of the Chief were about to do what they were about to do, a palm without a body came out between them, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿Is then He who is standing over every soul for what it has earned [like those who associate others with Him]?﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned between them, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do.﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned, and on it was written in Hebrew: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way.﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned a fourth time, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿And fear a day when you will be returned to Allah.﴾ Then Yusuf fled."

'Atiyyah reported from Ibn 'Abbas that the proof which Yusuf saw was that the image of the king was shown to him. Umar ibn Ishaq reported from some people of knowledge that it was Qatafir, his master, who arrived at the door at that moment; when he fled from her, she pursued him and found him at the door.

Ali ibn Musa al-Rida reported from his father, from Ja'far al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "My father told me, from his father, Ali ibn al-Husayn, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: The wife of the Chief went to the idol and covered it with a cloth. Yusuf said to her: 'What is this?' She said: 'I am ashamed before the idol that it should see us.' Yusuf said:

'Are you ashamed before one who does not hear, nor see, nor understand, nor witness, and I should not be ashamed before the One who created things and taught them?'"

Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: "The proof is the prophethood which Allah deposited in his breast, and it was what prevented him from what displeases Allah."

It was said: "It is what Allah gave him of knowledge and wisdom." The people of allusion (*ahl al-isharah*) said: "The believer has a proof from his Lord in his secret, from his knowledge, and he saw that proof, and it was his restrainer."

So the "proof" is the sign and the argument. The answer of *law-la* (had it not been) is omitted, its estimate being: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have committed adultery." He reconciled the natural desire with the desire of acquisition, according to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Accepting of repentance and Wise, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾. Its meaning: "You would have been destroyed." Imru' al-Qays said:

"If only she were a soul that dies in peace,
But she is a soul that wastes our souls."

He meant: "*Saqatat*" (she fell) — "fanīt" (perished), and "lahhan 'alayya" (anguished over me), and similar.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil﴾, the sin, ﴿and immorality﴾, adultery.

﴿Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.﴾ The people of Mecca and Basra read it with a kasra on the *lam* (*al-mukhlisin*), meaning those who made their devotion and worship sincere to Allah. The others read it with a fatha on the *lam* (*al-mukhlasin*), meaning those chosen for prophethood, and the evidence for it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We made them sincere with a pure sincerity﴾.

Al-Zuhri reported from Hamzah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Imran ibn Umar, who said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) became ill with the pain of which he died, he (ﷺ) said: 'Let Abu Bakr lead the people in prayer.' 'A'ishah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr is a tender man, and he cannot control himself when he recites the Qur'an, so command Umar to lead the people in prayer.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Let Abu Bakr lead the people in prayer.' I repeated it to him, and he said: 'Let Abu Bakr lead the people in prayer, for you are like the companions of Yusuf.'" 'A'ishah said: "By Allah, what moved me in that matter against them was only that he would be the first man to stand in the place of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba narrated to us: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Ja'far al-Mustamli narrated to us: some of our companions narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman said: "I heard a woman in some of the roads speaking with some lewdness, so I said to her: [....] [[Unreadable word.]] You are indeed the female companions of Yusuf." The woman said to him: "Alas! We invited him to pleasure, while you wanted to kill him. So whose companions are we or you? And is taking a life greater than what we wanted?"

﴿And they both raced to the door﴾. This is because when Yusuf saw the proof, he rose hastily toward the door of the house, fleeing from what she wanted from him, and the woman followed him. This is the meaning of the verse.

﴿And they both raced to the door﴾: Yusuf and Raahil (Zulaykha) hurried to the door. As for Yusuf, he fled from committing the immorality. As for the woman, she sought to reach Yusuf so that she might fulfill her desire, i.e., he had been solicited by her. She caught up with him and seized his shirt from behind and pulled him back toward her, preventing him from leaving.

﴿And tore his shirt﴾: she ripped and split his shirt. ﴿From behind﴾: from the back, not from the front, because Yusuf was the one fleeing and the woman was the one pursuing. When they both came out and ﴿found her master at the door﴾, meaning they found her husband Qitfir sitting at the door with a cousin of Raahil. When she saw him, she was overcome with fear, so she spoke first to her husband, saying: ﴿What is the recompense for one who intended evil for your family, except that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?﴾ She meant adultery; "imprisoned" means detained, and "a painful punishment" means being beaten with whips. This was reported by Ibn Abbas.

﴿Yusuf said: "It was she who sought to seduce me"﴾, and ﴿a witness from her family testified﴾. The scholars differed about this witness. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Hilal ibn Yasar and al-Dahhak said he was an infant in the cradle whom God made to speak by His power.

Al-Awfi narrated to us from Ibn Abbas, and Shahr ibn Hawshab from Abu Hurayra. What supports this is what Ata ibn al-Sa'ib narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Four spoke while they were infants: the son of the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter, the witness of Yusuf, the companion of Jurayj, and Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him)."

It was said that this infant was the son of the woman's maternal uncle. Al-Hasan said he was her servant boy. Qatada, al-Dahhak and Mujahid, through a narration [ ... ] [[Unreadable word.]], said: "He was not a child, but a wise man with a beard, possessing opinion, speech and a sign." This is the narration of Ibn Abi Mulayka from Ibn Abbas, who said: "He was among the close circle of the king." Al-Suddi said: "He was the cousin of Raahil, and he was sitting with her husband at the door, so he judged, and God the Exalted reported about him: ﴿If his shirt is torn from the front...﴾" (the verse).

Isa narrated from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "The witness is the shirt torn from behind." The meaning of ﴿a witness testified﴾ is that a judge decided. ﴿From her family﴾. Mujahid said: "The witness said: the explanation of this matter lies in the shirt."

﴿If his shirt is torn from behind, then she has lied and he is of the truthful. But if his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars.﴾ Ibn Abi Ishaq read "al-qubul" and "al-dubur" with a light pronunciation, while the others read them with emphasis; both are two dialects.

So the shirt was brought, and behold, it was torn from behind. When Qitfir saw his shirt torn from behind, he recognized his wife's betrayal and Yusuf's innocence. So he said to her: ﴿Indeed, this is of your guile; indeed, your guile is great.﴾ It was also said that this is the speech of the witness.

Then Qitfir turned to Yusuf and said: ﴿Yusuf﴾, meaning "O Yusuf", a singular vocative, ﴿turn away from this matter﴾, so do not mention it to anyone. It was also said that the meaning is: do not be concerned with it, for your innocence was clear. Then he said to his wife: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. It was also said that this is from the witness to Yusuf and to Raahil, and by his saying ﴿and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ he meant: ask your husband not to punish you for your sin, and to pardon you. This is the meaning reported from Ibn Abbas.

﴿Indeed, you were of those who committed sin﴾: that is, among the sinners, when you sought to seduce a young man against himself and betrayed your husband. When he refrained, you lied about him. It is said: "khati'a yakhta'u khata'an and khata'an and khatha'an and khata'an," meaning he sinned, and the noun derived from it is "khati'ah" (sin). God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, killing them was a great sin﴾ [Q 17:31]. Umayya said:

"Your servants err, and You are the Lord; in Your two palms are the deaths and the decrees."

That is, they sin. When one intends deliberate action, one says "khati'a" with the vowel of the verb being "a"? Here [the verb] is with alif, as God the Exalted said: ﴿And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by error﴾ [Q 4:92].

As for why He said ﴿of those who committed sin﴾ and did not say "of the sinful women", it is because He did not intend to speak about women, but about the one who does such a thing. Its implied sense is "of the sinful people". Similar to it is His saying: ﴿and she was of the obedient ones﴾ [Q 66:12]. Its explanation is His saying: ﴿indeed she was of a disbelieving people﴾ [Q 27:43].

And she in whose house he was, meaning the wife of the Chief (al-'Aziz), sought to seduce him, and she asked him to have intercourse with her. ﴿And she locked the doors﴾, and they were seven.

﴿And she said: "Come, you."﴾ The readers differed concerning it. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Sulami, Abu Wa'il and Qatadah read *hi'ta lak* (هئت لك) with a kasra on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*, with a hamza, meaning "I have prepared myself for you." Abu 'Amr rejected this reading. Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna said: I heard Abu 'Amr being asked about the reading of one who reads *hi'ta lak* with a kasra on the *ha'* and a hamza on the *ya'*, and Abu 'Amr said: "It is false. He has taken it from *tahayya'tu* (I prepared myself). Go and survey the Arabs until you reach Yemen; do you know anyone who says this?" Al-Kisa'i also said: "*Hi'ta* has not been transmitted from the Arabs." 'Ikrimah said: *hi'ta lak* means "she adorned herself for you and beautified herself," and this reading is not approved.

Nasr ibn 'Asim, Yahya ibn Ya'mar and Abdullah ibn Abi Ishaq read *hayta lak* (هيت لك) with a fatha on the *ha'* and a kasra on the *ta'*. Yahya ibn Wathhab read *hayt* (هِيتُ) with a kasra on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*. Ibn Kathir read it with a fatha on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*. Tarafah recited:

"My people are not the most distant when one calls from the clan, *hayt*,
They respond swiftly, like flocks of birds, leaving no house behind."

The people of Medina and Syria read it with a kasra on the *ha'* and a fatha on the *ta'*, and the rest read it with a fatha on both the *ha'* and the *ta'*. This is the dialect of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the well-known usage among the Arabs.

Al-Sha'bi reported from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "The Prophet (ﷺ) recited to me *hayta lak*."

Al-A'mash reported from Abu Wa'il from Ibn Mas'ud that he recited *hi'ta lak*, and it was said to him, "*Hayta lak*," and Ibn Mas'ud said: "We only recite it as we were taught it and as we heard it, all together: *hallumma*, come, and approach." A poet, addressing the Commander of the Faithful Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), said:

"Convey to the Commander of the Faithful, the people of Iraq, when you arrive,
That Iraq and its people are yours, so *hayta*, *hayta*."

Al-Suddi said: "In Coptic it means *halumma lak*" (come to you). Al-Husayn said: "*Hayta lak* is a word in Syriac meaning 'upon you'." Abu 'Ubayd said: "Al-Kisa'i used to say it is the dialect of the people of Hawran that reached the Hijaz, and its meaning is 'come'." Abu 'Ubayd said: "I asked a learned elder from Hawran, and he mentioned that it is their dialect." 'Ikrimah said likewise.

Mujahid and others said: "It is an Arabic dialect by which she invited him to herself. It is a word of urging and of turning toward something." The root of both is the calling and shouting. The Arabs say, "*Hayyata* so-and-so with so-and-so," when he called him and shouted at him. A poet said:

"The silence of the camel-driver has troubled me;
Had he been addressed by it, he would have shouted *hayyata*."

That is, he shouted at him. *Al-Kari* means the camel-driver.

Our teacher Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: "I saw in some exegeses, *hayta lak*, which says: 'Do you have a desire for my beauty and my comeliness?'" Abu 'Ubaydah mentioned that the Arabs do not form the dual of *hayta*, nor its plural, nor its feminine; it is in one form in every case, and it is distinguished only by what follows it and what precedes it.

Yusuf (peace be upon him) said at that: ﴿"Allah forbid! I seek refuge and protection in Allah from what you invite me to."﴾ *Ma'adha Allah* is a verbal noun, its estimated form being *'iyadhan billah* (seeking refuge in Allah).

﴿"Indeed, he is my lord; he has made my dwelling good."﴾ That is, your husband Qatafir, my master. This is the view of most exegetes. Some said: it refers back to Allah, ﴿"he has made my dwelling good"﴾, meaning He sheltered me and saved me from the trial of love.

﴿"Indeed, the wrongdoers will not prosper."﴾ That is, if I did it, after he honored me and entrusted me, I would have betrayed him regarding his family, and "he has made my dwelling good," so I would be a wrongdoer, and ﴿the wrongdoers will not prosper﴾. It was also said: the adulterers.

﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her.﴾ The meaning of desire (*hamm*) for a thing is that a person speaks to himself about it without doing it. A poet said:

"I desired, and did not act; I nearly did, and would that I had not,
Leaving the wives of 'Uthman weeping over him."

As for the desire that Yusuf (peace be upon him) had for the woman, and her desire for him, the scholars differed concerning it. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah reported from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: "I heard Ibn 'Abbas asked: 'How far did the desire of Yusuf go?' He said: 'He untied the drawstring and sat between her legs like a man sits with his wife.'"

Ibn Jurayj reported from Ibn Abi 'Atiyyah, who said: "I asked Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) how far the desire of Yusuf went. He said: 'She lay on her back, and he sat between her legs to take off his clothes.'"

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "He loosened the cord of his trousers." Mujahid said: "He untied the trousers until they reached the ankles, and he sat with her as a man sits with his wife."

Al-Dahhak said: "Satan ran between them; he struck with his hand at Yusuf's collar and with the other hand at the woman's collar until he joined them together."

Al-Suddi and Ibn Ishaq said: "When the wife of the Chief wanted to seduce Yusuf, she began to mention to him the excellence of his person and to express her longing for herself. She said to him: 'O Yusuf, how beautiful is your hair!' He said: 'It is the first thing to fall from my body.' She said: 'O Yusuf, how beautiful is your eye!' He said: 'It is the first thing to flow to the earth from my body.' She said: 'How beautiful is your face!' He said: 'It is for the dust to eat.' She kept obeying him once and frightening him another time, and inviting him to pleasure, while he was a young man in the full vigor of youth, with such desire as a man has, and she was a beautiful, lovely woman, until he softened toward her because of what he saw of her passion for him, and he was no longer wary of her, until they were left alone in some room, and he desired her." These are the sayings of the exegetes from the righteous predecessors.

A group of later scholars said: "This does not befit the prophets," so they interpreted the verse in various ways. Some said: "He desired to flee from her." This is not correct, because the fleeing is mentioned, and there is no mention of it in the verse. It was said: "He desired to strike her and push her away." It was said: "He desired to dispute with her and bring her case before her husband." It was said: "*Wa-hamma bihā* is a reference to something not mentioned." It was said: "The statement is complete at His saying: ﴿And she certainly desired him﴾, then the report about Yusuf begins: ﴿and he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾." This is with inversion (*taqdim wa ta'khir*), its estimate being: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have desired her, but he saw the proof and did not desire her," like His saying: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan﴾. This is corrupt according to the linguists, because the Arabs do not place the answer of *law-la* (had it not been) before it. One does not say: "I stood up had it not been for Zayd," meaning: "Had it not been for Zayd, I would have stood up."

Juwaybir reported from al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "She desired Yusuf that he should lie with her, and ﴿and he would have desired her﴾ means he wished her to be his wife."

These interpretations that we have related are all weak and not acceptable, because they contradict the sayings of the earlier scholars from whom interpretation is taken, and they took it from those who witnessed the revelation.

It has been reported in a sound report that when Yusuf entered upon the king and the woman confessed, Yusuf said: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence.﴾ Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: "Nor when you desired her, O Yusuf?" Yusuf then said: ﴿"And I do not acquit myself; indeed, the soul is most commanding of evil, except what my Lord has mercy upon."﴾

As for the people of realities (*ahl al-haqa'iq*), they said regarding this verse: "Desire is of two kinds: a settled desire (*hamm muqim*, lasting), which is when it is accompanied by determination, resolve, intention and consent, like the desire of the wife of the Chief, and in that case the covenant is taken. And a passing desire (*hamm 'arid*), which is a passing thought, a fancy and a self-talk without choice or determination, like the desire of Yusuf (peace be upon him), and the covenant is not taken as long as one does not speak it or do it." This is shown by what was reported from Ibn al-Mubarak, who said: "I said to Sufyan: 'Is one held accountable for a mere desire?' He said: 'If it is a determination, one is held accountable for it.'"

It was reported from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'When My servant desires a good deed and does not do it, I write it for him as a good deed; and if he does it, I write it for him as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times. And when My servant desires an evil deed and does not do it, I do not write it against him; if he does it, I write it against him as one evil deed; and if he leaves it for My sake, I write it for him as a good deed.'"

The affirmation of such slips and minor sins in the case of the prophets (peace be upon them) is not forbidden, for a kind of wisdom:
First: that they may be in awe of Allah, Exalted, when they recall them, so they strive in His obedience out of fear, and do not rely on the vastness of Allah's mercy.
Second: to make them know the position of His blessing and His favor upon them in turning it away from them.
Third: to make them leaders for the sinners in hope of Allah's mercy and in not despairing of His pardon and bounty.

'Ikrimah reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one meets Allah, Mighty and Majestic, without having desired a sin or committed it, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya, for he did not desire it and did not commit it."

It was reported from Mus'ab ibn Abd Allah, who said: Mus'ab ibn 'Uthman told me: "Sulayman ibn Yasar was among the most handsome of people. A woman came in to him seeking a fatwa, and she tempted him with herself, but he refused her and admonished her. She said to him: 'If you do not do it, I will certainly spread word against you and I will cry out against you.' He went out and left her, and he saw in his dream Yusuf the Prophet (peace be upon him), who said to him: 'Are you Yusuf?' He said: 'I am Yusuf the Prophet. I desired, and you are Sulayman, who did not desire.'"

As for the proof that Yusuf (peace be upon him) saw, the scholars differed concerning it. Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Husayn ibn 'Atiyyah, from Isra'il, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: "A likeness of Ya'qub appeared to him and struck his chest with his hand, and his desire came out through his fingertips."

Al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Ibn Sirin, Abu Salih, Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah and al-Dahhak said: "The ceiling of the room opened for him, and he saw Ya'qub biting his finger."

Ibn Jubayr said: "Every son of Ya'qub had twelve sons, except Yusuf, who had eleven sons, because some of his desire was reduced when he saw the image of his father, and so he felt shame."

Qatadah said: "He saw the image of Ya'qub, and said: 'O Yusuf, will you do the deed of fools while you are written among the prophets?'"

Ibn Abi Mulaykah reported from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "It was called out: 'O Yusuf, will you commit adultery, and be like a bird whose feathers have fallen, and it tries to fly but has no feathers?'"

Al-Suddi said: "It was called out: 'O Yusuf, will you lie with her? Your likeness, so long as you do not lie with her, is like a bird in the air of the sky that is not released; and your likeness if you lie with her is like a [bird] that dies and falls to the earth, unable to ward off itself. And your likeness, so long as you do not lie with her, is like the difficult bull on which no work is done; and your likeness if you lie with her is like the bull when it dies, and ants enter the base of its horns, and it cannot ward them off from itself.'"

Abu Mardud reported from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: "Yusuf raised his head to the ceiling of the room when he desired, and he saw a writing on the wall of the room: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way.﴾"

Abu Ma'shar reported from him: "Had he not seen what was in the Qur'an of the magnification and prohibition of adultery." Al-Qurazi added: "in the Qur'an and the scrolls of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)."

Layth reported from Mujahid from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: "He untied his trousers and sat between her thighs as a man sits with his wife, and behold, a palm was extended between them, with no arm and no wrist, on which was written: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do.﴾"

He said: "So he stood up fleeing, and she stood up. When the terror left them, she returned and he returned. When he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, behold, a palm was extended between them, with no arm and no wrist, on which was written: ﴿And fear a day when you will be returned to Allah, then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ So he stood up fleeing, and she stood up. When the terror left them, she returned and he returned. When he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, Allah, exalted is He, said to Jibril (peace be upon him): 'O Jibril, overtake My servant before he commits the sin.' Jibril saw him biting his finger or his palm, and he was saying: 'O Yusuf, will you do the deed of fools while you are written with Allah among the prophets?'"

That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil and immorality.﴾

Qatadah reported from 'Atiyyah from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: "When Yusuf and the wife of the Chief were about to do what they were about to do, a palm without a body came out between them, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿Is then He who is standing over every soul for what it has earned [like those who associate others with Him]?﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned between them, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do.﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned, and on it was written in Hebrew: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way.﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned a fourth time, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿And fear a day when you will be returned to Allah.﴾ Then Yusuf fled."

'Atiyyah reported from Ibn 'Abbas that the proof which Yusuf saw was that the image of the king was shown to him. Umar ibn Ishaq reported from some people of knowledge that it was Qatafir, his master, who arrived at the door at that moment; when he fled from her, she pursued him and found him at the door.

Ali ibn Musa al-Rida reported from his father, from Ja'far al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "My father told me, from his father, Ali ibn al-Husayn, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: The wife of the Chief went to the idol and covered it with a cloth.
