It was also said that the meaning is: do not be concerned with it, for your innocence was clear. Then he said to his wife: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. It was also said that this is from the witness to Yusuf and to Raahil, and by his saying ﴿and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ he meant: ask your husband not to punish you for your sin, and to pardon you. This is the meaning reported from Ibn Abbas.

﴿Indeed, you were of those who committed sin﴾: that is, among the sinners, when you sought to seduce a young man against himself and betrayed your husband. When he refrained, you lied about him. It is said: "khati'a yakhta'u khata'an and khata'an and khatha'an and khata'an," meaning he sinned, and the noun derived from it is "khati'ah" (sin). God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, killing them was a great sin﴾ [Q 17:31]. Umayya said:

"Your servants err, and You are the Lord; in Your two palms are the deaths and the decrees."

That is, they sin. When one intends deliberate action, one says "khati'a" with the vowel of the verb being "a"? Here [the verb] is with alif, as God the Exalted said: ﴿And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by error﴾ [Q 4:92].

As for why He said ﴿of those who committed sin﴾ and did not say "of the sinful women", it is because He did not intend to speak about women, but about the one who does such a thing. Its implied sense is "of the sinful people". Similar to it is His saying: ﴿and she was of the obedient ones﴾ [Q 66:12]. Its explanation is His saying: ﴿indeed she was of a disbelieving people﴾ [Q 27:43].

And she in whose house he was, meaning the wife of the Chief (al-'Aziz), sought to seduce him, and she asked him to have intercourse with her. ﴿And she locked the doors﴾, and they were seven.

﴿And she said: "Come, you."﴾ The readers differed concerning it. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Sulami, Abu Wa'il and Qatadah read *hi'ta lak* (هئت لك) with a kasra on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*, with a hamza, meaning "I have prepared myself for you." Abu 'Amr rejected this reading. Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna said: I heard Abu 'Amr being asked about the reading of one who reads *hi'ta lak* with a kasra on the *ha'* and a hamza on the *ya'*, and Abu 'Amr said: "It is false. He has taken it from *tahayya'tu* (I prepared myself). Go and survey the Arabs until you reach Yemen; do you know anyone who says this?" Al-Kisa'i also said: "*Hi'ta* has not been transmitted from the Arabs." 'Ikrimah said: *hi'ta lak* means "she adorned herself for you and beautified herself," and this reading is not approved.

Nasr ibn 'Asim, Yahya ibn Ya'mar and Abdullah ibn Abi Ishaq read *hayta lak* (هيت لك) with a fatha on the *ha'* and a kasra on the *ta'*. Yahya ibn Wathhab read *hayt* (هِيتُ) with a kasra on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*. Ibn Kathir read it with a fatha on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*. Tarafah recited:

"My people are not the most distant when one calls from the clan, *hayt*,
They respond swiftly, like flocks of birds, leaving no house behind."

The people of Medina and Syria read it with a kasra on the *ha'* and a fatha on the *ta'*, and the rest read it with a fatha on both the *ha'* and the *ta'*. This is the dialect of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the well-known usage among the Arabs.

Al-Sha'bi reported from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "The Prophet (ﷺ) recited to me *hayta lak*."

Al-A'mash reported from Abu Wa'il from Ibn Mas'ud that he recited *hi'ta lak*, and it was said to him, "*Hayta lak*," and Ibn Mas'ud said: "We only recite it as we were taught it and as we heard it, all together: *hallumma*, come, and approach." A poet, addressing the Commander of the Faithful Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), said:

"Convey to the Commander of the Faithful, the people of Iraq, when you arrive,
That Iraq and its people are yours, so *hayta*, *hayta*."

Al-Suddi said: "In Coptic it means *halumma lak*" (come to you). Al-Husayn said: "*Hayta lak* is a word in Syriac meaning 'upon you'." Abu 'Ubayd said: "Al-Kisa'i used to say it is the dialect of the people of Hawran that reached the Hijaz, and its meaning is 'come'." Abu 'Ubayd said: "I asked a learned elder from Hawran, and he mentioned that it is their dialect." 'Ikrimah said likewise.

Mujahid and others said: "It is an Arabic dialect by which she invited him to herself. It is a word of urging and of turning toward something." The root of both is the calling and shouting. The Arabs say, "*Hayyata* so-and-so with so-and-so," when he called him and shouted at him. A poet said:

"The silence of the camel-driver has troubled me;
Had he been addressed by it, he would have shouted *hayyata*."

That is, he shouted at him. *Al-Kari* means the camel-driver.

Our teacher Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: "I saw in some exegeses, *hayta lak*, which says: 'Do you have a desire for my beauty and my comeliness?'" Abu 'Ubaydah mentioned that the Arabs do not form the dual of *hayta*, nor its plural, nor its feminine; it is in one form in every case, and it is distinguished only by what follows it and what precedes it.

Yusuf (peace be upon him) said at that: ﴿"Allah forbid! I seek refuge and protection in Allah from what you invite me to."﴾ *Ma'adha Allah* is a verbal noun, its estimated form being *'iyadhan billah* (seeking refuge in Allah).

﴿"Indeed, he is my lord; he has made my dwelling good."﴾ That is, your husband Qatafir, my master. This is the view of most exegetes. Some said: it refers back to Allah, ﴿"he has made my dwelling good"﴾, meaning He sheltered me and saved me from the trial of love.

﴿"Indeed, the wrongdoers will not prosper."﴾ That is, if I did it, after he honored me and entrusted me, I would have betrayed him regarding his family, and "he has made my dwelling good," so I would be a wrongdoer, and ﴿the wrongdoers will not prosper﴾. It was also said: the adulterers.

﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her.﴾ The meaning of desire (*hamm*) for a thing is that a person speaks to himself about it without doing it. A poet said:

"I desired, and did not act; I nearly did, and would that I had not,
Leaving the wives of 'Uthman weeping over him."

As for the desire that Yusuf (peace be upon him) had for the woman, and her desire for him, the scholars differed concerning it. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah reported from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: "I heard Ibn 'Abbas asked: 'How far did the desire of Yusuf go?' He said: 'He untied the drawstring and sat between her legs like a man sits with his wife.'"

Ibn Jurayj reported from Ibn Abi 'Atiyyah, who said: "I asked Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) how far the desire of Yusuf went. He said: 'She lay on her back, and he sat between her legs to take off his clothes.'"

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "He loosened the cord of his trousers." Mujahid said: "He untied the trousers until they reached the ankles, and he sat with her as a man sits with his wife."

Al-Dahhak said: "Satan ran between them; he struck with his hand at Yusuf's collar and with the other hand at the woman's collar until he joined them together."

Al-Suddi and Ibn Ishaq said: "When the wife of the Chief wanted to seduce Yusuf, she began to mention to him the excellence of his person and to express her longing for herself. She said to him: 'O Yusuf, how beautiful is your hair!' He said: 'It is the first thing to fall from my body.' She said: 'O Yusuf, how beautiful is your eye!' He said: 'It is the first thing to flow to the earth from my body.' She said: 'How beautiful is your face!' He said: 'It is for the dust to eat.' She kept obeying him once and frightening him another time, and inviting him to pleasure, while he was a young man in the full vigor of youth, with such desire as a man has, and she was a beautiful, lovely woman, until he softened toward her because of what he saw of her passion for him, and he was no longer wary of her, until they were left alone in some room, and he desired her." These are the sayings of the exegetes from the righteous predecessors.

A group of later scholars said: "This does not befit the prophets," so they interpreted the verse in various ways. Some said: "He desired to flee from her." This is not correct, because the fleeing is mentioned, and there is no mention of it in the verse. It was said: "He desired to strike her and push her away." It was said: "He desired to dispute with her and bring her case before her husband." It was said: "*Wa-hamma bihā* is a reference to something not mentioned." It was said: "The statement is complete at His saying: ﴿And she certainly desired him﴾, then the report about Yusuf begins: ﴿and he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾." This is with inversion (*taqdim wa ta'khir*), its estimate being: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have desired her, but he saw the proof and did not desire her," like His saying: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan﴾. This is corrupt according to the linguists, because the Arabs do not place the answer of *law-la* (had it not been) before it. One does not say: "I stood up had it not been for Zayd," meaning: "Had it not been for Zayd, I would have stood up."

Juwaybir reported from al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "She desired Yusuf that he should lie with her, and ﴿and he would have desired her﴾ means he wished her to be his wife."

These interpretations that we have related are all weak and not acceptable, because they contradict the sayings of the earlier scholars from whom interpretation is taken, and they took it from those who witnessed the revelation.

It has been reported in a sound report that when Yusuf entered upon the king and the woman confessed, Yusuf said: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence.﴾ Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: "Nor when you desired her, O Yusuf?" Yusuf then said: ﴿"And I do not acquit myself; indeed, the soul is most commanding of evil, except what my Lord has mercy upon."﴾

As for the people of realities (*ahl al-haqa'iq*), they said regarding this verse: "Desire is of two kinds: a settled desire (*hamm muqim*, lasting), which is when it is accompanied by determination, resolve, intention and consent, like the desire of the wife of the Chief, and in that case the covenant is taken. And a passing desire (*hamm 'arid*), which is a passing thought, a fancy and a self-talk without choice or determination, like the desire of Yusuf (peace be upon him), and the covenant is not taken as long as one does not speak it or do it." This is shown by what was reported from Ibn al-Mubarak, who said: "I said to Sufyan: 'Is one held accountable for a mere desire?' He said: 'If it is a determination, one is held accountable for it.'"

It was reported from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'When My servant desires a good deed and does not do it, I write it for him as a good deed; and if he does it, I write it for him as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times. And when My servant desires an evil deed and does not do it, I do not write it against him; if he does it, I write it against him as one evil deed; and if he leaves it for My sake, I write it for him as a good deed.'"

The affirmation of such slips and minor sins in the case of the prophets (peace be upon them) is not forbidden, for a kind of wisdom:
First: that they may be in awe of Allah, Exalted, when they recall them, so they strive in His obedience out of fear, and do not rely on the vastness of Allah's mercy.
Second: to make them know the position of His blessing and His favor upon them in turning it away from them.
Third: to make them leaders for the sinners in hope of Allah's mercy and in not despairing of His pardon and bounty.

'Ikrimah reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one meets Allah, Mighty and Majestic, without having desired a sin or committed it, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya, for he did not desire it and did not commit it."

It was reported from Mus'ab ibn Abd Allah, who said: Mus'ab ibn 'Uthman told me: "Sulayman ibn Yasar was among the most handsome of people. A woman came in to him seeking a fatwa, and she tempted him with herself, but he refused her and admonished her. She said to him: 'If you do not do it, I will certainly spread word against you and I will cry out against you.' He went out and left her, and he saw in his dream Yusuf the Prophet (peace be upon him), who said to him: 'Are you Yusuf?' He said: 'I am Yusuf the Prophet. I desired, and you are Sulayman, who did not desire.'"

As for the proof that Yusuf (peace be upon him) saw, the scholars differed concerning it. Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Husayn ibn 'Atiyyah, from Isra'il, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: "A likeness of Ya'qub appeared to him and struck his chest with his hand, and his desire came out through his fingertips."

Al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Ibn Sirin, Abu Salih, Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah and al-Dahhak said: "The ceiling of the room opened for him, and he saw Ya'qub biting his finger."

Ibn Jubayr said: "Every son of Ya'qub had twelve sons, except Yusuf, who had eleven sons, because some of his desire was reduced when he saw the image of his father, and so he felt shame."

Qatadah said: "He saw the image of Ya'qub, and said: 'O Yusuf, will you do the deed of fools while you are written among the prophets?'"

Ibn Abi Mulaykah reported from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "It was called out: 'O Yusuf, will you commit adultery, and be like a bird whose feathers have fallen, and it tries to fly but has no feathers?'"

Al-Suddi said: "It was called out: 'O Yusuf, will you lie with her? Your likeness, so long as you do not lie with her, is like a bird in the air of the sky that is not released; and your likeness if you lie with her is like a [bird] that dies and falls to the earth, unable to ward off itself. And your likeness, so long as you do not lie with her, is like the difficult bull on which no work is done; and your likeness if you lie with her is like the bull when it dies, and ants enter the base of its horns, and it cannot ward them off from itself.'"

Abu Mardud reported from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: "Yusuf raised his head to the ceiling of the room when he desired, and he saw a writing on the wall of the room: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way.﴾"

Abu Ma'shar reported from him: "Had he not seen what was in the Qur'an of the magnification and prohibition of adultery." Al-Qurazi added: "in the Qur'an and the scrolls of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)."

Layth reported from Mujahid from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: "He untied his trousers and sat between her thighs as a man sits with his wife, and behold, a palm was extended between them, with no arm and no wrist, on which was written: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do.﴾"

He said: "So he stood up fleeing, and she stood up. When the terror left them, she returned and he returned. When he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, behold, a palm was extended between them, with no arm and no wrist, on which was written: ﴿And fear a day when you will be returned to Allah, then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ So he stood up fleeing, and she stood up. When the terror left them, she returned and he returned. When he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, Allah, exalted is He, said to Jibril (peace be upon him): 'O Jibril, overtake My servant before he commits the sin.' Jibril saw him biting his finger or his palm, and he was saying: 'O Yusuf, will you do the deed of fools while you are written with Allah among the prophets?'"

That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil and immorality.﴾

Qatadah reported from 'Atiyyah from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: "When Yusuf and the wife of the Chief were about to do what they were about to do, a palm without a body came out between them, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿Is then He who is standing over every soul for what it has earned [like those who associate others with Him]?﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned between them, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do.﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned, and on it was written in Hebrew: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way.﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned a fourth time, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿And fear a day when you will be returned to Allah.﴾ Then Yusuf fled."

'Atiyyah reported from Ibn 'Abbas that the proof which Yusuf saw was that the image of the king was shown to him. Umar ibn Ishaq reported from some people of knowledge that it was Qatafir, his master, who arrived at the door at that moment; when he fled from her, she pursued him and found him at the door.

Ali ibn Musa al-Rida reported from his father, from Ja'far al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "My father told me, from his father, Ali ibn al-Husayn, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: The wife of the Chief went to the idol and covered it with a cloth. Yusuf said to her: 'What is this?' She said: 'I am ashamed before the idol that it should see us.' Yusuf said:

'Are you ashamed before one who does not hear, nor see, nor understand, nor witness, and I should not be ashamed before the One who created things and taught them?'"

Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: "The proof is the prophethood which Allah deposited in his breast, and it was what prevented him from what displeases Allah."

It was said: "It is what Allah gave him of knowledge and wisdom." The people of allusion (*ahl al-isharah*) said: "The believer has a proof from his Lord in his secret, from his knowledge, and he saw that proof, and it was his restrainer."

So the "proof" is the sign and the argument. The answer of *law-la* (had it not been) is omitted, its estimate being: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have committed adultery." He reconciled the natural desire with the desire of acquisition, according to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Accepting of repentance and Wise, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾. Its meaning: "You would have been destroyed." Imru' al-Qays said:

"If only she were a soul that dies in peace,
But she is a soul that wastes our souls."

He meant: "*Saqatat*" (she fell) — "fanīt" (perished), and "lahhan 'alayya" (anguished over me), and similar.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil﴾, the sin, ﴿and immorality﴾, adultery.

﴿Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.﴾ The people of Mecca and Basra read it with a kasra on the *lam* (*al-mukhlisin*), meaning those who made their devotion and worship sincere to Allah. The others read it with a fatha on the *lam* (*al-mukhlasin*), meaning those chosen for prophethood, and the evidence for it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We made them sincere with a pure sincerity﴾.

Al-Zuhri reported from Hamzah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Imran ibn Umar, who said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) became ill with the pain of which he died, he (ﷺ) said: 'Let Abu Bakr lead the people in prayer.' 'A'ishah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr is a tender man, and he cannot control himself when he recites the Qur'an, so command Umar to lead the people in prayer.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Let Abu Bakr lead the people in prayer.' I repeated it to him, and he said: 'Let Abu Bakr lead the people in prayer, for you are like the companions of Yusuf.'" 'A'ishah said: "By Allah, what moved me in that matter against them was only that he would be the first man to stand in the place of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba narrated to us: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Ja'far al-Mustamli narrated to us: some of our companions narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman said: "I heard a woman in some of the roads speaking with some lewdness, so I said to her: [....] [[Unreadable word.]] You are indeed the female companions of Yusuf." The woman said to him: "Alas! We invited him to pleasure, while you wanted to kill him. So whose companions are we or you? And is taking a life greater than what we wanted?"

﴿And they both raced to the door﴾. This is because when Yusuf saw the proof, he rose hastily toward the door of the house, fleeing from what she wanted from him, and the woman followed him. This is the meaning of the verse.

﴿And they both raced to the door﴾: Yusuf and Raahil (Zulaykha) hurried to the door. As for Yusuf, he fled from committing the immorality. As for the woman, she sought to reach Yusuf so that she might fulfill her desire, i.e., he had been solicited by her. She caught up with him and seized his shirt from behind and pulled him back toward her, preventing him from leaving.

﴿And tore his shirt﴾: she ripped and split his shirt. ﴿From behind﴾: from the back, not from the front, because Yusuf was the one fleeing and the woman was the one pursuing. When they both came out and ﴿found her master at the door﴾, meaning they found her husband Qitfir sitting at the door with a cousin of Raahil. When she saw him, she was overcome with fear, so she spoke first to her husband, saying: ﴿What is the recompense for one who intended evil for your family, except that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?﴾ She meant adultery; "imprisoned" means detained, and "a painful punishment" means being beaten with whips. This was reported by Ibn Abbas.

﴿Yusuf said: "It was she who sought to seduce me"﴾, and ﴿a witness from her family testified﴾. The scholars differed about this witness. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Hilal ibn Yasar and al-Dahhak said he was an infant in the cradle whom God made to speak by His power.

Al-Awfi narrated to us from Ibn Abbas, and Shahr ibn Hawshab from Abu Hurayra. What supports this is what Ata ibn al-Sa'ib narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Four spoke while they were infants: the son of the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter, the witness of Yusuf, the companion of Jurayj, and Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him)."

It was said that this infant was the son of the woman's maternal uncle. Al-Hasan said he was her servant boy. Qatada, al-Dahhak and Mujahid, through a narration [ ... ] [[Unreadable word.]], said: "He was not a child, but a wise man with a beard, possessing opinion, speech and a sign." This is the narration of Ibn Abi Mulayka from Ibn Abbas, who said: "He was among the close circle of the king." Al-Suddi said: "He was the cousin of Raahil, and he was sitting with her husband at the door, so he judged, and God the Exalted reported about him: ﴿If his shirt is torn from the front...﴾" (the verse).

Isa narrated from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "The witness is the shirt torn from behind." The meaning of ﴿a witness testified﴾ is that a judge decided. ﴿From her family﴾. Mujahid said: "The witness said: the explanation of this matter lies in the shirt."

﴿If his shirt is torn from behind, then she has lied and he is of the truthful. But if his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars.﴾ Ibn Abi Ishaq read "al-qubul" and "al-dubur" with a light pronunciation, while the others read them with emphasis; both are two dialects.

So the shirt was brought, and behold, it was torn from behind. When Qitfir saw his shirt torn from behind, he recognized his wife's betrayal and Yusuf's innocence. So he said to her: ﴿Indeed, this is of your guile; indeed, your guile is great.﴾ It was also said that this is the speech of the witness.

Then Qitfir turned to Yusuf and said: ﴿Yusuf﴾, meaning "O Yusuf", a singular vocative, ﴿turn away from this matter﴾, so do not mention it to anyone. It was also said that the meaning is: do not be concerned with it, for your innocence was clear. Then he said to his wife: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. It was also said that this is from the witness to Yusuf and to Raahil, and by his saying ﴿and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ he meant: ask your husband not to punish you for your sin, and to pardon you. This is the meaning reported from Ibn Abbas.

﴿Indeed, you were of those who committed sin﴾: that is, among the sinners, when you sought to seduce a young man against himself and betrayed your husband. When he refrained, you lied about him. It is said: "khati'a yakhta'u khata'an and khata'an and khatha'an and khata'an," meaning he sinned, and the noun derived from it is "khati'ah" (sin). God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, killing them was a great sin﴾ [Q 17:31]. Umayya said:

"Your servants err, and You are the Lord; in Your two palms are the deaths and the decrees."

That is, they sin. When one intends deliberate action, one says "khati'a" with the vowel of the verb being "a"? Here [the verb] is with alif, as God the Exalted said: ﴿And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by error﴾ [Q 4:92].

As for why He said ﴿of those who committed sin﴾ and did not say "of the sinful women", it is because He did not intend to speak about women, but about the one who does such a thing. Its implied sense is "of the sinful people". Similar to it is His saying: ﴿and she was of the obedient ones﴾ [Q 66:12]. Its explanation is His saying: ﴿indeed she was of a disbelieving people﴾ [Q 27:43].

And she in whose house he was, meaning the wife of the Chief (al-'Aziz), sought to seduce him, and she asked him to have intercourse with her. ﴿And she locked the doors﴾, and they were seven.

﴿And she said: "Come, you."﴾ The readers differed concerning it. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Sulami, Abu Wa'il and Qatadah read *hi'ta lak* (هئت لك) with a kasra on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*, with a hamza, meaning "I have prepared myself for you." Abu 'Amr rejected this reading. Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna said: I heard Abu 'Amr being asked about the reading of one who reads *hi'ta lak* with a kasra on the *ha'* and a hamza on the *ya'*, and Abu 'Amr said: "It is false. He has taken it from *tahayya'tu* (I prepared myself). Go and survey the Arabs until you reach Yemen; do you know anyone who says this?" Al-Kisa'i also said: "*Hi'ta* has not been transmitted from the Arabs." 'Ikrimah said: *hi'ta lak* means "she adorned herself for you and beautified herself," and this reading is not approved.

Nasr ibn 'Asim, Yahya ibn Ya'mar and Abdullah ibn Abi Ishaq read *hayta lak* (هيت لك) with a fatha on the *ha'* and a kasra on the *ta'*. Yahya ibn Wathhab read *hayt* (هِيتُ) with a kasra on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*. Ibn Kathir read it with a fatha on the *ha'* and a damma on the *ta'*. Tarafah recited:

"My people are not the most distant when one calls from the clan, *hayt*,
They respond swiftly, like flocks of birds, leaving no house behind."

The people of Medina and Syria read it with a kasra on the *ha'* and a fatha on the *ta'*, and the rest read it with a fatha on both the *ha'* and the *ta'*. This is the dialect of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the well-known usage among the Arabs.

Al-Sha'bi reported from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "The Prophet (ﷺ) recited to me *hayta lak*."

Al-A'mash reported from Abu Wa'il from Ibn Mas'ud that he recited *hi'ta lak*, and it was said to him, "*Hayta lak*," and Ibn Mas'ud said: "We only recite it as we were taught it and as we heard it, all together: *hallumma*, come, and approach." A poet, addressing the Commander of the Faithful Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), said:

"Convey to the Commander of the Faithful, the people of Iraq, when you arrive,
That Iraq and its people are yours, so *hayta*, *hayta*."

Al-Suddi said: "In Coptic it means *halumma lak*" (come to you). Al-Husayn said: "*Hayta lak* is a word in Syriac meaning 'upon you'." Abu 'Ubayd said: "Al-Kisa'i used to say it is the dialect of the people of Hawran that reached the Hijaz, and its meaning is 'come'." Abu 'Ubayd said: "I asked a learned elder from Hawran, and he mentioned that it is their dialect." 'Ikrimah said likewise.

Mujahid and others said: "It is an Arabic dialect by which she invited him to herself. It is a word of urging and of turning toward something." The root of both is the calling and shouting. The Arabs say, "*Hayyata* so-and-so with so-and-so," when he called him and shouted at him. A poet said:

"The silence of the camel-driver has troubled me;
Had he been addressed by it, he would have shouted *hayyata*."

That is, he shouted at him. *Al-Kari* means the camel-driver.

Our teacher Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: "I saw in some exegeses, *hayta lak*, which says: 'Do you have a desire for my beauty and my comeliness?'" Abu 'Ubaydah mentioned that the Arabs do not form the dual of *hayta*, nor its plural, nor its feminine; it is in one form in every case, and it is distinguished only by what follows it and what precedes it.

Yusuf (peace be upon him) said at that: ﴿"Allah forbid! I seek refuge and protection in Allah from what you invite me to."﴾ *Ma'adha Allah* is a verbal noun, its estimated form being *'iyadhan billah* (seeking refuge in Allah).

﴿"Indeed, he is my lord; he has made my dwelling good."﴾ That is, your husband Qatafir, my master. This is the view of most exegetes. Some said: it refers back to Allah, ﴿"he has made my dwelling good"﴾, meaning He sheltered me and saved me from the trial of love.

﴿"Indeed, the wrongdoers will not prosper."﴾ That is, if I did it, after he honored me and entrusted me, I would have betrayed him regarding his family, and "he has made my dwelling good," so I would be a wrongdoer, and ﴿the wrongdoers will not prosper﴾. It was also said: the adulterers.

﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her.﴾ The meaning of desire (*hamm*) for a thing is that a person speaks to himself about it without doing it. A poet said:

"I desired, and did not act; I nearly did, and would that I had not,
Leaving the wives of 'Uthman weeping over him."

As for the desire that Yusuf (peace be upon him) had for the woman, and her desire for him, the scholars differed concerning it. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah reported from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: "I heard Ibn 'Abbas asked: 'How far did the desire of Yusuf go?' He said: 'He untied the drawstring and sat between her legs like a man sits with his wife.'"

Ibn Jurayj reported from Ibn Abi 'Atiyyah, who said: "I asked Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) how far the desire of Yusuf went. He said: 'She lay on her back, and he sat between her legs to take off his clothes.'"

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "He loosened the cord of his trousers." Mujahid said: "He untied the trousers until they reached the ankles, and he sat with her as a man sits with his wife."

Al-Dahhak said: "Satan ran between them; he struck with his hand at Yusuf's collar and with the other hand at the woman's collar until he joined them together."

Al-Suddi and Ibn Ishaq said: "When the wife of the Chief wanted to seduce Yusuf, she began to mention to him the excellence of his person and to express her longing for herself. She said to him: 'O Yusuf, how beautiful is your hair!' He said: 'It is the first thing to fall from my body.' She said: 'O Yusuf, how beautiful is your eye!' He said: 'It is the first thing to flow to the earth from my body.' She said: 'How beautiful is your face!' He said: 'It is for the dust to eat.' She kept obeying him once and frightening him another time, and inviting him to pleasure, while he was a young man in the full vigor of youth, with such desire as a man has, and she was a beautiful, lovely woman, until he softened toward her because of what he saw of her passion for him, and he was no longer wary of her, until they were left alone in some room, and he desired her." These are the sayings of the exegetes from the righteous predecessors.

A group of later scholars said: "This does not befit the prophets," so they interpreted the verse in various ways. Some said: "He desired to flee from her." This is not correct, because the fleeing is mentioned, and there is no mention of it in the verse. It was said: "He desired to strike her and push her away." It was said: "He desired to dispute with her and bring her case before her husband." It was said: "*Wa-hamma bihā* is a reference to something not mentioned." It was said: "The statement is complete at His saying: ﴿And she certainly desired him﴾, then the report about Yusuf begins: ﴿and he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾." This is with inversion (*taqdim wa ta'khir*), its estimate being: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have desired her, but he saw the proof and did not desire her," like His saying: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan﴾. This is corrupt according to the linguists, because the Arabs do not place the answer of *law-la* (had it not been) before it. One does not say: "I stood up had it not been for Zayd," meaning: "Had it not been for Zayd, I would have stood up."

Juwaybir reported from al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "She desired Yusuf that he should lie with her, and ﴿and he would have desired her﴾ means he wished her to be his wife."

These interpretations that we have related are all weak and not acceptable, because they contradict the sayings of the earlier scholars from whom interpretation is taken, and they took it from those who witnessed the revelation.

It has been reported in a sound report that when Yusuf entered upon the king and the woman confessed, Yusuf said: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence.﴾ Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: "Nor when you desired her, O Yusuf?" Yusuf then said: ﴿"And I do not acquit myself; indeed, the soul is most commanding of evil, except what my Lord has mercy upon."﴾

As for the people of realities (*ahl al-haqa'iq*), they said regarding this verse: "Desire is of two kinds: a settled desire (*hamm muqim*, lasting), which is when it is accompanied by determination, resolve, intention and consent, like the desire of the wife of the Chief, and in that case the covenant is taken. And a passing desire (*hamm 'arid*), which is a passing thought, a fancy and a self-talk without choice or determination, like the desire of Yusuf (peace be upon him), and the covenant is not taken as long as one does not speak it or do it." This is shown by what was reported from Ibn al-Mubarak, who said: "I said to Sufyan: 'Is one held accountable for a mere desire?' He said: 'If it is a determination, one is held accountable for it.'"

It was reported from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'When My servant desires a good deed and does not do it, I write it for him as a good deed; and if he does it, I write it for him as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times. And when My servant desires an evil deed and does not do it, I do not write it against him; if he does it, I write it against him as one evil deed; and if he leaves it for My sake, I write it for him as a good deed.'"

The affirmation of such slips and minor sins in the case of the prophets (peace be upon them) is not forbidden, for a kind of wisdom:
First: that they may be in awe of Allah, Exalted, when they recall them, so they strive in His obedience out of fear, and do not rely on the vastness of Allah's mercy.
Second: to make them know the position of His blessing and His favor upon them in turning it away from them.
Third: to make them leaders for the sinners in hope of Allah's mercy and in not despairing of His pardon and bounty.

'Ikrimah reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one meets Allah, Mighty and Majestic, without having desired a sin or committed it, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya, for he did not desire it and did not commit it."

It was reported from Mus'ab ibn Abd Allah, who said: Mus'ab ibn 'Uthman told me: "Sulayman ibn Yasar was among the most handsome of people. A woman came in to him seeking a fatwa, and she tempted him with herself, but he refused her and admonished her. She said to him: 'If you do not do it, I will certainly spread word against you and I will cry out against you.' He went out and left her, and he saw in his dream Yusuf the Prophet (peace be upon him), who said to him: 'Are you Yusuf?' He said: 'I am Yusuf the Prophet. I desired, and you are Sulayman, who did not desire.'"

As for the proof that Yusuf (peace be upon him) saw, the scholars differed concerning it. Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Husayn ibn 'Atiyyah, from Isra'il, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: "A likeness of Ya'qub appeared to him and struck his chest with his hand, and his desire came out through his fingertips."

Al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Ibn Sirin, Abu Salih, Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah and al-Dahhak said: "The ceiling of the room opened for him, and he saw Ya'qub biting his finger."

Ibn Jubayr said: "Every son of Ya'qub had twelve sons, except Yusuf, who had eleven sons, because some of his desire was reduced when he saw the image of his father, and so he felt shame."

Qatadah said: "He saw the image of Ya'qub, and said: 'O Yusuf, will you do the deed of fools while you are written among the prophets?'"

Ibn Abi Mulaykah reported from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "It was called out: 'O Yusuf, will you commit adultery, and be like a bird whose feathers have fallen, and it tries to fly but has no feathers?'"

Al-Suddi said: "It was called out: 'O Yusuf, will you lie with her? Your likeness, so long as you do not lie with her, is like a bird in the air of the sky that is not released; and your likeness if you lie with her is like a [bird] that dies and falls to the earth, unable to ward off itself. And your likeness, so long as you do not lie with her, is like the difficult bull on which no work is done; and your likeness if you lie with her is like the bull when it dies, and ants enter the base of its horns, and it cannot ward them off from itself.'"

Abu Mardud reported from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: "Yusuf raised his head to the ceiling of the room when he desired, and he saw a writing on the wall of the room: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way.﴾"

Abu Ma'shar reported from him: "Had he not seen what was in the Qur'an of the magnification and prohibition of adultery." Al-Qurazi added: "in the Qur'an and the scrolls of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)."

Layth reported from Mujahid from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: "He untied his trousers and sat between her thighs as a man sits with his wife, and behold, a palm was extended between them, with no arm and no wrist, on which was written: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do.﴾"

He said: "So he stood up fleeing, and she stood up. When the terror left them, she returned and he returned. When he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, behold, a palm was extended between them, with no arm and no wrist, on which was written: ﴿And fear a day when you will be returned to Allah, then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ So he stood up fleeing, and she stood up. When the terror left them, she returned and he returned. When he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, Allah, exalted is He, said to Jibril (peace be upon him): 'O Jibril, overtake My servant before he commits the sin.' Jibril saw him biting his finger or his palm, and he was saying: 'O Yusuf, will you do the deed of fools while you are written with Allah among the prophets?'"

That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil and immorality.﴾

Qatadah reported from 'Atiyyah from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: "When Yusuf and the wife of the Chief were about to do what they were about to do, a palm without a body came out between them, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿Is then He who is standing over every soul for what it has earned [like those who associate others with Him]?﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned between them, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do.﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned, and on it was written in Hebrew: ﴿And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an abomination and an evil way.﴾ Then the palm withdrew, and they stood in their places. Then the palm returned a fourth time, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿And fear a day when you will be returned to Allah.﴾ Then Yusuf fled."

'Atiyyah reported from Ibn 'Abbas that the proof which Yusuf saw was that the image of the king was shown to him. Umar ibn Ishaq reported from some people of knowledge that it was Qatafir, his master, who arrived at the door at that moment; when he fled from her, she pursued him and found him at the door.

Ali ibn Musa al-Rida reported from his father, from Ja'far al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "My father told me, from his father, Ali ibn al-Husayn, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾: The wife of the Chief went to the idol and covered it with a cloth. Yusuf said to her: 'What is this?' She said: 'I am ashamed before the idol that it should see us.' Yusuf said:

'Are you ashamed before one who does not hear, nor see, nor understand, nor witness, and I should not be ashamed before the One who created things and taught them?'"

Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: "The proof is the prophethood which Allah deposited in his breast, and it was what prevented him from what displeases Allah."

It was said: "It is what Allah gave him of knowledge and wisdom." The people of allusion (*ahl al-isharah*) said: "The believer has a proof from his Lord in his secret, from his knowledge, and he saw that proof, and it was his restrainer."

So the "proof" is the sign and the argument. The answer of *law-la* (had it not been) is omitted, its estimate being: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have committed adultery." He reconciled the natural desire with the desire of acquisition, according to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Accepting of repentance and Wise, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾. Its meaning: "You would have been destroyed." Imru' al-Qays said:

"If only she were a soul that dies in peace,
But she is a soul that wastes our souls."

He meant: "*Saqatat*" (she fell) — "fanīt" (perished), and "lahhan 'alayya" (anguished over me), and similar.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Thus, that We might turn away from him evil﴾, the sin, ﴿and immorality﴾, adultery.

﴿Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.﴾ The people of Mecca and Basra read it with a kasra on the *lam* (*al-mukhlisin*), meaning those who made their devotion and worship sincere to Allah. The others read it with a fatha on the *lam* (*al-mukhlasin*), meaning those chosen for prophethood, and the evidence for it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We made them sincere with a pure sincerity﴾.

Al-Zuhri reported from Hamzah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Imran ibn Umar, who said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) became ill with the pain of which he died, he (ﷺ) said: 'Let Abu Bakr lead the people in prayer.' 'A'ishah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr is a tender man, and he cannot control himself when he recites the Qur'an, so command Umar to lead the people in prayer.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Let Abu Bakr lead the people in prayer.' I repeated it to him, and he said: 'Let Abu Bakr lead the people in prayer, for you are like the companions of Yusuf.'" 'A'ishah said: "By Allah, what moved me in that matter against them was only that he would be the first man to stand in the place of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba narrated to us: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Ja'far al-Mustamli narrated to us: some of our companions narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman said: "I heard a woman in some of the roads speaking with some lewdness, so I said to her: [....] [[Unreadable word.]] You are indeed the female companions of Yusuf." The woman said to him: "Alas! We invited him to pleasure, while you wanted to kill him. So whose companions are we or you? And is taking a life greater than what we wanted?"

﴿And they both raced to the door﴾. This is because when Yusuf saw the proof, he rose hastily toward the door of the house, fleeing from what she wanted from him, and the woman followed him. This is the meaning of the verse.

﴿And they both raced to the door﴾: Yusuf and Raahil (Zulaykha) hurried to the door. As for Yusuf, he fled from committing the immorality. As for the woman, she sought to reach Yusuf so that she might fulfill her desire, i.e., he had been solicited by her. She caught up with him and seized his shirt from behind and pulled him back toward her, preventing him from leaving.

﴿And tore his shirt﴾: she ripped and split his shirt. ﴿From behind﴾: from the back, not from the front, because Yusuf was the one fleeing and the woman was the one pursuing. When they both came out and ﴿found her master at the door﴾, meaning they found her husband Qitfir sitting at the door with a cousin of Raahil. When she saw him, she was overcome with fear, so she spoke first to her husband, saying: ﴿What is the recompense for one who intended evil for your family, except that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?﴾ She meant adultery; "imprisoned" means detained, and "a painful punishment" means being beaten with whips. This was reported by Ibn Abbas.

﴿Yusuf said: "It was she who sought to seduce me"﴾, and ﴿a witness from her family testified﴾. The scholars differed about this witness. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Hilal ibn Yasar and al-Dahhak said he was an infant in the cradle whom God made to speak by His power.

Al-Awfi narrated to us from Ibn Abbas, and Shahr ibn Hawshab from Abu Hurayra. What supports this is what Ata ibn al-Sa'ib narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Four spoke while they were infants: the son of the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter, the witness of Yusuf, the companion of Jurayj, and Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him)."

It was said that this infant was the son of the woman's maternal uncle. Al-Hasan said he was her servant boy. Qatada, al-Dahhak and Mujahid, through a narration [ ... ] [[Unreadable word.]], said: "He was not a child, but a wise man with a beard, possessing opinion, speech and a sign." This is the narration of Ibn Abi Mulayka from Ibn Abbas, who said: "He was among the close circle of the king." Al-Suddi said: "He was the cousin of Raahil, and he was sitting with her husband at the door, so he judged, and God the Exalted reported about him: ﴿If his shirt is torn from the front...﴾" (the verse).

Isa narrated from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "The witness is the shirt torn from behind." The meaning of ﴿a witness testified﴾ is that a judge decided. ﴿From her family﴾. Mujahid said: "The witness said: the explanation of this matter lies in the shirt."

﴿If his shirt is torn from behind, then she has lied and he is of the truthful. But if his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars.﴾ Ibn Abi Ishaq read "al-qubul" and "al-dubur" with a light pronunciation, while the others read them with emphasis; both are two dialects.

So the shirt was brought, and behold, it was torn from behind. When Qitfir saw his shirt torn from behind, he recognized his wife's betrayal and Yusuf's innocence. So he said to her: ﴿Indeed, this is of your guile; indeed, your guile is great.﴾ It was also said that this is the speech of the witness.

Then Qitfir turned to Yusuf and said: ﴿Yusuf﴾, meaning "O Yusuf", a singular vocative, ﴿turn away from this matter﴾, so do not mention it to anyone. It was also said that the meaning is: do not be concerned with it, for your innocence was clear. Then he said to his wife: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. It was also said that this is from the witness to Yusuf and to Raahil, and by his saying ﴿and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ he meant: ask your husband not to punish you for your sin, and to pardon you. This is the meaning reported from Ibn Abbas.

﴿Indeed, you were of those who committed sin﴾: that is, among the sinners, when you sought to seduce a young man against himself and betrayed your husband. When he refrained, you lied about him. It is said: "khati'a yakhta'u khata'an and khata'an and khatha'an and khata'an," meaning he sinned, and the noun derived from it is "khati'ah" (sin). God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, killing them was a great sin﴾ [Q 17:31]. Umayya said:

"Your servants err, and You are the Lord; in Your two palms are the deaths and the decrees."

That is, they sin. When one intends deliberate action, one says "khati'a" with the vowel of the verb being "a"? Here [the verb] is with alif, as God the Exalted said: ﴿And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by error﴾ [Q 4:92].

As for why He said ﴿of those who committed sin﴾ and did not say "of the sinful women", it is because He did not intend to speak about women, but about the one who does such a thing. Its implied sense is "of the sinful people". Similar to it is His saying: ﴿and she was of the obedient ones﴾ [Q 66:12]. Its explanation is His saying: ﴿indeed she was of a disbelieving people﴾ [Q 27:43].

And women in the city said: that is, the news of Joseph and the woman spread in the city of Egypt, and the women talked about it. They said, meaning the wife of the cupbearer, the wife of the baker, the wife of the prison keeper, and the wife of the chamberlain. Muqatil said: "The wife of al-'Aziz." In the language of the Arabs, *al-'Aziz* means the king. Abu Dawud said:

*A pearl that a merchant dove for,*
*Was displayed before the 'Aziz on a day of drizzle.* [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 12/259.]]

That is, "which king."

She seeks to seduce her young man, the Canaanite, away from himself.

*Has smitten her with love*: that is, she loved him so intensely that his love entered the *shaghaf* of her heart. The *shaghaf* is its covering and sheath. Al-Suddi said: "The *shaghaf* is a thin membrane over the heart, called the 'tongue of the heart.' One says: love penetrated the skin until it reached the heart." Al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani said:

*And a concern has come between me and that, entering*
*Like the entering of the shaghaf, which the fingers seek.* [[Kitab al-'Ayn: 4/360; Lisan al-'Arab: 9/179, where "wali[j]" is used instead of "dakhil" and "makan" instead of "dukhul".]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: "He hung her with love (*'allaqaha*)." Al-Hasan said: "He entered her inner part with love (*batnaha*)." Qatadah said: "He penetrated her interior with her love for him (*istabṭanaha*)." Abu Raja' said: "He made her sincere in love (*sadaqaha*)." Al-Kalbi said: "His love veiled her heart so that she could understand nothing other than him."

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, al-Sha'bi and al-A'raj read *sha'afaha*, with an unpointed 'ayn (*ayn* without a dot). Scholars differ on its meaning. Al-Farra' said: "He took her in every direction," from *sha'af al-jibal*, meaning the peaks of mountains. Al-Nakha'i and al-Dahhak said: "He enticed her and carried her away." Its root is from *sha'af al-dabbah*, when a beast rolls in the dirt in fright. Imru' al-Qais said:

*Will you kill me, when she has been smitten through her heart,*
*As the mange-stricken camel is smitten by the tar-smeared herdsman?* [[Jami' al-Bayan: 12/262; Lisan al-'Arab: 9/177, where "li-taqtulani" is used instead of "ataqtulani".]]

His meaning is: her heart went as the tar-smeared herdsman goes among the camels, who fear him and then find relief from him. Al-Akhfash said: "From her love for him." Muhammad ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: "Love encompassed her."

*Indeed, we see her in clear error*: that is, in manifest error. When she (Ra'il) heard *of their scheming*, that is, of their words and talk, Qatadah and al-Suddi said... Ibn Ishaq said: "They only said that as a scheme against her, so that they could see Joseph, for she had described to them his beauty and handsomeness." *She sent for them*. Wahb said: "She prepared a banquet and invited forty women, among them those who had reproached her." *And prepared for them*: she prepared (*a'tadat*, from the root of *i'tad*), which means provision and preparation. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire﴾ [[Surah al-Kahf 18:29.]].

*A cushion for them*: a place for food and the cushions and pillows they lean on. It is said: "He threw for him a *muttaka'*," meaning something to lean upon. This is the meaning of Ibn 'Abbas's statement in the narration of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Ishaq and Ibn Zayd said: "Food." Al-Qutabi said: "The origin of this is that when you invite someone to a meal at your place, you prepare a cushion or a *muttaka'* for him, so the food was called *muttaka'* by metaphor. One says: 'We reclined (*ittaka'na*) at so-and-so's place,' meaning we ate." 'Adi ibn Zayd said:

*So we lived in blessing and reclined (to eat),*
*And drank the lawful from its jugs.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/178.]]

It is reported from al-Hasan that he said: "*Muttaka'*" with a shadda and a long vowel is not eloquent. From al-Hasan also: "I do not think that is sound." Mujahid read *muttaka'*, light and unhamzated, and this is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas.

They differed over its meaning. Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the citron (*utrunj*)." 'Ikrimah said: "It is food." Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, said: "It is the *zamawards* (a kind of fruit or food)." 'Ali ibn al-Hakam and 'Ubayd ibn Hakim, from him, said: "Everything that is cut with a knife is, in the language of the Arabs, *muttaka'*." *Al-matk* and *al-batk* mean cutting. The Arabs interchange the letters *ba'* and *mim*: they say *samada* and *sabada* (for shaving the head), and *aghbatun 'alayhi* and *aghmatuhu*. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿So they shall slit the ears of the cattle﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa' 4:119.]].

*And she gave each one of them a knife*, and *she said to Joseph*: "Come out to them." This is because she had seated him in a place other than the one where they were sitting, so Joseph (peace be upon him) came out to them. 'Ikrimah said: "Joseph's superiority over people in beauty and handsomeness was like the superiority of the full moon on the night of the full moon over the stars of the sky."

It is reported from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken up to the heaven, I passed by Joseph, and I said: 'O Gabriel, who is this?' He said: 'This is Joseph.'" They said: "How did you see him, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Like the moon on the night of the full moon." [114] [[Tarikh Dimashq: 3/484, abridged.]]

It is reported from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Gabriel descended and said: 'O Muhammad, God, exalted is He, says: I clothed the beauty of Joseph with the light of the Throne (*kursi*), and I clothed the light of the beauty of your face with the light of My Throne (*'arsh*).'" [115].

Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated from Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwah, who said: "When Joseph walked through the lanes of Egypt, the radiance of his face was seen on the walls, just as the light of the sun and water is seen on walls."

*So when they saw him, they exalted him*: that is, they magnified him and honored him. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "His affair overwhelmed them, and they were stunned." 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Ali narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, from his father, from his grandfather Ibn 'Abbas, regarding God's words ﴿So when they saw him, they exalted him﴾: "They menstruated (*hadna*) from joy." Then he said:

*We come to women in their states of purity,*
*And we do not come to women when they menstruate with a great menstruation.* [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/269.]]

On this interpretation, *akbarnahu* means *akbarna lahu*, that is, they menstruated on account of him, from his beauty, and they found what women find in such a state. [[See Zad al-Masir: 4/167.]] This is like the saying of 'Antarah:

*Indeed I spend the night hungry, and he shades me,*
*Until I obtain by it the noble feast.* [[Kitab al-'Ayn: 7/466; Lisan al-'Arab: 11/419.]]

That is, "and he shades over it."

Al-Asma'i said: This verse was recited before the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said:

*There is no pre-Islamic poet whom I wished to see, other than [.............]*

[[Illegible word.]] *the verse...*

*And they cut their hands*, meaning they slashed their hands with the knives they had. They thought they were cutting the citron. Qatadah said: "They cut their hands until they let them go." Mujahid said: "They felt nothing but the blood; some of them did not feel any pain but only saw the blood, because their hearts were occupied with Joseph." Wahb said: "It has reached me that nine of the forty women died in that gathering from passion for Joseph."

*And they said: "Ha[sha] lillah!"*: that is, "God forbid!" Abu 'Ubaydah said: "This expression has two meanings: declaring God free from imperfection (*tanzih*), and exception (*istithna'*)." The reciters differed over it. The common reading is *hasha lillah*, with the alif dropped because the expression is used so often on tongues, just as the Arabs dropped the alif in their saying *la-ab li-ghayrika* and *la-ab li-sha'niika*, meaning *la ab* (not a father). Abu 'Ubaydah chose this reading and said: "Following the Book, which is the reading of the great majority. Moreover, I have read it in the Imam, the Mushaf of 'Uthman (peace be upon him): *hasha lillah*, and the other is like it." Abu 'Amr read *hashi lillah*, keeping the *ya'* as in the original form. Ibn Mas'ud read *hasha Allah*, like the poet's saying:

*Hasha Abi Thawban; indeed, in him*
*Is stinginess toward the one who reproaches and insults.* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 14/182.]]

*This is not a human (bashar)*: the accusative here is by removing the preposition, and it is also the predicate of *ma* of negation, as you say: *ma Zayd qa'iman* (Zayd is not standing). Al-A'mash read *ma hadha bashar* with the nominative, which is the dialect of the people of Najd. Al-Farra' recited:

*Hasil claims that he is the branch of his people,*
*But you, O Husayl, are neither branch nor root.* [[In the source: "wayazgham" narrated by Husayl; "wa-ma" and "wa-lam anta."]] [[Zad al-Masir: 7/317.]]

Another recited:

*How different are what I intend and what the sons of my father intend,*
*All together; these two are not equal.*
*They wished for me the death which makes a young man weary,*
*And every young man, and death, will meet.* [[Jami' al-Bayan: 12/274, where "li" is used instead of "ilayya".]]

Al-Farra' narrated from Di'amah ibn Raja' al-Taymi, from Abu al-Huwayrith al-Hanafi, that he read: *ma hadha bashariyy*, and al-Farra' said: "Meaning: a buyer (*bi-mushtari*)."

*This is none but a noble angel (malak karim)* among the angels. Al-Tha'labi said: "I heard Ibn Furak say: they only said of him 'a noble angel' because he opposed his natural inclinations, turned away from this world, its adornments and desires when they displayed them to him, and that is contrary to the nature of humans."

She said (Ra'il to the women): *"That is the one you blamed me for."* That is, for my love of him and my infatuation with him. Then she confessed to them, saying: *"Indeed, I sought to seduce him from himself, but he preserved himself (istasama)."* That is, he refrained and resisted. They said to him: "Obey your mistress." Then she said: *"And if he does not do what I command him,* that is, if he does not comply with me in what I invited him to, *he will surely be imprisoned,* that is, we will jail him, *and he will surely be among the humiliated (al-saghirin)*: that is, the abased."

The emphatic nun (*nun al-tawkid*) is pronounced heavy or light. Pausing on *layusjananna* with the nun is heavy with a shadda. Pausing on *walayakunan* with the alif is light. It resembles the nun of declension in nouns, as in your saying *ra'aytu rajulan* ("I saw a man"), and when you pause you say *rajulan*. Similar to this is God's word ﴿We will surely seize him by the forelock﴾ [[Surah al-'Alaq 96:15.]], and similar to it is pausing on it with an alif, as in the saying of al-A'sha:

*And pray at the time of the evenings and the morning,*
*And do not worship Satan, but worship God.* [[Jami' al-Bayan: 12/275; Lisan al-'Arab: 2/473, where "sabbih" is used instead of "salli".]]

That is, he intended *fa-'budan* (worship), and when he paused on it, the pause was with an alif.

Joseph chose, when the woman repeatedly sought him and threatened him, the prison over disobedience. *He said: "My Lord!"*: that is, O my Lord, a vocative with a possessive pronoun. *The prison (sijn)*: the place of detention. The common reading is with a kasra on the *sin*, as a noun. Ya'qub read it with a damma on the *sin*, as a verbal noun, meaning confinement. *It is dearer to me than what they invite me to.* Then he knew that he could not be preserved except by God's preservation, so he said: *"And unless You turn their scheme away from me, I shall incline toward them (asbu) and be one of the ignorant."* I would lean toward them and yield to them. One says: "So-and-so inclined (*sabā*) to such-and-such," *sabā yasbū, sabwan wa-sabwatan*, when he leaned and longed for it. Yazid ibn Dabbah said:

*To Hind my heart inclined,*
*And Hind, like her, is seductive.* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 14/450.]]

*So his Lord responded to him, and turned away from him their scheme. Indeed He is the All-Hearing of his supplication and his complaint, the All-Knowing of their deceit.*

*Then it appeared to them*: that is, to the 'Aziz and his associates, *in judgment, after they had seen the signs* indicating Joseph's innocence, which were the tearing of the shirt from behind, the scratching of the face, and the cutting of the women's hands, *that they should imprison him for a while.* Al-Farra' said: "This *lam* is the *lam* of oath, and it occurs with every verb in the future tense used in speech, as in God's words ﴿And they certainly knew that whoever bought it﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah 2:102.]] and ﴿and they thought they would have no escape﴾ [[Surah Fussilat 41:48.]]. The *lam* and *ma* entered both of them, because they carry the meaning of speech and oath."

*For a time (hatta hin)*: that is, until the time when they would see their opinion.

'Ikrimah said: "Nine years." Al-Kalbi said: "Five years." *Hatta* here means *ila*, as in God's words ﴿until the rising of dawn﴾ [[Surah al-Qadr 97:5.]]. Al-Suddi said: "That is because the woman said to her husband: 'This Hebrew slave has disgraced me among the people. He is making excuses to them and informing them that I sought to seduce him from himself. I cannot bring myself to excuse myself with my excuse, so either you permit me to go out and make my excuse, or you imprison him as you imprisoned me.'" So he imprisoned him after he knew of his innocence. It is mentioned that God, exalted is He, made that imprisonment a purification for Joseph from his intent toward the woman, and an expiation for his slip.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Joseph stumbled three times: when he intended her and was imprisoned; when he said *'Mention me to your lord'* ... *so Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his Lord*, and he remained in prison for several years; and when he said to them *'Indeed you are thieves'*, and they said *'If he steals, a brother of his stole before him.'*"

And women in the city said: that is, the news of Joseph and the woman spread in the city of Egypt, and the women talked about it. They said, meaning the wife of the cupbearer, the wife of the baker, the wife of the prison keeper, and the wife of the chamberlain. Muqatil said: "The wife of al-'Aziz." In the language of the Arabs, *al-'Aziz* means the king. Abu Dawud said:

*A pearl that a merchant dove for,*
*Was displayed before the 'Aziz on a day of drizzle.* [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 12/259.]]

That is, "which king."

She seeks to seduce her young man, the Canaanite, away from himself.

Then she said: *"And if he does not do what I command him,* that is, if he does not comply with me in what I invited him to, *he will surely be imprisoned,* that is, we will jail him, *and he will surely be among the humiliated (al-saghirin)*: that is, the abased."

The emphatic nun (*nun al-tawkid*) is pronounced heavy or light. Pausing on *layusjananna* with the nun is heavy with a shadda. Pausing on *walayakunan* with the alif is light. It resembles the nun of declension in nouns, as in your saying *ra'aytu rajulan* ("I saw a man"), and when you pause you say *rajulan*. Similar to this is God's word ﴿We will surely seize him by the forelock﴾ [[Surah al-'Alaq 96:15.]], and similar to it is pausing on it with an alif, as in the saying of al-A'sha:

*And pray at the time of the evenings and the morning,*
*And do not worship Satan, but worship God.* [[Jami' al-Bayan: 12/275; Lisan al-'Arab: 2/473, where "sabbih" is used instead of "salli".]]

That is, he intended *fa-'budan* (worship), and when he paused on it, the pause was with an alif.

Joseph chose, when the woman repeatedly sought him and threatened him, the prison over disobedience. *He said: "My Lord!"*: that is, O my Lord, a vocative with a possessive pronoun. *The prison (sijn)*: the place of detention. The common reading is with a kasra on the *sin*, as a noun. Ya'qub read it with a damma on the *sin*, as a verbal noun, meaning confinement. *It is dearer to me than what they invite me to.* Then he knew that he could not be preserved except by God's preservation, so he said: *"And unless You turn their scheme away from me, I shall incline toward them (asbu) and be one of the ignorant."* I would lean toward them and yield to them. One says: "So-and-so inclined (*sabā*) to such-and-such," *sabā yasbū, sabwan wa-sabwatan*, when he leaned and longed for it. Yazid ibn Dabbah said:

*To Hind my heart inclined,*
*And Hind, like her, is seductive.* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 14/450.]]

*So his Lord responded to him, and turned away from him their scheme. Indeed He is the All-Hearing of his supplication and his complaint, the All-Knowing of their deceit.*

*Then it appeared to them*: that is, to the 'Aziz and his associates, *in judgment, after they had seen the signs* indicating Joseph's innocence, which were the tearing of the shirt from behind, the scratching of the face, and the cutting of the women's hands, *that they should imprison him for a while.* Al-Farra' said: "This *lam* is the *lam* of oath, and it occurs with every verb in the future tense used in speech, as in God's words ﴿And they certainly knew that whoever bought it﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah 2:102.]] and ﴿and they thought they would have no escape﴾ [[Surah Fussilat 41:48.]]. The *lam* and *ma* entered both of them, because they carry the meaning of speech and oath."

*For a time (hatta hin)*: that is, until the time when they would see their opinion.

'Ikrimah said: "Nine years." Al-Kalbi said: "Five years." *Hatta* here means *ila*, as in God's words ﴿until the rising of dawn﴾ [[Surah al-Qadr 97:5.]]. Al-Suddi said: "That is because the woman said to her husband: 'This Hebrew slave has disgraced me among the people. He is making excuses to them and informing them that I sought to seduce him from himself. I cannot bring myself to excuse myself with my excuse, so either you permit me to go out and make my excuse, or you imprison him as you imprisoned me.'" So he imprisoned him after he knew of his innocence. It is mentioned that God, exalted is He, made that imprisonment a purification for Joseph from his intent toward the woman, and an expiation for his slip.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Joseph stumbled three times: when he intended her and was imprisoned; when he said *'Mention me to your lord'* ... *so Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his Lord*, and he remained in prison for several years; and when he said to them *'Indeed you are thieves'*, and they said *'If he steals, a brother of his stole before him.'*"

And women in the city said: that is, the news of Joseph and the woman spread in the city of Egypt, and the women talked about it. They said, meaning the wife of the cupbearer, the wife of the baker, the wife of the prison keeper, and the wife of the chamberlain. Muqatil said: "The wife of al-'Aziz." In the language of the Arabs, *al-'Aziz* means the king. Abu Dawud said:

*A pearl that a merchant dove for,*
*Was displayed before the 'Aziz on a day of drizzle.* [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 12/259.]]

That is, "which king."

She seeks to seduce her young man, the Canaanite, away from himself.

*Has smitten her with love*: that is, she loved him so intensely that his love entered the *shaghaf* of her heart. The *shaghaf* is its covering and sheath. Al-Suddi said: "The *shaghaf* is a thin membrane over the heart, called the 'tongue of the heart.' One says: love penetrated the skin until it reached the heart." Al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani said:

*And a concern has come between me and that, entering*
*Like the entering of the shaghaf, which the fingers seek.* [[Kitab al-'Ayn: 4/360; Lisan al-'Arab: 9/179, where "wali[j]" is used instead of "dakhil" and "makan" instead of "dukhul".]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: "He hung her with love (*'allaqaha*)." Al-Hasan said: "He entered her inner part with love (*batnaha*)." Qatadah said: "He penetrated her interior with her love for him (*istabṭanaha*)." Abu Raja' said: "He made her sincere in love (*sadaqaha*)." Al-Kalbi said: "His love veiled her heart so that she could understand nothing other than him."

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, al-Sha'bi and al-A'raj read *sha'afaha*, with an unpointed 'ayn (*ayn* without a dot). Scholars differ on its meaning. Al-Farra' said: "He took her in every direction," from *sha'af al-jibal*, meaning the peaks of mountains. Al-Nakha'i and al-Dahhak said: "He enticed her and carried her away." Its root is from *sha'af al-dabbah*, when a beast rolls in the dirt in fright. Imru' al-Qais said:

*Will you kill me, when she has been smitten through her heart,*
*As the mange-stricken camel is smitten by the tar-smeared herdsman?* [[Jami' al-Bayan: 12/262; Lisan al-'Arab: 9/177, where "li-taqtulani" is used instead of "ataqtulani".]]

His meaning is: her heart went as the tar-smeared herdsman goes among the camels, who fear him and then find relief from him. Al-Akhfash said: "From her love for him." Muhammad ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: "Love encompassed her."

*Indeed, we see her in clear error*: that is, in manifest error. When she (Ra'il) heard *of their scheming*, that is, of their words and talk, Qatadah and al-Suddi said... Ibn Ishaq said: "They only said that as a scheme against her, so that they could see Joseph, for she had described to them his beauty and handsomeness." *She sent for them*. Wahb said: "She prepared a banquet and invited forty women, among them those who had reproached her." *And prepared for them*: she prepared (*a'tadat*, from the root of *i'tad*), which means provision and preparation. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire﴾ [[Surah al-Kahf 18:29.]].

*A cushion for them*: a place for food and the cushions and pillows they lean on. It is said: "He threw for him a *muttaka'*," meaning something to lean upon. This is the meaning of Ibn 'Abbas's statement in the narration of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Ishaq and Ibn Zayd said: "Food." Al-Qutabi said: "The origin of this is that when you invite someone to a meal at your place, you prepare a cushion or a *muttaka'* for him, so the food was called *muttaka'* by metaphor. One says: 'We reclined (*ittaka'na*) at so-and-so's place,' meaning we ate." 'Adi ibn Zayd said:

*So we lived in blessing and reclined (to eat),*
*And drank the lawful from its jugs.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/178.]]

It is reported from al-Hasan that he said: "*Muttaka'*" with a shadda and a long vowel is not eloquent. From al-Hasan also: "I do not think that is sound." Mujahid read *muttaka'*, light and unhamzated, and this is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas.

They differed over its meaning. Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the citron (*utrunj*)." 'Ikrimah said: "It is food." Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, said: "It is the *zamawards* (a kind of fruit or food)." 'Ali ibn al-Hakam and 'Ubayd ibn Hakim, from him, said: "Everything that is cut with a knife is, in the language of the Arabs, *muttaka'*." *Al-matk* and *al-batk* mean cutting. The Arabs interchange the letters *ba'* and *mim*: they say *samada* and *sabada* (for shaving the head), and *aghbatun 'alayhi* and *aghmatuhu*. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿So they shall slit the ears of the cattle﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa' 4:119.]].

*And she gave each one of them a knife*, and *she said to Joseph*: "Come out to them." This is because she had seated him in a place other than the one where they were sitting, so Joseph (peace be upon him) came out to them. 'Ikrimah said: "Joseph's superiority over people in beauty and handsomeness was like the superiority of the full moon on the night of the full moon over the stars of the sky."

It is reported from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken up to the heaven, I passed by Joseph, and I said: 'O Gabriel, who is this?' He said: 'This is Joseph.'" They said: "How did you see him, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Like the moon on the night of the full moon." [114] [[Tarikh Dimashq: 3/484, abridged.]]

It is reported from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Gabriel descended and said: 'O Muhammad, God, exalted is He, says: I clothed the beauty of Joseph with the light of the Throne (*kursi*), and I clothed the light of the beauty of your face with the light of My Throne (*'arsh*).'" [115].

Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated from Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwah, who said: "When Joseph walked through the lanes of Egypt, the radiance of his face was seen on the walls, just as the light of the sun and water is seen on walls."

*So when they saw him, they exalted him*: that is, they magnified him and honored him. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "His affair overwhelmed them, and they were stunned." 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Ali narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, from his father, from his grandfather Ibn 'Abbas, regarding God's words ﴿So when they saw him, they exalted him﴾: "They menstruated (*hadna*) from joy." Then he said:

*We come to women in their states of purity,*
*And we do not come to women when they menstruate with a great menstruation.* [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/269.]]

On this interpretation, *akbarnahu* means *akbarna lahu*, that is, they menstruated on account of him, from his beauty, and they found what women find in such a state. [[See Zad al-Masir: 4/167.]] This is like the saying of 'Antarah:

*Indeed I spend the night hungry, and he shades me,*
*Until I obtain by it the noble feast.* [[Kitab al-'Ayn: 7/466; Lisan al-'Arab: 11/419.]]

That is, "and he shades over it."

Al-Asma'i said: This verse was recited before the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said:

*There is no pre-Islamic poet whom I wished to see, other than [.............]*

[[Illegible word.]] *the verse...*

*And they cut their hands*, meaning they slashed their hands with the knives they had. They thought they were cutting the citron. Qatadah said: "They cut their hands until they let them go." Mujahid said: "They felt nothing but the blood; some of them did not feel any pain but only saw the blood, because their hearts were occupied with Joseph." Wahb said: "It has reached me that nine of the forty women died in that gathering from passion for Joseph."

*And they said: "Ha[sha] lillah!"*: that is, "God forbid!" Abu 'Ubaydah said: "This expression has two meanings: declaring God free from imperfection (*tanzih*), and exception (*istithna'*)." The reciters differed over it. The common reading is *hasha lillah*, with the alif dropped because the expression is used so often on tongues, just as the Arabs dropped the alif in their saying *la-ab li-ghayrika* and *la-ab li-sha'niika*, meaning *la ab* (not a father). Abu 'Ubaydah chose this reading and said: "Following the Book, which is the reading of the great majority. Moreover, I have read it in the Imam, the Mushaf of 'Uthman (peace be upon him): *hasha lillah*, and the other is like it." Abu 'Amr read *hashi lillah*, keeping the *ya'* as in the original form. Ibn Mas'ud read *hasha Allah*, like the poet's saying:

*Hasha Abi Thawban; indeed, in him*
*Is stinginess toward the one who reproaches and insults.* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 14/182.]]

*This is not a human (bashar)*: the accusative here is by removing the preposition, and it is also the predicate of *ma* of negation, as you say: *ma Zayd qa'iman* (Zayd is not standing). Al-A'mash read *ma hadha bashar* with the nominative, which is the dialect of the people of Najd. Al-Farra' recited:

*Hasil claims that he is the branch of his people,*
*But you, O Husayl, are neither branch nor root.* [[In the source: "wayazgham" narrated by Husayl; "wa-ma" and "wa-lam anta."]] [[Zad al-Masir: 7/317.]]

Another recited:

*How different are what I intend and what the sons of my father intend,*
*All together; these two are not equal.*
*They wished for me the death which makes a young man weary,*
*And every young man, and death, will meet.* [[Jami' al-Bayan: 12/274, where "li" is used instead of "ilayya".]]

Al-Farra' narrated from Di'amah ibn Raja' al-Taymi, from Abu al-Huwayrith al-Hanafi, that he read: *ma hadha bashariyy*, and al-Farra' said: "Meaning: a buyer (*bi-mushtari*)."

*This is none but a noble angel (malak karim)* among the angels. Al-Tha'labi said: "I heard Ibn Furak say: they only said of him 'a noble angel' because he opposed his natural inclinations, turned away from this world, its adornments and desires when they displayed them to him, and that is contrary to the nature of humans."

She said (Ra'il to the women): *"That is the one you blamed me for."* That is, for my love of him and my infatuation with him. Then she confessed to them, saying: *"Indeed, I sought to seduce him from himself, but he preserved himself (istasama)."* That is, he refrained and resisted. They said to him: "Obey your mistress." Then she said: *"And if he does not do what I command him,* that is, if he does not comply with me in what I invited him to, *he will surely be imprisoned,* that is, we will jail him, *and he will surely be among the humiliated (al-saghirin)*: that is, the abased."

*And pray at the time of the evenings and the morning,*
*And do not worship Satan, but worship God.* [[Jami' al-Bayan: 12/275; Lisan al-'Arab: 2/473, where "sabbih" is used instead of "salli".]]

That is, he intended *fa-'budan* (worship), and when he paused on it, the pause was with an alif.
