Qatadah explained "thought" as the sense of supposition that is the opposite of certainty, and said: The interpretation of dreams is only by supposition, and Allah creates whatever He wills. The first view is more correct and more fitting to the condition of the prophets. ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾, your master, meaning the king. It was said to him that in the prison there was a young man imprisoned unjustly. ﴿But Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his lord﴾, meaning Satan caused Yusuf to forget the remembrance of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, until he sought relief from someone else and sought help from a created being. That was a heedlessness that befell Yusuf from Satan. For this reason he forgot his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, who, had he appealed to Him, would have quickly brought his release. But he was heedless, and his imprisonment was prolonged because of it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The pronoun in His saying ﴿Satan caused him to forget﴾ refers to the cupbearer. So we say: Satan caused the cupbearer to forget the mention of Yusuf to the king. According to this view, the meaning of the verse is: "Satan caused him to forget his remembrance of his lord," like His saying: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies﴾, meaning he frightens you with his allies.

﴿He remained﴾, stayed, ﴿in the prison a few years.﴾ The scholars differed about the meaning of "few" (bidʿ). Abu ʿUbaydah said it is between three and five. Mujahid said: between three and nine. Al-Asmaʿi said: between three and nine. Ibn ʿAbbas said: fewer than ten. Al-Farraʾ claimed that "bidʿ" is only mentioned with ten and with twenty up to ninety, and that it is more than three up to nine. He said: "So I have seen the Arabs use it, and they do not say bidʿ and a hundred, nor bidʿ and a thousand." When the noun is masculine it is said bidʿah. Most exegetes hold that "bidʿ" in this verse means seven years. Wahb said: Job (peace be upon him) suffered affliction for seven years, Yusuf was left in the prison for seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar was punished and transformed among the beasts for seven years.

Yunus narrated from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on Yusuf. Had it not been for his statement, he would not have remained in the prison as long as he did." He meant His saying: "Mention me to your lord." He said: Then al-Hasan wept and said: "When a matter befalls us, we turn to people."

Malik ibn Dinar said: When Yusuf said to the cupbearer, "Mention me to your lord," it was said to him: "O Yusuf, you have taken other than Me as a guardian. I will surely prolong your imprisonment." Yusuf wept and said: "O my Lord, the abundance of hunger troubled me, so I spoke a word. Woe to my brothers."

It is related that Jibril (Gabriel) came to Yusuf (peace be upon them both). When Yusuf saw him, he recognized him and said: "O brother of those who warn, why do I see you among the sinners?" Then Jibril said to him: "O pure one among the pure, the Lord of the worlds sends you greetings and says: What is wrong with you? Were you not ashamed before Me when you sought help from human beings? By My might, I will surely keep you in the prison a few years." Yusuf said: "And He is pleased with me in that?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then I do not mind."

Kaʿb said: Jibril said to Yusuf: "Indeed Allah, may He be exalted, says: Who created you? He said: Allah. He said: Then who made you beloved to your father? He said: Allah. He said: Then who was your companion in the well when you entered it naked? He said: Allah. He said: Then who rescued you from the distress of the well? He said: Allah. He said: Then who taught you the interpretation of dreams? He said: Allah. He said: Then how did you seek intercession from a human being like yourself?"

When the seven years had passed, al-Kalbi said, and these seven were in addition to the five that had been before that, and when the relief of Yusuf drew near, the great king of Egypt saw a strange and terrifying dream. He saw: ﴿Indeed I see seven fat cows coming out of a dry river, and seven lean cows,﴾ that is, emaciated ones, and the lean ones swallowed the fat ones. They devoured them until they reached them, and he saw nothing of them. And he saw ﴿seven green ears of grain whose grain had formed, and seven others dry, withered, and the dry ones entwined around the green until they overcame them.﴾ He gathered the magicians, soothsayers, diviners, and physiognomists, and related it to them, and said: ﴿O assembly,﴾ that is, the nobles, ﴿explain to me my vision, if you are able to interpret visions, you interpret.﴾ The word "ruʾyā" means dream, and its plural is ruʾā.

They said: ﴿They are confused dreams,﴾ that is, muddled and ambiguous dreams, false fancies. Its singular is ḍighth, and its root is a bundle of crops or grass. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle (ḍighth)﴾. Ibn Muqbil said:

"A tender woman, as if the scents of her bed were scattered bundles of basil brought by the north wind in the morning."

And another said:

"In the protected grazing land of Dhimar, when its defender was scarce, a hungry one, like a bundle of dry herbs in the belly, was confined."

"Aḥlām" is the plural of ḥulm, which is ruʾyā. The verb from it is ḥalimtu and aḥlamu, with a fatḥah on the ʿayn in the past tense. And ḥalimtuhā in the future, and ḥulman, and it becomes "ḥāliman" with the yāʾ dropped.

﴿We are not versed in the interpretation of dreams.﴾

﴿And the one who was saved from the two of them, the cupbearer, said, and he remembered after a time,﴾ that is, and he recalled Yusuf's need, his saying: "Mention me to your lord." ﴿After a period.﴾ That is, after a time. Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, and al-Dahhak recited "baʿda ummah," meaning after forgetting. It is said: "ummah," "yaʾmah," "ummah," if he forgot. And a man who is "mā huwa" is one whose intellect has gone.

Abu ʿUbaydah recited:

"I forgot, though I used to not forget a narration; thus time destroys intellects."

Mujahid recited "amh," with a sukūn on the mīm and a fatḥah on the alif and a clear hāʾ, and it is also a form like "al-umh," and they are two dialects, meaning forgetfulness. ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation,﴾ that is, I will tell you its explanation and what you are looking at. ﴿So send me.﴾ That is, release me, let me go, and permit me to proceed and come to you with its interpretation. The verse contains an ellipsis; its implied sense is "so send me," and he came to the prison. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The prison was not in the city. He said: ﴿Yusuf, O Yusuf,﴾ that is, "O Yusuf," ﴿O truthful one,﴾ regarding what you explained to us of the dream. "Ṣiddīq" means one who is very truthful. That is why Abu Bakr was called "al-Ṣiddīq." The form faʿīl is for intensity and abundance, like fasīq, ḍalīl, sharīb, khamīr, and similar words.

﴿Explain to us regarding seven fat cows﴾, the verse, for the king saw this dream.

I wish to return to the people, the people of Egypt, so that they may know its interpretation. It was also said: "so that they may know your merit and your knowledge." Then Yusuf, as a teacher and interpreter, said to them: "As for the seven fat cows and the seven green ears of grain, they are seven years of abundance; and the lean cows and the dry ears are the years of hardship, the barren and famine-stricken years." This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You shall sow for seven years in your usual manner﴾. That is, as is your custom. Some said it means with diligence and effort. Some of them read "daaban" with a fatha on the hamza, and both are dialectal forms (lughatan). It is said: "dabbat fi al-amr, adbu dabban and daban" when one exerts effort in a matter. Al-Farra' said: "Likewise, for every word whose first letter is vocalized with a fatha and whose second letter is sukun, its heavy form is permissible when its second letter is a hamza, an 'ayn, a ha', a kha', or a ha'."

﴿So whatever you harvest, leave it in its ear, except for a little that you eat﴾. He advised them to do this only so that it would remain and not spoil. ﴿Then after that will come seven hard years﴾, meaning seven years of drought and famine, ﴿which will consume what you have stored up for them﴾, meaning it will be eaten; what you prepared for them of food in the years of plenty will be consumed in them. This is like the saying of the poet:
"Your day, O deceived one, is heedlessness and negligence,
and your night is sleep, and death is bound to you."
[Al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: 9/231.]
Yet the day does not grow heedless and the night does not sleep; rather, one is heedless during the day and sleeps at night. ﴿Except for a little that you store up﴾, that is, that you keep in reserve and hoard.

﴿Then after that will come a year﴾. This is a report from Yusuf (peace be upon him) about what was not in the king's dream, but it is from the knowledge of the unseen that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave him. As Qatadah said: "Allah increased him in knowledge of a year they had not asked him about, so he said: ﴿Then after that will come a year﴾ ﴿in which the people will be given rain﴾, meaning they will be rained upon with the rain of showers. It was also said: "they will be relieved (yughathun)," from the Arab usage "istaghathtu bi-fulan wa aghathani" (I sought help from so-and-so and he helped me). ﴿And in it they will press (ya'sirun)﴾. The people of Kufa except 'Asim read "ta'sirun" with a ta', because the whole discourse is in the second person, while the rest read it with a ya', returning it to "the people." Most exegetes said: "they will press grapes into wine, olives into oil, and sesame into oil," and what is meant by the grapes, fruits, and grains is abundance of blessings and good. Al-Faraj ibn Fudalah related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "ta'sirun means ta'lubun (you will milk)." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "they will be saved (yanjuna) from drought and distress; and al-'asr means the refuge and the shelter." Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i said:
"Thirsty, seeking help and not being helped,
though he had been a refuge for the one who was saved."
[Al-Sihah: 2/749.]

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari, Abu 'Ali ibn Habash the reciter, and Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl the reciter informed me, saying: Abu Zur'ah related to me, Hafs ibn 'Umar related to me, Abu Jamilah related to me, from 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd who said: I heard 'Isa ibn al-A'raj recite it as "fihi yughathu al-nas wa fihi ya'sarun" with a damma on the ya', and he said: I said: "What is ya'sarun?" He said: "The rain," meaning they will be rained upon. And he recited: ﴿And We sent down from the pressing clouds water pouring forth﴾ [Surah al-Naba': 14].

And two young men entered the prison with him. They were two servants of the great king, al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan. One was his baker, the keeper of his food, named Mujlith. The other was his cupbearer, the keeper of his drink, named Bunw. The king had become angry with them and imprisoned them. The reason was that he had learned that his baker intended to poison him and that his cupbearer had agreed to this. The cause was that a group of people from Egypt wanted to scheme against the king and assassinate him. They approached these two men and promised them money in return for poisoning the king's food and drink. They agreed to this. Then the cupbearer backed out, but the baker accepted the bribe and poisoned the food.

When the time came and the food was brought, the cupbearer said: "O king, do not eat, for the food is poisoned." The baker said: "Do not drink, O king, for the drink is poisoned." The king said to the cupbearer: "Drink." He drank and it did him no harm. He said to the baker: "Eat from your food." He refused. So they tested that food on one of the animals, and it ate it and died. The king ordered them imprisoned.

When Yusuf (peace be upon him) entered the prison, he said to his companions: "I interpret dreams." One of the two young men said to his companion: "Come, let us test this Hebrew servant." They approached him and asked him, though neither of them had actually seen anything. ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: "The two companions of Yusuf did not see anything. They had only agreed together to test his knowledge."

ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever claims to have seen in a dream what he has not seen will be commanded on the Day of Resurrection to tie together two barley grains, and whoever listens to the conversation of a people who dislike him, molten lead will be poured into his ears."

Others said: "The two had seen real dreams, true in substance." Mujahid said: When the two young men saw Yusuf, they said to him: "By Allah, we loved you the moment we saw you." Yusuf said to them: "I implore you by Allah not to love me, for no one has ever loved me without a trial coming upon me because of his love.

My paternal aunt loved me, and a trial came upon me because of her love. Then my father loved me, and a trial came upon me because of his love. Then the wife of this king loved me, and a trial came upon me because of her love for me. So do not love me, may Allah bless you both." He said: They refused anything but to love him and to be close to him wherever he was. They were pleased by what they saw of his understanding and intellect. When the two had entered the prison, they had seen dreams. So they came to Yusuf, and the cupbearer said to him: "O scholar, I saw myself pressing wine from a grape vine on which there were three clusters of grapes, and the king's cup was in my hand, so I squeezed them into it and gave the king to drink, and he drank it."

The baker said: "I saw that on my head there were three baskets containing bread and various kinds of food, and birds of prey were pecking at it." That is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿One of them said, "Indeed I saw myself pressing wine."﴾ That is, the cupbearer, "Indeed I saw myself," meaning, I saw myself, "pressing wine," meaning grapes, in the dialect of ʿUmān. The recitation of Ibn Masʿud supports this: "pressing grapes" (aʿṣiru ʿinaban).

Al-Asmaʿi said: Al-Muʿtamir informed me that he met a Bedouin who had grapes with him. He said: "What do you have with you?" He said: "Wine." From this, vinegar made from grapes is called "wine vinegar" (khall khamra). This is by way of nearness of meaning. Al-Qutaybi said: It may also be wine itself, as one says, "I pressed oil," while he only pressed olives.

The other, namely Mujlith, said: ﴿Indeed I see myself carrying bread upon my head, and birds are eating from it. Inform us of its interpretation.﴾ That is, inform us of its explanation, its meaning, and what the outcome of this dream will be.

﴿Indeed we see you to be among the good-doers.﴾ That is, among the scholars who do good. Al-Farraʾ said, and Ibn Ishaq said: ﴿Indeed we see you to be among the good-doers﴾ toward us, if you do that and explain our dreams, just as one says, "Do such-and-such, you are a good-doer."

Salamah ibn Nabt narrated from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed we see you to be among the good-doers﴾: What was his goodness? He said: When a man fell ill in the prison, he would go to him. When someone was in distress, he would make room for him. If someone was in need, he would gather for him and ask on his behalf.

Qatadah said: We have been told that his goodness was that he would treat their sick, console their grieving, and strive in worship of his Lord.

It is also said: When Yusuf reached the prison, he found people whose hope had been cut off, whose trials had grown severe, and whose sorrow had lengthened. So he began to say: "Be glad and be patient, you will be rewarded. Indeed there is reward and recompense in this." They said to him: "O young man, may Allah bless you. How beautiful your face is, how beautiful your character is, and how beautiful your speech is! We have been blessed by your presence in the prison. Since we were imprisoned, we have been in something other than this, because of what you tell us of reward, expiation, and purification. Who are you, young man?"

He said: "I am Yusuf, son of Yaʿqub, the chosen of Allah, son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah." The jailer said to him: "O young man, by Allah, if I could, I would release you. But how good your company is and how good your reports are! Stay in whichever section of the prison you wish."

Yusuf (peace be upon him) disliked to interpret for them what they had asked him, because he knew that it would bring harm upon one of them. So he turned away from their question and moved on to something else. He said to them: ﴿No food will come to you that you are provided with in your sleep except that I will inform you of its interpretation while you are awake.﴾

This is the statement of most of the exegetes. Some of them said: He meant by it while awake. He said: ﴿No food will come to you that you are provided with﴾ that you will eat and consume, ﴿except that I will inform you of its interpretation﴾, of its explanation. He said: Whatever food you have eaten, when you ate it, and how much you ate. They said to him: "This is the work of fortune-tellers and soothsayers." He (peace be upon him) said to them: ﴿I am not a soothsayer. That is of what my Lord has taught me. Indeed I have abandoned the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.﴾ He repeated them for emphasis. It is also said: The first "they" is a substitute for a repeated, dropped element, as in His saying: ﴿Does he promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?﴾ So the first is dropped and the second is a new beginning, and "disbelievers" is its predicate.

﴿And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Yaʿqub. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah.﴾ Some people pronounced his yāʾ with a fatḥah, and others with a sukūn. [For such forms (as in the words) "wafā" and similar, the jazm (sukūn) is the original form, and the fatḥah is to match the alif, which it finds heavy, since it is its sister vowel.] Al-Aʿmash recited "ābāy Ibrāhīm" and "duʿāy illā firāran," with a short final vowel, not hamzated, and with the yāʾ of both pronounced with a fatḥah like [ ... ].

﴿Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Yaʿqub. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah.﴾ "Anything" is an object-like element; its sense is: that we associate with Allah anything.

﴿That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind﴾, that is, the tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) and knowledge. ﴿But most of mankind do not give thanks.﴾ Then Yusuf showed them his intelligence and knowledge, and then called them to Islam. He turned to them and to the people of the prison. Before them were idols that they worshipped. So he said, to press the argument: ﴿O two companions of the prison﴾. He called them the two companions of the prison because they were in it, like His saying to the inhabitants of Paradise: ﴿Companions of Paradise﴾ and to the inhabitants of the Fire: ﴿Companions of the Fire.﴾

﴿Are many lords dispersed better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ That is, many gods, various ones, who neither benefit nor harm. ﴿The One﴾ who has no partner. ﴿The Subduer﴾ who has subdued everything. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ Then he clarified the stone idols and their weakness, and said: ﴿What you worship besides Him﴾, that is, besides Allah. He said ﴿what you worship﴾ though he had begun speaking to two persons, because he meant by it all who were in the same state as them of association. ﴿Only names that you have named﴾, that is, their naming of their idols as gods and lords without that naming being true. ﴿You and your fathers have named them; Allah has not sent down any authority for them﴾, meaning proof and evidence. ﴿Judgment belongs only to Allah﴾, meaning the decision, command, and prohibition. ﴿He has commanded that you not worship except Him﴾. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion.﴾ ﴿That is the upright religion﴾, that is, what I have called you to, of tawhid and abandoning association. ﴿But most of mankind do not know.﴾

Then he explained their dreams, saying: ﴿O two companions of the prison. As for one of you, he will give his lord, his master, meaning the king, wine to drink.﴾ As for the three clusters he saw, they are three days; he will remain in the prison, then the king will release him and he will be restored to what he was. ﴿As for the other, he will be crucified.﴾ As for the three baskets he saw, they are three days; he will remain in the prison, then the king will bring him out [on] the fourth day and crucify him. ﴿And birds will eat from his head.﴾

Ibn Masʿud said: When they heard the words of Yusuf, they said: "We saw nothing; we were only playing." Yusuf (peace be upon him) said: ﴿The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire,﴾ that is, the matter about which you ask has been finished, and Allah's judgment has become binding upon you both according to what I told you.

Muʿallā ibn ʿAtaʾ narrated from Wakiʿ ibn ʿAdas, from his paternal uncle Abu Razin al-Uqayli, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Indeed a dream hangs over a man as a bird does, as long as it is not interpreted. When it is interpreted, it comes to pass. Indeed a dream is one part of forty-six parts of prophethood." I think he said: "Do not relate it except to one who has understanding."

And ʿAbdullah ibn Hamid informed us, from Ismaʿil ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn ʿAffan, from Ibn Numayr, from al-Aʿmash, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A dream follows the first interpreter."

And Yusuf said at that time, to the one who thought, meaning knew, that he would be saved from the two of them, namely the cupbearer. This is the statement of most of the exegetes. Qatadah explained "thought" as the sense of supposition that is the opposite of certainty, and said: The interpretation of dreams is only by supposition, and Allah creates whatever He wills. The first view is more correct and more fitting to the condition of the prophets. ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾, your master, meaning the king. It was said to him that in the prison there was a young man imprisoned unjustly. ﴿But Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his lord﴾, meaning Satan caused Yusuf to forget the remembrance of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, until he sought relief from someone else and sought help from a created being. That was a heedlessness that befell Yusuf from Satan. For this reason he forgot his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, who, had he appealed to Him, would have quickly brought his release. But he was heedless, and his imprisonment was prolonged because of it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The pronoun in His saying ﴿Satan caused him to forget﴾ refers to the cupbearer. So we say: Satan caused the cupbearer to forget the mention of Yusuf to the king. According to this view, the meaning of the verse is: "Satan caused him to forget his remembrance of his lord," like His saying: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies﴾, meaning he frightens you with his allies.

﴿He remained﴾, stayed, ﴿in the prison a few years.﴾ The scholars differed about the meaning of "few" (bidʿ). Abu ʿUbaydah said it is between three and five. Mujahid said: between three and nine. Al-Asmaʿi said: between three and nine. Ibn ʿAbbas said: fewer than ten. Al-Farraʾ claimed that "bidʿ" is only mentioned with ten and with twenty up to ninety, and that it is more than three up to nine. He said: "So I have seen the Arabs use it, and they do not say bidʿ and a hundred, nor bidʿ and a thousand." When the noun is masculine it is said bidʿah. Most exegetes hold that "bidʿ" in this verse means seven years. Wahb said: Job (peace be upon him) suffered affliction for seven years, Yusuf was left in the prison for seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar was punished and transformed among the beasts for seven years.

Yunus narrated from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on Yusuf. Had it not been for his statement, he would not have remained in the prison as long as he did." He meant His saying: "Mention me to your lord." He said: Then al-Hasan wept and said: "When a matter befalls us, we turn to people."

Malik ibn Dinar said: When Yusuf said to the cupbearer, "Mention me to your lord," it was said to him: "O Yusuf, you have taken other than Me as a guardian. I will surely prolong your imprisonment." Yusuf wept and said: "O my Lord, the abundance of hunger troubled me, so I spoke a word. Woe to my brothers."

It is related that Jibril (Gabriel) came to Yusuf (peace be upon them both). When Yusuf saw him, he recognized him and said: "O brother of those who warn, why do I see you among the sinners?" Then Jibril said to him: "O pure one among the pure, the Lord of the worlds sends you greetings and says: What is wrong with you? Were you not ashamed before Me when you sought help from human beings? By My might, I will surely keep you in the prison a few years." Yusuf said: "And He is pleased with me in that?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then I do not mind."

Kaʿb said: Jibril said to Yusuf: "Indeed Allah, may He be exalted, says: Who created you? He said: Allah. He said: Then who made you beloved to your father? He said: Allah. He said: Then who was your companion in the well when you entered it naked? He said: Allah. He said: Then who rescued you from the distress of the well? He said: Allah. He said: Then who taught you the interpretation of dreams? He said: Allah. He said: Then how did you seek intercession from a human being like yourself?"

When the seven years had passed, al-Kalbi said, and these seven were in addition to the five that had been before that, and when the relief of Yusuf drew near, the great king of Egypt saw a strange and terrifying dream. He saw: ﴿Indeed I see seven fat cows coming out of a dry river, and seven lean cows,﴾ that is, emaciated ones, and the lean ones swallowed the fat ones. They devoured them until they reached them, and he saw nothing of them. And he saw ﴿seven green ears of grain whose grain had formed, and seven others dry, withered, and the dry ones entwined around the green until they overcame them.﴾ He gathered the magicians, soothsayers, diviners, and physiognomists, and related it to them, and said: ﴿O assembly,﴾ that is, the nobles, ﴿explain to me my vision, if you are able to interpret visions, you interpret.﴾ The word "ruʾyā" means dream, and its plural is ruʾā.

They said: ﴿They are confused dreams,﴾ that is, muddled and ambiguous dreams, false fancies. Its singular is ḍighth, and its root is a bundle of crops or grass. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle (ḍighth)﴾. Ibn Muqbil said:

"A tender woman, as if the scents of her bed were scattered bundles of basil brought by the north wind in the morning."

And another said:

"In the protected grazing land of Dhimar, when its defender was scarce, a hungry one, like a bundle of dry herbs in the belly, was confined."

"Aḥlām" is the plural of ḥulm, which is ruʾyā. The verb from it is ḥalimtu and aḥlamu, with a fatḥah on the ʿayn in the past tense. And ḥalimtuhā in the future, and ḥulman, and it becomes "ḥāliman" with the yāʾ dropped.

﴿We are not versed in the interpretation of dreams.﴾

﴿And the one who was saved from the two of them, the cupbearer, said, and he remembered after a time,﴾ that is, and he recalled Yusuf's need, his saying: "Mention me to your lord." ﴿After a period.﴾ That is, after a time. Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, and al-Dahhak recited "baʿda ummah," meaning after forgetting. It is said: "ummah," "yaʾmah," "ummah," if he forgot. And a man who is "mā huwa" is one whose intellect has gone.

Abu ʿUbaydah recited:

"I forgot, though I used to not forget a narration; thus time destroys intellects."

Mujahid recited "amh," with a sukūn on the mīm and a fatḥah on the alif and a clear hāʾ, and it is also a form like "al-umh," and they are two dialects, meaning forgetfulness. ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation,﴾ that is, I will tell you its explanation and what you are looking at. ﴿So send me.﴾ That is, release me, let me go, and permit me to proceed and come to you with its interpretation. The verse contains an ellipsis; its implied sense is "so send me," and he came to the prison. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The prison was not in the city. He said: ﴿Yusuf, O Yusuf,﴾ that is, "O Yusuf," ﴿O truthful one,﴾ regarding what you explained to us of the dream. "Ṣiddīq" means one who is very truthful. That is why Abu Bakr was called "al-Ṣiddīq." The form faʿīl is for intensity and abundance, like fasīq, ḍalīl, sharīb, khamīr, and similar words.

﴿Explain to us regarding seven fat cows﴾, the verse, for the king saw this dream.

I wish to return to the people, the people of Egypt, so that they may know its interpretation. It was also said: "so that they may know your merit and your knowledge." Then Yusuf, as a teacher and interpreter, said to them: "As for the seven fat cows and the seven green ears of grain, they are seven years of abundance; and the lean cows and the dry ears are the years of hardship, the barren and famine-stricken years." This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You shall sow for seven years in your usual manner﴾. That is, as is your custom. Some said it means with diligence and effort. Some of them read "daaban" with a fatha on the hamza, and both are dialectal forms (lughatan). It is said: "dabbat fi al-amr, adbu dabban and daban" when one exerts effort in a matter. Al-Farra' said: "Likewise, for every word whose first letter is vocalized with a fatha and whose second letter is sukun, its heavy form is permissible when its second letter is a hamza, an 'ayn, a ha', a kha', or a ha'."

﴿So whatever you harvest, leave it in its ear, except for a little that you eat﴾. He advised them to do this only so that it would remain and not spoil. ﴿Then after that will come seven hard years﴾, meaning seven years of drought and famine, ﴿which will consume what you have stored up for them﴾, meaning it will be eaten; what you prepared for them of food in the years of plenty will be consumed in them. This is like the saying of the poet:
"Your day, O deceived one, is heedlessness and negligence,
and your night is sleep, and death is bound to you."
[Al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: 9/231.]
Yet the day does not grow heedless and the night does not sleep; rather, one is heedless during the day and sleeps at night. ﴿Except for a little that you store up﴾, that is, that you keep in reserve and hoard.

﴿Then after that will come a year﴾. This is a report from Yusuf (peace be upon him) about what was not in the king's dream, but it is from the knowledge of the unseen that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave him. As Qatadah said: "Allah increased him in knowledge of a year they had not asked him about, so he said: ﴿Then after that will come a year﴾ ﴿in which the people will be given rain﴾, meaning they will be rained upon with the rain of showers. It was also said: "they will be relieved (yughathun)," from the Arab usage "istaghathtu bi-fulan wa aghathani" (I sought help from so-and-so and he helped me). ﴿And in it they will press (ya'sirun)﴾. The people of Kufa except 'Asim read "ta'sirun" with a ta', because the whole discourse is in the second person, while the rest read it with a ya', returning it to "the people." Most exegetes said: "they will press grapes into wine, olives into oil, and sesame into oil," and what is meant by the grapes, fruits, and grains is abundance of blessings and good. Al-Faraj ibn Fudalah related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "ta'sirun means ta'lubun (you will milk)." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "they will be saved (yanjuna) from drought and distress; and al-'asr means the refuge and the shelter." Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i said:
"Thirsty, seeking help and not being helped,
though he had been a refuge for the one who was saved."
[Al-Sihah: 2/749.]

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari, Abu 'Ali ibn Habash the reciter, and Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl the reciter informed me, saying: Abu Zur'ah related to me, Hafs ibn 'Umar related to me, Abu Jamilah related to me, from 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd who said: I heard 'Isa ibn al-A'raj recite it as "fihi yughathu al-nas wa fihi ya'sarun" with a damma on the ya', and he said: I said: "What is ya'sarun?" He said: "The rain," meaning they will be rained upon. And he recited: ﴿And We sent down from the pressing clouds water pouring forth﴾ [Surah al-Naba': 14].

And two young men entered the prison with him. They were two servants of the great king, al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan. One was his baker, the keeper of his food, named Mujlith. The other was his cupbearer, the keeper of his drink, named Bunw. The king had become angry with them and imprisoned them. The reason was that he had learned that his baker intended to poison him and that his cupbearer had agreed to this. The cause was that a group of people from Egypt wanted to scheme against the king and assassinate him. They approached these two men and promised them money in return for poisoning the king's food and drink. They agreed to this. Then the cupbearer backed out, but the baker accepted the bribe and poisoned the food.

When the time came and the food was brought, the cupbearer said: "O king, do not eat, for the food is poisoned." The baker said: "Do not drink, O king, for the drink is poisoned." The king said to the cupbearer: "Drink." He drank and it did him no harm. He said to the baker: "Eat from your food." He refused. So they tested that food on one of the animals, and it ate it and died. The king ordered them imprisoned.

When Yusuf (peace be upon him) entered the prison, he said to his companions: "I interpret dreams." One of the two young men said to his companion: "Come, let us test this Hebrew servant." They approached him and asked him, though neither of them had actually seen anything. ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: "The two companions of Yusuf did not see anything. They had only agreed together to test his knowledge."

ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever claims to have seen in a dream what he has not seen will be commanded on the Day of Resurrection to tie together two barley grains, and whoever listens to the conversation of a people who dislike him, molten lead will be poured into his ears."

Others said: "The two had seen real dreams, true in substance." Mujahid said: When the two young men saw Yusuf, they said to him: "By Allah, we loved you the moment we saw you." Yusuf said to them: "I implore you by Allah not to love me, for no one has ever loved me without a trial coming upon me because of his love.

My paternal aunt loved me, and a trial came upon me because of her love. Then my father loved me, and a trial came upon me because of his love. Then the wife of this king loved me, and a trial came upon me because of her love for me. So do not love me, may Allah bless you both." He said: They refused anything but to love him and to be close to him wherever he was. They were pleased by what they saw of his understanding and intellect. When the two had entered the prison, they had seen dreams. So they came to Yusuf, and the cupbearer said to him: "O scholar, I saw myself pressing wine from a grape vine on which there were three clusters of grapes, and the king's cup was in my hand, so I squeezed them into it and gave the king to drink, and he drank it."

The baker said: "I saw that on my head there were three baskets containing bread and various kinds of food, and birds of prey were pecking at it." That is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿One of them said, "Indeed I saw myself pressing wine."﴾ That is, the cupbearer, "Indeed I saw myself," meaning, I saw myself, "pressing wine," meaning grapes, in the dialect of ʿUmān. The recitation of Ibn Masʿud supports this: "pressing grapes" (aʿṣiru ʿinaban).

Al-Asmaʿi said: Al-Muʿtamir informed me that he met a Bedouin who had grapes with him. He said: "What do you have with you?" He said: "Wine." From this, vinegar made from grapes is called "wine vinegar" (khall khamra). This is by way of nearness of meaning. Al-Qutaybi said: It may also be wine itself, as one says, "I pressed oil," while he only pressed olives.

The other, namely Mujlith, said: ﴿Indeed I see myself carrying bread upon my head, and birds are eating from it. Inform us of its interpretation.﴾ That is, inform us of its explanation, its meaning, and what the outcome of this dream will be.

﴿Indeed we see you to be among the good-doers.﴾ That is, among the scholars who do good. Al-Farraʾ said, and Ibn Ishaq said: ﴿Indeed we see you to be among the good-doers﴾ toward us, if you do that and explain our dreams, just as one says, "Do such-and-such, you are a good-doer."

Salamah ibn Nabt narrated from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed we see you to be among the good-doers﴾: What was his goodness? He said: When a man fell ill in the prison, he would go to him. When someone was in distress, he would make room for him. If someone was in need, he would gather for him and ask on his behalf.

Qatadah said: We have been told that his goodness was that he would treat their sick, console their grieving, and strive in worship of his Lord.

It is also said: When Yusuf reached the prison, he found people whose hope had been cut off, whose trials had grown severe, and whose sorrow had lengthened. So he began to say: "Be glad and be patient, you will be rewarded. Indeed there is reward and recompense in this." They said to him: "O young man, may Allah bless you. How beautiful your face is, how beautiful your character is, and how beautiful your speech is! We have been blessed by your presence in the prison. Since we were imprisoned, we have been in something other than this, because of what you tell us of reward, expiation, and purification. Who are you, young man?"

He said: "I am Yusuf, son of Yaʿqub, the chosen of Allah, son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah." The jailer said to him: "O young man, by Allah, if I could, I would release you. But how good your company is and how good your reports are! Stay in whichever section of the prison you wish."

Yusuf (peace be upon him) disliked to interpret for them what they had asked him, because he knew that it would bring harm upon one of them. So he turned away from their question and moved on to something else. He said to them: ﴿No food will come to you that you are provided with in your sleep except that I will inform you of its interpretation while you are awake.﴾

This is the statement of most of the exegetes. Some of them said: He meant by it while awake. He said: ﴿No food will come to you that you are provided with﴾ that you will eat and consume, ﴿except that I will inform you of its interpretation﴾, of its explanation. He said: Whatever food you have eaten, when you ate it, and how much you ate. They said to him: "This is the work of fortune-tellers and soothsayers." He (peace be upon him) said to them: ﴿I am not a soothsayer. That is of what my Lord has taught me. Indeed I have abandoned the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.﴾ He repeated them for emphasis. It is also said: The first "they" is a substitute for a repeated, dropped element, as in His saying: ﴿Does he promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?﴾ So the first is dropped and the second is a new beginning, and "disbelievers" is its predicate.

﴿And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Yaʿqub. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah.﴾ Some people pronounced his yāʾ with a fatḥah, and others with a sukūn. [For such forms (as in the words) "wafā" and similar, the jazm (sukūn) is the original form, and the fatḥah is to match the alif, which it finds heavy, since it is its sister vowel.] Al-Aʿmash recited "ābāy Ibrāhīm" and "duʿāy illā firāran," with a short final vowel, not hamzated, and with the yāʾ of both pronounced with a fatḥah like [ ... ].

﴿Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Yaʿqub. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah.﴾ "Anything" is an object-like element; its sense is: that we associate with Allah anything.

﴿That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind﴾, that is, the tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) and knowledge. ﴿But most of mankind do not give thanks.﴾ Then Yusuf showed them his intelligence and knowledge, and then called them to Islam. He turned to them and to the people of the prison. Before them were idols that they worshipped. So he said, to press the argument: ﴿O two companions of the prison﴾. He called them the two companions of the prison because they were in it, like His saying to the inhabitants of Paradise: ﴿Companions of Paradise﴾ and to the inhabitants of the Fire: ﴿Companions of the Fire.﴾

﴿Are many lords dispersed better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ That is, many gods, various ones, who neither benefit nor harm. ﴿The One﴾ who has no partner. ﴿The Subduer﴾ who has subdued everything. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ Then he clarified the stone idols and their weakness, and said: ﴿What you worship besides Him﴾, that is, besides Allah. He said ﴿what you worship﴾ though he had begun speaking to two persons, because he meant by it all who were in the same state as them of association. ﴿Only names that you have named﴾, that is, their naming of their idols as gods and lords without that naming being true. ﴿You and your fathers have named them; Allah has not sent down any authority for them﴾, meaning proof and evidence. ﴿Judgment belongs only to Allah﴾, meaning the decision, command, and prohibition. ﴿He has commanded that you not worship except Him﴾. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion.﴾ ﴿That is the upright religion﴾, that is, what I have called you to, of tawhid and abandoning association. ﴿But most of mankind do not know.﴾

Then he explained their dreams, saying: ﴿O two companions of the prison. As for one of you, he will give his lord, his master, meaning the king, wine to drink.﴾ As for the three clusters he saw, they are three days; he will remain in the prison, then the king will release him and he will be restored to what he was. ﴿As for the other, he will be crucified.﴾ As for the three baskets he saw, they are three days; he will remain in the prison, then the king will bring him out [on] the fourth day and crucify him. ﴿And birds will eat from his head.﴾

Ibn Masʿud said: When they heard the words of Yusuf, they said: "We saw nothing; we were only playing." Yusuf (peace be upon him) said: ﴿The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire,﴾ that is, the matter about which you ask has been finished, and Allah's judgment has become binding upon you both according to what I told you.

Muʿallā ibn ʿAtaʾ narrated from Wakiʿ ibn ʿAdas, from his paternal uncle Abu Razin al-Uqayli, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Indeed a dream hangs over a man as a bird does, as long as it is not interpreted. When it is interpreted, it comes to pass. Indeed a dream is one part of forty-six parts of prophethood." I think he said: "Do not relate it except to one who has understanding."

And ʿAbdullah ibn Hamid informed us, from Ismaʿil ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn ʿAffan, from Ibn Numayr, from al-Aʿmash, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A dream follows the first interpreter."

And Yusuf said at that time, to the one who thought, meaning knew, that he would be saved from the two of them, namely the cupbearer. This is the statement of most of the exegetes. Qatadah explained "thought" as the sense of supposition that is the opposite of certainty, and said: The interpretation of dreams is only by supposition, and Allah creates whatever He wills. The first view is more correct and more fitting to the condition of the prophets. ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾, your master, meaning the king. It was said to him that in the prison there was a young man imprisoned unjustly. ﴿But Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his lord﴾, meaning Satan caused Yusuf to forget the remembrance of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, until he sought relief from someone else and sought help from a created being. That was a heedlessness that befell Yusuf from Satan. For this reason he forgot his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, who, had he appealed to Him, would have quickly brought his release. But he was heedless, and his imprisonment was prolonged because of it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The pronoun in His saying ﴿Satan caused him to forget﴾ refers to the cupbearer. So we say: Satan caused the cupbearer to forget the mention of Yusuf to the king. According to this view, the meaning of the verse is: "Satan caused him to forget his remembrance of his lord," like His saying: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies﴾, meaning he frightens you with his allies.

﴿He remained﴾, stayed, ﴿in the prison a few years.﴾ The scholars differed about the meaning of "few" (bidʿ). Abu ʿUbaydah said it is between three and five. Mujahid said: between three and nine. Al-Asmaʿi said: between three and nine. Ibn ʿAbbas said: fewer than ten. Al-Farraʾ claimed that "bidʿ" is only mentioned with ten and with twenty up to ninety, and that it is more than three up to nine. He said: "So I have seen the Arabs use it, and they do not say bidʿ and a hundred, nor bidʿ and a thousand." When the noun is masculine it is said bidʿah. Most exegetes hold that "bidʿ" in this verse means seven years. Wahb said: Job (peace be upon him) suffered affliction for seven years, Yusuf was left in the prison for seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar was punished and transformed among the beasts for seven years.

Yunus narrated from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on Yusuf. Had it not been for his statement, he would not have remained in the prison as long as he did." He meant His saying: "Mention me to your lord." He said: Then al-Hasan wept and said: "When a matter befalls us, we turn to people."

Malik ibn Dinar said: When Yusuf said to the cupbearer, "Mention me to your lord," it was said to him: "O Yusuf, you have taken other than Me as a guardian. I will surely prolong your imprisonment." Yusuf wept and said: "O my Lord, the abundance of hunger troubled me, so I spoke a word. Woe to my brothers."

It is related that Jibril (Gabriel) came to Yusuf (peace be upon them both). When Yusuf saw him, he recognized him and said: "O brother of those who warn, why do I see you among the sinners?" Then Jibril said to him: "O pure one among the pure, the Lord of the worlds sends you greetings and says: What is wrong with you? Were you not ashamed before Me when you sought help from human beings? By My might, I will surely keep you in the prison a few years." Yusuf said: "And He is pleased with me in that?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then I do not mind."

Kaʿb said: Jibril said to Yusuf: "Indeed Allah, may He be exalted, says: Who created you? He said: Allah. He said: Then who made you beloved to your father? He said: Allah. He said: Then who was your companion in the well when you entered it naked? He said: Allah. He said: Then who rescued you from the distress of the well? He said: Allah. He said: Then who taught you the interpretation of dreams? He said: Allah. He said: Then how did you seek intercession from a human being like yourself?"

When the seven years had passed, al-Kalbi said, and these seven were in addition to the five that had been before that, and when the relief of Yusuf drew near, the great king of Egypt saw a strange and terrifying dream. He saw: ﴿Indeed I see seven fat cows coming out of a dry river, and seven lean cows,﴾ that is, emaciated ones, and the lean ones swallowed the fat ones. They devoured them until they reached them, and he saw nothing of them. And he saw ﴿seven green ears of grain whose grain had formed, and seven others dry, withered, and the dry ones entwined around the green until they overcame them.﴾ He gathered the magicians, soothsayers, diviners, and physiognomists, and related it to them, and said: ﴿O assembly,﴾ that is, the nobles, ﴿explain to me my vision, if you are able to interpret visions, you interpret.﴾ The word "ruʾyā" means dream, and its plural is ruʾā.

They said: ﴿They are confused dreams,﴾ that is, muddled and ambiguous dreams, false fancies. Its singular is ḍighth, and its root is a bundle of crops or grass. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle (ḍighth)﴾. Ibn Muqbil said:

"A tender woman, as if the scents of her bed were scattered bundles of basil brought by the north wind in the morning."

And another said:

"In the protected grazing land of Dhimar, when its defender was scarce, a hungry one, like a bundle of dry herbs in the belly, was confined."

"Aḥlām" is the plural of ḥulm, which is ruʾyā. The verb from it is ḥalimtu and aḥlamu, with a fatḥah on the ʿayn in the past tense. And ḥalimtuhā in the future, and ḥulman, and it becomes "ḥāliman" with the yāʾ dropped.

﴿We are not versed in the interpretation of dreams.﴾

﴿And the one who was saved from the two of them, the cupbearer, said, and he remembered after a time,﴾ that is, and he recalled Yusuf's need, his saying: "Mention me to your lord." ﴿After a period.﴾ That is, after a time. Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, and al-Dahhak recited "baʿda ummah," meaning after forgetting. It is said: "ummah," "yaʾmah," "ummah," if he forgot. And a man who is "mā huwa" is one whose intellect has gone.

Abu ʿUbaydah recited:

"I forgot, though I used to not forget a narration; thus time destroys intellects."

Mujahid recited "amh," with a sukūn on the mīm and a fatḥah on the alif and a clear hāʾ, and it is also a form like "al-umh," and they are two dialects, meaning forgetfulness. ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation,﴾ that is, I will tell you its explanation and what you are looking at. ﴿So send me.﴾ That is, release me, let me go, and permit me to proceed and come to you with its interpretation. The verse contains an ellipsis; its implied sense is "so send me," and he came to the prison. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The prison was not in the city. He said: ﴿Yusuf, O Yusuf,﴾ that is, "O Yusuf," ﴿O truthful one,﴾ regarding what you explained to us of the dream. "Ṣiddīq" means one who is very truthful. That is why Abu Bakr was called "al-Ṣiddīq." The form faʿīl is for intensity and abundance, like fasīq, ḍalīl, sharīb, khamīr, and similar words.

﴿Explain to us regarding seven fat cows﴾, the verse, for the king saw this dream.

I wish to return to the people, the people of Egypt, so that they may know its interpretation. It was also said: "so that they may know your merit and your knowledge." Then Yusuf, as a teacher and interpreter, said to them: "As for the seven fat cows and the seven green ears of grain, they are seven years of abundance; and the lean cows and the dry ears are the years of hardship, the barren and famine-stricken years." This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You shall sow for seven years in your usual manner﴾. That is, as is your custom. Some said it means with diligence and effort. Some of them read "daaban" with a fatha on the hamza, and both are dialectal forms (lughatan). It is said: "dabbat fi al-amr, adbu dabban and daban" when one exerts effort in a matter. Al-Farra' said: "Likewise, for every word whose first letter is vocalized with a fatha and whose second letter is sukun, its heavy form is permissible when its second letter is a hamza, an 'ayn, a ha', a kha', or a ha'."

﴿So whatever you harvest, leave it in its ear, except for a little that you eat﴾. He advised them to do this only so that it would remain and not spoil. ﴿Then after that will come seven hard years﴾, meaning seven years of drought and famine, ﴿which will consume what you have stored up for them﴾, meaning it will be eaten; what you prepared for them of food in the years of plenty will be consumed in them. This is like the saying of the poet:
"Your day, O deceived one, is heedlessness and negligence,
and your night is sleep, and death is bound to you."
[Al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: 9/231.]
Yet the day does not grow heedless and the night does not sleep; rather, one is heedless during the day and sleeps at night. ﴿Except for a little that you store up﴾, that is, that you keep in reserve and hoard.

﴿Then after that will come a year﴾. This is a report from Yusuf (peace be upon him) about what was not in the king's dream, but it is from the knowledge of the unseen that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave him. As Qatadah said: "Allah increased him in knowledge of a year they had not asked him about, so he said: ﴿Then after that will come a year﴾ ﴿in which the people will be given rain﴾, meaning they will be rained upon with the rain of showers. It was also said: "they will be relieved (yughathun)," from the Arab usage "istaghathtu bi-fulan wa aghathani" (I sought help from so-and-so and he helped me). ﴿And in it they will press (ya'sirun)﴾. The people of Kufa except 'Asim read "ta'sirun" with a ta', because the whole discourse is in the second person, while the rest read it with a ya', returning it to "the people." Most exegetes said: "they will press grapes into wine, olives into oil, and sesame into oil," and what is meant by the grapes, fruits, and grains is abundance of blessings and good. Al-Faraj ibn Fudalah related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "ta'sirun means ta'lubun (you will milk)." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "they will be saved (yanjuna) from drought and distress; and al-'asr means the refuge and the shelter." Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i said:
"Thirsty, seeking help and not being helped,
though he had been a refuge for the one who was saved."
[Al-Sihah: 2/749.]

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari, Abu 'Ali ibn Habash the reciter, and Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl the reciter informed me, saying: Abu Zur'ah related to me, Hafs ibn 'Umar related to me, Abu Jamilah related to me, from 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd who said: I heard 'Isa ibn al-A'raj recite it as "fihi yughathu al-nas wa fihi ya'sarun" with a damma on the ya', and he said: I said: "What is ya'sarun?" He said: "The rain," meaning they will be rained upon. And he recited: ﴿And We sent down from the pressing clouds water pouring forth﴾ [Surah al-Naba': 14].

And two young men entered the prison with him. They were two servants of the great king, al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan. One was his baker, the keeper of his food, named Mujlith. The other was his cupbearer, the keeper of his drink, named Bunw. The king had become angry with them and imprisoned them. The reason was that he had learned that his baker intended to poison him and that his cupbearer had agreed to this. The cause was that a group of people from Egypt wanted to scheme against the king and assassinate him. They approached these two men and promised them money in return for poisoning the king's food and drink. They agreed to this. Then the cupbearer backed out, but the baker accepted the bribe and poisoned the food.

When the time came and the food was brought, the cupbearer said: "O king, do not eat, for the food is poisoned." The baker said: "Do not drink, O king, for the drink is poisoned." The king said to the cupbearer: "Drink." He drank and it did him no harm. He said to the baker: "Eat from your food." He refused. So they tested that food on one of the animals, and it ate it and died. The king ordered them imprisoned.

When Yusuf (peace be upon him) entered the prison, he said to his companions: "I interpret dreams." One of the two young men said to his companion: "Come, let us test this Hebrew servant." They approached him and asked him, though neither of them had actually seen anything. ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: "The two companions of Yusuf did not see anything. They had only agreed together to test his knowledge."

ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever claims to have seen in a dream what he has not seen will be commanded on the Day of Resurrection to tie together two barley grains, and whoever listens to the conversation of a people who dislike him, molten lead will be poured into his ears."

Others said: "The two had seen real dreams, true in substance." Mujahid said: When the two young men saw Yusuf, they said to him: "By Allah, we loved you the moment we saw you." Yusuf said to them: "I implore you by Allah not to love me, for no one has ever loved me without a trial coming upon me because of his love.

My paternal aunt loved me, and a trial came upon me because of her love. Then my father loved me, and a trial came upon me because of his love. Then the wife of this king loved me, and a trial came upon me because of her love for me. So do not love me, may Allah bless you both." He said: They refused anything but to love him and to be close to him wherever he was. They were pleased by what they saw of his understanding and intellect. When the two had entered the prison, they had seen dreams. So they came to Yusuf, and the cupbearer said to him: "O scholar, I saw myself pressing wine from a grape vine on which there were three clusters of grapes, and the king's cup was in my hand, so I squeezed them into it and gave the king to drink, and he drank it."

The baker said: "I saw that on my head there were three baskets containing bread and various kinds of food, and birds of prey were pecking at it." That is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿One of them said, "Indeed I saw myself pressing wine."﴾ That is, the cupbearer, "Indeed I saw myself," meaning, I saw myself, "pressing wine," meaning grapes, in the dialect of ʿUmān. The recitation of Ibn Masʿud supports this: "pressing grapes" (aʿṣiru ʿinaban).

Al-Asmaʿi said: Al-Muʿtamir informed me that he met a Bedouin who had grapes with him. He said: "What do you have with you?" He said: "Wine." From this, vinegar made from grapes is called "wine vinegar" (khall khamra). This is by way of nearness of meaning. Al-Qutaybi said: It may also be wine itself, as one says, "I pressed oil," while he only pressed olives.

The other, namely Mujlith, said: ﴿Indeed I see myself carrying bread upon my head, and birds are eating from it. Inform us of its interpretation.﴾ That is, inform us of its explanation, its meaning, and what the outcome of this dream will be.

﴿Indeed we see you to be among the good-doers.﴾ That is, among the scholars who do good. Al-Farraʾ said, and Ibn Ishaq said: ﴿Indeed we see you to be among the good-doers﴾ toward us, if you do that and explain our dreams, just as one says, "Do such-and-such, you are a good-doer."

Salamah ibn Nabt narrated from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed we see you to be among the good-doers﴾: What was his goodness? He said: When a man fell ill in the prison, he would go to him. When someone was in distress, he would make room for him. If someone was in need, he would gather for him and ask on his behalf.

Qatadah said: We have been told that his goodness was that he would treat their sick, console their grieving, and strive in worship of his Lord.

It is also said: When Yusuf reached the prison, he found people whose hope had been cut off, whose trials had grown severe, and whose sorrow had lengthened. So he began to say: "Be glad and be patient, you will be rewarded. Indeed there is reward and recompense in this." They said to him: "O young man, may Allah bless you. How beautiful your face is, how beautiful your character is, and how beautiful your speech is! We have been blessed by your presence in the prison. Since we were imprisoned, we have been in something other than this, because of what you tell us of reward, expiation, and purification. Who are you, young man?"

He said: "I am Yusuf, son of Yaʿqub, the chosen of Allah, son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah." The jailer said to him: "O young man, by Allah, if I could, I would release you. But how good your company is and how good your reports are! Stay in whichever section of the prison you wish."

Yusuf (peace be upon him) disliked to interpret for them what they had asked him, because he knew that it would bring harm upon one of them. So he turned away from their question and moved on to something else. He said to them: ﴿No food will come to you that you are provided with in your sleep except that I will inform you of its interpretation while you are awake.﴾

This is the statement of most of the exegetes. Some of them said: He meant by it while awake. He said: ﴿No food will come to you that you are provided with﴾ that you will eat and consume, ﴿except that I will inform you of its interpretation﴾, of its explanation. He said: Whatever food you have eaten, when you ate it, and how much you ate. They said to him: "This is the work of fortune-tellers and soothsayers." He (peace be upon him) said to them: ﴿I am not a soothsayer. That is of what my Lord has taught me. Indeed I have abandoned the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.﴾ He repeated them for emphasis. It is also said: The first "they" is a substitute for a repeated, dropped element, as in His saying: ﴿Does he promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?﴾ So the first is dropped and the second is a new beginning, and "disbelievers" is its predicate.

﴿And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Yaʿqub. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah.﴾ Some people pronounced his yāʾ with a fatḥah, and others with a sukūn. [For such forms (as in the words) "wafā" and similar, the jazm (sukūn) is the original form, and the fatḥah is to match the alif, which it finds heavy, since it is its sister vowel.] Al-Aʿmash recited "ābāy Ibrāhīm" and "duʿāy illā firāran," with a short final vowel, not hamzated, and with the yāʾ of both pronounced with a fatḥah like [ ... ].

﴿Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Yaʿqub. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah.﴾ "Anything" is an object-like element; its sense is: that we associate with Allah anything.

﴿That is from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind﴾, that is, the tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) and knowledge. ﴿But most of mankind do not give thanks.﴾ Then Yusuf showed them his intelligence and knowledge, and then called them to Islam. He turned to them and to the people of the prison. Before them were idols that they worshipped. So he said, to press the argument: ﴿O two companions of the prison﴾. He called them the two companions of the prison because they were in it, like His saying to the inhabitants of Paradise: ﴿Companions of Paradise﴾ and to the inhabitants of the Fire: ﴿Companions of the Fire.﴾

﴿Are many lords dispersed better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ That is, many gods, various ones, who neither benefit nor harm. ﴿The One﴾ who has no partner. ﴿The Subduer﴾ who has subdued everything. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ Then he clarified the stone idols and their weakness, and said: ﴿What you worship besides Him﴾, that is, besides Allah. He said ﴿what you worship﴾ though he had begun speaking to two persons, because he meant by it all who were in the same state as them of association. ﴿Only names that you have named﴾, that is, their naming of their idols as gods and lords without that naming being true. ﴿You and your fathers have named them; Allah has not sent down any authority for them﴾, meaning proof and evidence. ﴿Judgment belongs only to Allah﴾, meaning the decision, command, and prohibition. ﴿He has commanded that you not worship except Him﴾. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion.﴾ ﴿That is the upright religion﴾, that is, what I have called you to, of tawhid and abandoning association. ﴿But most of mankind do not know.﴾

Then he explained their dreams, saying: ﴿O two companions of the prison. As for one of you, he will give his lord, his master, meaning the king, wine to drink.﴾ As for the three clusters he saw, they are three days; he will remain in the prison, then the king will release him and he will be restored to what he was. ﴿As for the other, he will be crucified.﴾ As for the three baskets he saw, they are three days; he will remain in the prison, then the king will bring him out [on] the fourth day and crucify him. ﴿And birds will eat from his head.﴾

Ibn Masʿud said: When they heard the words of Yusuf, they said: "We saw nothing; we were only playing." Yusuf (peace be upon him) said: ﴿The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire,﴾ that is, the matter about which you ask has been finished, and Allah's judgment has become binding upon you both according to what I told you.

Muʿallā ibn ʿAtaʾ narrated from Wakiʿ ibn ʿAdas, from his paternal uncle Abu Razin al-Uqayli, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Indeed a dream hangs over a man as a bird does, as long as it is not interpreted. When it is interpreted, it comes to pass. Indeed a dream is one part of forty-six parts of prophethood." I think he said: "Do not relate it except to one who has understanding."

And ʿAbdullah ibn Hamid informed us, from Ismaʿil ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn ʿAffan, from Ibn Numayr, from al-Aʿmash, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A dream follows the first interpreter."

And Yusuf said at that time, to the one who thought, meaning knew, that he would be saved from the two of them, namely the cupbearer. This is the statement of most of the exegetes. Qatadah explained "thought" as the sense of supposition that is the opposite of certainty, and said: The interpretation of dreams is only by supposition, and Allah creates whatever He wills. The first view is more correct and more fitting to the condition of the prophets. ﴿Mention me to your lord﴾, your master, meaning the king. It was said to him that in the prison there was a young man imprisoned unjustly. ﴿But Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his lord﴾, meaning Satan caused Yusuf to forget the remembrance of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, until he sought relief from someone else and sought help from a created being. That was a heedlessness that befell Yusuf from Satan. For this reason he forgot his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, who, had he appealed to Him, would have quickly brought his release. But he was heedless, and his imprisonment was prolonged because of it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The pronoun in His saying ﴿Satan caused him to forget﴾ refers to the cupbearer. So we say: Satan caused the cupbearer to forget the mention of Yusuf to the king. According to this view, the meaning of the verse is: "Satan caused him to forget his remembrance of his lord," like His saying: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies﴾, meaning he frightens you with his allies.

﴿He remained﴾, stayed, ﴿in the prison a few years.﴾ The scholars differed about the meaning of "few" (bidʿ). Abu ʿUbaydah said it is between three and five. Mujahid said: between three and nine. Al-Asmaʿi said: between three and nine. Ibn ʿAbbas said: fewer than ten. Al-Farraʾ claimed that "bidʿ" is only mentioned with ten and with twenty up to ninety, and that it is more than three up to nine. He said: "So I have seen the Arabs use it, and they do not say bidʿ and a hundred, nor bidʿ and a thousand." When the noun is masculine it is said bidʿah. Most exegetes hold that "bidʿ" in this verse means seven years. Wahb said: Job (peace be upon him) suffered affliction for seven years, Yusuf was left in the prison for seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar was punished and transformed among the beasts for seven years.

Yunus narrated from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on Yusuf. Had it not been for his statement, he would not have remained in the prison as long as he did." He meant His saying: "Mention me to your lord." He said: Then al-Hasan wept and said: "When a matter befalls us, we turn to people."

Malik ibn Dinar said: When Yusuf said to the cupbearer, "Mention me to your lord," it was said to him: "O Yusuf, you have taken other than Me as a guardian. I will surely prolong your imprisonment." Yusuf wept and said: "O my Lord, the abundance of hunger troubled me, so I spoke a word. Woe to my brothers."

It is related that Jibril (Gabriel) came to Yusuf (peace be upon them both). When Yusuf saw him, he recognized him and said: "O brother of those who warn, why do I see you among the sinners?" Then Jibril said to him: "O pure one among the pure, the Lord of the worlds sends you greetings and says: What is wrong with you? Were you not ashamed before Me when you sought help from human beings? By My might, I will surely keep you in the prison a few years." Yusuf said: "And He is pleased with me in that?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then I do not mind."

Kaʿb said: Jibril said to Yusuf: "Indeed Allah, may He be exalted, says: Who created you? He said: Allah. He said: Then who made you beloved to your father? He said: Allah. He said: Then who was your companion in the well when you entered it naked? He said: Allah. He said: Then who rescued you from the distress of the well? He said: Allah. He said: Then who taught you the interpretation of dreams? He said: Allah. He said: Then how did you seek intercession from a human being like yourself?"

When the seven years had passed, al-Kalbi said, and these seven were in addition to the five that had been before that, and when the relief of Yusuf drew near, the great king of Egypt saw a strange and terrifying dream. He saw: ﴿Indeed I see seven fat cows coming out of a dry river, and seven lean cows,﴾ that is, emaciated ones, and the lean ones swallowed the fat ones. They devoured them until they reached them, and he saw nothing of them. And he saw ﴿seven green ears of grain whose grain had formed, and seven others dry, withered, and the dry ones entwined around the green until they overcame them.﴾ He gathered the magicians, soothsayers, diviners, and physiognomists, and related it to them, and said: ﴿O assembly,﴾ that is, the nobles, ﴿explain to me my vision, if you are able to interpret visions, you interpret.﴾ The word "ruʾyā" means dream, and its plural is ruʾā.

They said: ﴿They are confused dreams,﴾ that is, muddled and ambiguous dreams, false fancies. Its singular is ḍighth, and its root is a bundle of crops or grass. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle (ḍighth)﴾. Ibn Muqbil said:

"A tender woman, as if the scents of her bed were scattered bundles of basil brought by the north wind in the morning."

And another said:

"In the protected grazing land of Dhimar, when its defender was scarce, a hungry one, like a bundle of dry herbs in the belly, was confined."

"Aḥlām" is the plural of ḥulm, which is ruʾyā. The verb from it is ḥalimtu and aḥlamu, with a fatḥah on the ʿayn in the past tense. And ḥalimtuhā in the future, and ḥulman, and it becomes "ḥāliman" with the yāʾ dropped.

﴿We are not versed in the interpretation of dreams.﴾

﴿And the one who was saved from the two of them, the cupbearer, said, and he remembered after a time,﴾ that is, and he recalled Yusuf's need, his saying: "Mention me to your lord." ﴿After a period.﴾ That is, after a time. Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, and al-Dahhak recited "baʿda ummah," meaning after forgetting. It is said: "ummah," "yaʾmah," "ummah," if he forgot. And a man who is "mā huwa" is one whose intellect has gone.

Abu ʿUbaydah recited:

"I forgot, though I used to not forget a narration; thus time destroys intellects."

Mujahid recited "amh," with a sukūn on the mīm and a fatḥah on the alif and a clear hāʾ, and it is also a form like "al-umh," and they are two dialects, meaning forgetfulness. ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation,﴾ that is, I will tell you its explanation and what you are looking at. ﴿So send me.﴾ That is, release me, let me go, and permit me to proceed and come to you with its interpretation. The verse contains an ellipsis; its implied sense is "so send me," and he came to the prison. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The prison was not in the city. He said: ﴿Yusuf, O Yusuf,﴾ that is, "O Yusuf," ﴿O truthful one,﴾ regarding what you explained to us of the dream. "Ṣiddīq" means one who is very truthful. That is why Abu Bakr was called "al-Ṣiddīq." The form faʿīl is for intensity and abundance, like fasīq, ḍalīl, sharīb, khamīr, and similar words.

﴿Explain to us regarding seven fat cows﴾, the verse, for the king saw this dream.

I wish to return to the people, the people of Egypt, so that they may know its interpretation. It was also said: "so that they may know your merit and your knowledge." Then Yusuf, as a teacher and interpreter, said to them: "As for the seven fat cows and the seven green ears of grain, they are seven years of abundance; and the lean cows and the dry ears are the years of hardship, the barren and famine-stricken years." This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You shall sow for seven years in your usual manner﴾. That is, as is your custom. Some said it means with diligence and effort. Some of them read "daaban" with a fatha on the hamza, and both are dialectal forms (lughatan). It is said: "dabbat fi al-amr, adbu dabban and daban" when one exerts effort in a matter. Al-Farra' said: "Likewise, for every word whose first letter is vocalized with a fatha and whose second letter is sukun, its heavy form is permissible when its second letter is a hamza, an 'ayn, a ha', a kha', or a ha'."

﴿So whatever you harvest, leave it in its ear, except for a little that you eat﴾. He advised them to do this only so that it would remain and not spoil. ﴿Then after that will come seven hard years﴾, meaning seven years of drought and famine, ﴿which will consume what you have stored up for them﴾, meaning it will be eaten; what you prepared for them of food in the years of plenty will be consumed in them. This is like the saying of the poet:
"Your day, O deceived one, is heedlessness and negligence,
and your night is sleep, and death is bound to you."
[Al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: 9/231.]
Yet the day does not grow heedless and the night does not sleep; rather, one is heedless during the day and sleeps at night. ﴿Except for a little that you store up﴾, that is, that you keep in reserve and hoard.

﴿Then after that will come a year﴾. This is a report from Yusuf (peace be upon him) about what was not in the king's dream, but it is from the knowledge of the unseen that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave him. As Qatadah said: "Allah increased him in knowledge of a year they had not asked him about, so he said: ﴿Then after that will come a year﴾ ﴿in which the people will be given rain﴾, meaning they will be rained upon with the rain of showers. It was also said: "they will be relieved (yughathun)," from the Arab usage "istaghathtu bi-fulan wa aghathani" (I sought help from so-and-so and he helped me). ﴿And in it they will press (ya'sirun)﴾. The people of Kufa except 'Asim read "ta'sirun" with a ta', because the whole discourse is in the second person, while the rest read it with a ya', returning it to "the people." Most exegetes said: "they will press grapes into wine, olives into oil, and sesame into oil," and what is meant by the grapes, fruits, and grains is abundance of blessings and good. Al-Faraj ibn Fudalah related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "ta'sirun means ta'lubun (you will milk)." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "they will be saved (yanjuna) from drought and distress; and al-'asr means the refuge and the shelter." Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i said:
"Thirsty, seeking help and not being helped,
though he had been a refuge for the one who was saved."
[Al-Sihah: 2/749.]

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari, Abu 'Ali ibn Habash the reciter, and Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl the reciter informed me, saying: Abu Zur'ah related to me, Hafs ibn 'Umar related to me, Abu Jamilah related to me, from 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd who said: I heard 'Isa ibn al-A'raj recite it as "fihi yughathu al-nas wa fihi ya'sarun" with a damma on the ya', and he said: I said: "What is ya'sarun?" He said: "The rain," meaning they will be rained upon. And he recited: ﴿And We sent down from the pressing clouds water pouring forth﴾ [Surah al-Naba': 14].

And two young men entered the prison with him. They were two servants of the great king, al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan. One was his baker, the keeper of his food, named Mujlith. The other was his cupbearer, the keeper of his drink, named Bunw. The king had become angry with them and imprisoned them. The reason was that he had learned that his baker intended to poison him and that his cupbearer had agreed to this. The cause was that a group of people from Egypt wanted to scheme against the king and assassinate him. They approached these two men and promised them money in return for poisoning the king's food and drink. They agreed to this. Then the cupbearer backed out, but the baker accepted the bribe and poisoned the food.

When the time came and the food was brought, the cupbearer said: "O king, do not eat, for the food is poisoned." The baker said: "Do not drink, O king, for the drink is poisoned." The king said to the cupbearer: "Drink." He drank and it did him no harm. He said to the baker: "Eat from your food." He refused. So they tested that food on one of the animals, and it ate it and died. The king ordered them imprisoned.

When Yusuf (peace be upon him) entered the prison, he said to his companions: "I interpret dreams." One of the two young men said to his companion: "Come, let us test this Hebrew servant." They approached him and asked him, though neither of them had actually seen anything. ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: "The two companions of Yusuf did not see anything. They had only agreed together to test his knowledge."

ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever claims to have seen in a dream what he has not seen will be commanded on the Day of Resurrection to tie together two barley grains, and whoever listens to the conversation of a people who dislike him, molten lead will be poured into his ears."

Others said: "The two had seen real dreams, true in substance." Mujahid said: When the two young men saw Yusuf, they said to him: "By Allah, we loved you the moment we saw you." Yusuf said to them: "I implore you by Allah not to love me, for no one has ever loved me without a trial coming upon me because of his love.

My paternal aunt loved me, and a trial came upon me because of her love. Then my father loved me, and a trial came upon me because of his love. Then the wife of this king loved me, and a trial came upon me because of her love for me. So do not love me, may Allah bless you both." He said: They refused anything but to love him and to be close to him wherever he was. They were pleased by what they saw of his understanding and intellect. When the two had entered the prison, they had seen dreams. So they came to Yusuf, and the cupbearer said to him: "O scholar, I saw myself pressing wine from a grape vine on which there were three clusters of grapes, and the king's cup was in my hand, so I squeezed them into it and gave the king to drink, and he drank it."

The baker said: "I saw that on my head there were three baskets containing bread and various kinds of food, and birds of prey were pecking at it."
