Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Jahmayn related to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Mujlaz related to us, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Baghdādī said, Khalaf ibn Tamīm, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Muslim, from al-Khaffāf, from Jaʿfar ibn Nawqān, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar: that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib came to ʿUthmān while he was besieged. He sent to him greetings and said, "I have come to support you." ʿUthmān sent greetings back and said, "May God reward you with good. There is no need for fighting these people." ʿAlī then took off his turban, removed it, threw it into the courtyard, and turned away, saying: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence, and that God does not guide the plot of the treacherous.﴾

The people of exegesis said: when Yusuf said this statement, Gabriel said to him, "Not even when you desired her?" At that, Yusuf said, ﴿"Nor do I absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon whom my Lord has mercy."﴾ That is, except one whom my Lord has shown mercy to and so protected. "Mā" here means "man," like God's saying, ﴿Marry what is good for you of women﴾ (Qur'an 4:3), that is, those who are good for you. The exception ﴿except﴾ is a discontinuous exception from what precedes it, like God's saying, ﴿nor will they be saved, except as a mercy from Us﴾ (Qur'an 36:43–44), meaning, except that they be shown mercy. When "in" carries the sense of a verbal noun, it corresponds to "mā."

﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ When the truth of Yusuf became clear to the king and he recognised his trustworthiness and knowledge, he said:

﴿"Bring him to me; I will take him for myself,"﴾ that is, I will make him exclusively mine, apart from anyone else. When the messenger came to Yusuf he said to him, ﴿"Answer the king"﴾, now.

Yusuf went out and supplicated for the people of the prison with a supplication that is known to this day. He said:

"O God, incline toward them the hearts of the righteous and grant them good news, for they are the most knowledgeable of people about tidings in every land." When he came out of the prison, he wrote on its door: "This is the grave of the living, the house of sorrows, the burning of friends, and the gloating of enemies." Then Yusuf (peace be upon him) washed, cleansed himself of the filth of the prison, put on new fine clothes, and went to the king.

Wahb said: when he stood at the door of the king he said (peace be upon him): "God is sufficient for me in my worldly affairs, and God is sufficient for me against His creation. Mighty is His protection, exalted is His praise, and there is no god but Him."

Then he entered the palace. When he entered upon the king, he said: "O God, I ask You for Your might from its good, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of others." When the king looked at him, Yusuf greeted him in Arabic. The king said to him, "What language is this?" He said, "The language of my paternal uncle Ismāʿīl." Then he greeted him in Hebrew, and the king said, "What language is this?" He said, "The language of my fathers."

Wahb said: the king used to speak seventy languages. Whenever he spoke to Yusuf in one language, Yusuf answered him in that language, and the king was pleased. The king was astonished at what he saw of him. Yusuf was then thirty years old. When the king saw his youthfulness, he said to those with him: "This is the knowledge of the interpretation of my dream, which the magicians and soothsayers did not know." Then he seated him on his throne and said to him: "I wish to hear my dream from you directly." Yusuf said to him, "Yes, O king. You saw seven fat cows, white, bright and handsome, whom the Nile revealed to you; they came up to you from its bank, their udders dripping milk. While you were looking at them and marvelling at their beauty, the Nile subsided, its water receded and it became dry. Out of its mud and slime came seven lean cows, dishevelled, dusty, with shrunken bellies, having no udders or teats, with fangs and molars, paws like dogs' paws, and snouts like those of beasts. They mixed with the fat ones and devoured them like a beast of prey; they ate their flesh, tore their skins, broke their bones, and sucked their marrow.

While you were looking and marvelling, behold, seven green ears of grain and seven others dry and black, in a single place of growth, their roots in the soil and water. While you were saying to yourself, 'How is this possible? These are green and fruitful, and these are black and dried up, yet they grow from one place and their roots are in the water,' a wind blew and scattered the leaves of the dry black ones onto the green fruitful ones. Fire then broke out among them, burned them, and they became black and changed.

That is the last of what you saw of the world. Then you awoke from your sleep in alarm." The king said, "By God, what is the matter with this dream? Though it is strange, it is no stranger than what I have heard from you. So what do you see in my dream, O truthful one?" Yusuf said: "I advise that you gather food and sow abundant crops in these fruitful years, and build [storehouses] and treasuries, and place the grain in them with its stalk and ear, so that its stalk and ear become fodder for the animals. Command the people to set aside a fifth of their produce, and it will suffice you, from the food you have gathered, for the people of Egypt and those around it. People will come to you from all regions seeking grain, and treasures will gather with you that have not gathered for anyone before you."

The king said, "Who can do this for me, and who will gather it, [sell it] and take up the task of managing it?" Yusuf said: ﴿"Set me over the storehouses of the land"﴾. The figurative meaning of the verse is: over the storehouses of your land. "Khazāʾin" is the plural of "khizāna," and the definite article entered as a substitute for the genitive construction, as in the words of al-Nābigha:

"And dreams are not false."

﴿Indeed, I am a guardian, knowing.﴾ Meaning: a writer and reckoner. Qatāda: "Guardian of what I am entrusted with, knowing of its affairs." Ibn Isḥāq: "Guardian of what you have entrusted to me, knowing of what you have appointed me to." Shayba al-Ḍabbī: "Guardian of what you have entrusted to me, and knowing of the years of famine." Al-Aʿshā: "Keeping account, and knowing of languages, knowing the language of whoever asks me." Al-Kalbī: "Guardian of the estimation in these barren years, knowing when the hunger will strike." It has also been said: "Guardian of what has reached me, knowing of its accounting of wealth."

The king said to him, "Who is more deserving of it than you?" So he appointed him to that office and said to him: ﴿"Indeed, today you are with us established and trusted,"﴾ possessing rank and standing, trustworthy over the treasuries.

Juwaybir narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "May God have mercy on my brother Yusuf. Had he not said, ﴿Set me over the storehouses of the land﴾, he would have employed him immediately. But he delayed that for a year, so he remained with him in his house for a year, with the king." [121] [[Zād al-Masīr: 4/185; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 9/211.]]

Sufyān narrated from Abū Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl, who said: The king said to Yusuf: "I want you to mix with me in everything, except that I disdain that you should eat with me." Yusuf (peace be upon him) said: "I have more right to disdain it. I am the son of Yaʿqūb, Isrāʾīl of God, son of Isḥāq, the sacrificed one of God, son of Ibrāhīm, the friend of God." So from then on he ate with him.

Ḥamza al-Rayyān narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Maysara, who said: When the ʿAzīz saw Yusuf's opinion and his refinement, he invited him, and he used to lunch and dine with him apart from his servants. When what happened between him and the woman happened, she said to him once, "Let him lunch with the servants." So he said, "Go and lunch with the servants." Yusuf said to him to his face: "Have you disdained to eat with me? I am, by God, Yusuf son of Yaʿqūb, the prophet of God, son of Isḥāq, the sacrificed one of God, son of Ibrāhīm, the friend of God."

Muqātil narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb offered Abū Hurayra the governorship, and he said: "I will not do it, nor do I want it. I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever seeks leadership will not act justly.'" [122] [[In Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ (12/94): "Whoever is eager for leadership will not act justly in it."]] ʿUmar said: "Indeed, one better than you sought leadership: Yusuf (peace be upon him), who said, ﴿Set me over the storehouses of the land﴾."

Ibn Isḥāq narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When a year had passed since the day he asked for the governorship, the king summoned him, crowned him, girded him with his sword, and placed for him a golden throne adorned with pearls and rubies, and draped over it a silk brocade. The throne was thirty cubits long and ten cubits wide, with thirty mattresses and ninety cushions on it. Then he ordered him to go out, and he went out crowned, his complexion like snow and his face like the moon, so that the beholder could see his face in the clarity of its colour. He went and sat on the throne, and the kings submitted to him. The king entered his house with his women and entrusted to him the affairs of Egypt, removing Qiṭfīr from what he had been over and placing Yusuf in his position.

Ibn Isḥāq said: Ibn Zayd said: Pharaoh, king of Egypt, had many treasuries besides the food, so he handed over all his authority to him and made his command and judgement binding. Then Qiṭfīr died during those nights, and the king married Yusuf to Rāḥīl, the wife of Qiṭfīr. When he entered upon her, he said, "Is this not better than what you used to desire?" She said: "O truthful one, do not blame me, for I was a beautiful, pampered woman, as you see, in wealth and luxury, and my husband did not come near women. I was as God made you in your beauty and form, and my self overcame me." Yusuf found her to be a virgin, and he had intercourse with her, and she bore him two sons: Ifrāʾīm son of Yusuf and Manashā son of Yusuf.

The rule of Egypt became settled for Yusuf, and he established justice among them, so men and women loved him. This is God's saying:

﴿And thus did We establish Yusuf in the land﴾, meaning the land of Egypt, that is, We gave him authority there, ﴿to settle therein wherever he willed﴾, and to act in it as he wished. "Tabawwu'" means to dwell; it is said "bawwa'tuhu" and "tabawwa'a." The reading of the people of Mecca is "nashāʾ" (we will) with a nūn, in response to His saying "makkannā" and what follows it: ﴿We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will﴾, that is, by Our favour.

﴿And We do not waste the reward of the good-doers.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbās and Wahb said: that is, the patient, like his patience in the well, his patience in prison, his patience in servitude, and his patience against what the woman invited him to. Mujāhid and others said: he continued to supplicate and to be gentle with him until the king and many people became Muslim. This is in this world. ﴿And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believed and were mindful of God.﴾ Al-Buḥturī said:

"Is there not in the Messenger of God, Yusuf, an example for one like you, imprisoned [....]"
[[An illegible word.]]

"He persisted in beautiful patience in confinement for a time, until beautiful patience brought him to the king."
[[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 9/220.]]

One of them wrote to a friend of his:

"Beyond the narrow passage of fear is the wide expanse of safety, and the first joy is followed by the last sorrow.
So do not despair, for God has granted Yusuf his treasuries after his release from prison."
[[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 9/220, where it reads "the end of sorrow" instead of "the last sorrow."]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 12, verses 50–57:

The king said, "Bring him to me," (the verse). This is because when the messenger returned to the king and informed him of what Yusuf had explained to him about the interpretation of his dream, it was as clear as daylight, and the king recognised that what he had said would come to pass. He said, "Bring me the one who interpreted my dream." When the messenger came to Yusuf and told him, "Inform the king," Yusuf refused to leave with the messenger until his innocence and clean record were made evident and the soundness of his case was known from the women's side. So he said to the messenger, ﴿Return to your lord﴾, that is, your master, meaning the king, ﴿and ask him what happened to the women who cut their hands﴾, and the woman who imprisoned me because of her wrongdoing. It is narrated by ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Ṣabbāḥ al-Burjumī and Muḥammad ibn Ḥabīb al-Shamūnī, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, from ʿĀṣim, that he recited "al-nusūh" (the women) with a ḍamma on the nūn.

﴿Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot﴾: indeed God, exalted is He, is Knowing of their deeds. It has also been said that the meaning is: indeed my master, Qiṭfīr the ʿAzīz, is Aware of my innocence regarding what the woman accuses me of.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: Yusuf was then released before the king had settled his affair. When the suspicion remained in the heart of the ʿAzīz about him, he would say, "This is the one who sought to seduce my wife."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I have marvelled at Yusuf, at his generosity, his patience, and God forgives him, when he was asked about the lean cows and the fat ones. Had I been in his place, I would not have informed them until I had stipulated that they bring me out. And I have marvelled at Yusuf, his generosity and his patience, and God forgives him, when the messenger came to him and he said, ﴿Return to your lord﴾. Had I been in his place and had I remained in prison as long as he remained, I would have hastened to answer and rushed to the door. I would not have sought forgiveness. He was forbearing, possessed of deliberation." [120] [[Tafsīr Majmaʿ al-Bayān: 5/413, in full; Jāmiʿ al-Bayān of al-Ṭabarī: 12/307, with slight variation.]]

﴿He said, "What was your affair, when you sought to seduce Yusuf?"﴾ (the verse). In the speech there is an omitted part that is not needed, and the sense indicates it, which is:

The messenger returned to the king from Yusuf with a message. The king then summoned the women who had cut their hands and the wife of the ʿAzīz, and said to them, ﴿"What was your affair (khaṭbukunna), that is, what was your situation and matter, when you sought to seduce Yusuf from himself?"﴾ So they fell in love with him. ﴿They said, "Ḥāsha lillāh (far be it from God), we know nothing evil of him."﴾ ﴿The wife of the ʿAzīz said, "Now the truth has become manifest (ḥaṣḥaṣa al-ḥaqq)"﴾, that is, it became apparent and clear. The root of it is ḥaṣṣ, and it is said that it is ḥaṣṣaṣ, as they said kabkabū for kabbū, kafkaf for kaff, and radded for radd. The original meaning of ḥaṣṣ is the uprooting of a thing; it is said ḥaṣṣa shaʿrahu when he shaved it off completely. Abū Qays ibn al-Aslat said:

"The helmet has shaved my head, so I do not taste sleep except light dozing."
[[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 3/1032.]]

And her saying "Now the truth has become manifest" means: falsehood and lying have departed and ceased, and the truth has become clear and shone forth. ﴿"I sought to seduce him from himself, and he is indeed among the truthful,"﴾ meaning in his saying, "It is she who sought to seduce me."

When Yusuf heard that, he said, so that this may be known, namely the matter of my returning the king's messenger concerning the women, ﴿that the ʿAzīz may know﴾.

﴿that I did not betray him in his wife in his absence, and that God does not guide the plot of the treacherous.﴾ The speech of Yusuf, ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence﴾, is connected to the woman's saying, "I sought to seduce him from himself," without a clarifying phrase. He separated them so that the hearers would know its meaning. This resembles the connection of God's saying, ﴿And thus they do﴾ (Qur'an 27:34), to the words of Bilqīs, ﴿and they make the most honoured of its people abject﴾. Likewise is the saying of Pharaoh to his counsellors, ﴿"What do you advise?"﴾, which is connected to the words of the chiefs, ﴿"He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic"﴾ (Qur'an 26:35).

Abū ʿUbayda narrated from al-Farrāʾ that he said: this is among the most obscure things that occur in speech, that one reports something about a man and then says something about another matter in the words of another man who has not been mentioned.

Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Jahmayn related to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, who said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Mujlaz related to us, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Baghdādī said, Khalaf ibn Tamīm, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Muslim, from al-Khaffāf, from Jaʿfar ibn Nawqān, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar: that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib came to ʿUthmān while he was besieged. He sent to him greetings and said, "I have come to support you." ʿUthmān sent greetings back and said, "May God reward you with good. There is no need for fighting these people." ʿAlī then took off his turban, removed it, threw it into the courtyard, and turned away, saying: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence, and that God does not guide the plot of the treacherous.﴾

The people of exegesis said: when Yusuf said this statement, Gabriel said to him, "Not even when you desired her?" At that, Yusuf said, ﴿"Nor do I absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon whom my Lord has mercy."﴾ That is, except one whom my Lord has shown mercy to and so protected. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ When the truth of Yusuf became clear to the king and he recognised his trustworthiness and knowledge, he said:

﴿"Bring him to me; I will take him for myself,"﴾ that is, I will make him exclusively mine, apart from anyone else. When the messenger came to Yusuf he said to him, ﴿"Answer the king"﴾, now.

Yusuf went out and supplicated for the people of the prison with a supplication that is known to this day. He said:

"O God, incline toward them the hearts of the righteous and grant them good news, for they are the most knowledgeable of people about tidings in every land." When he came out of the prison, he wrote on its door: "This is the grave of the living, the house of sorrows, the burning of friends, and the gloating of enemies." Then Yusuf (peace be upon him) washed, cleansed himself of the filth of the prison, put on new fine clothes, and went to the king.

Wahb said: when he stood at the door of the king he said (peace be upon him): "God is sufficient for me in my worldly affairs, and God is sufficient for me against His creation. Mighty is His protection, exalted is His praise, and there is no god but Him."

Then he entered the palace. When he entered upon the king, he said: "O God, I ask You for Your might from its good, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of others." When the king looked at him, Yusuf greeted him in Arabic. The king said to him, "What language is this?" He said, "The language of my paternal uncle Ismāʿīl." Then he greeted him in Hebrew, and the king said, "What language is this?" He said, "The language of my fathers."

Wahb said: the king used to speak seventy languages. Whenever he spoke to Yusuf in one language, Yusuf answered him in that language, and the king was pleased. The king was astonished at what he saw of him. Yusuf was then thirty years old. When the king saw his youthfulness, he said to those with him: "This is the knowledge of the interpretation of my dream, which the magicians and soothsayers did not know." Then he seated him on his throne and said to him: "I wish to hear my dream from you directly." Yusuf said to him, "Yes, O king. You saw seven fat cows, white, bright and handsome, whom the Nile revealed to you; they came up to you from its bank, their udders dripping milk. While you were looking at them and marvelling at their beauty, the Nile subsided, its water receded and it became dry. Out of its mud and slime came seven lean cows, dishevelled, dusty, with shrunken bellies, having no udders or teats, with fangs and molars, paws like dogs' paws, and snouts like those of beasts. Fire then broke out among them, burned them, and they became black and changed.

That is the last of what you saw of the world. Then you awoke from your sleep in alarm." The king said, "By God, what is the matter with this dream? Though it is strange, it is no stranger than what I have heard from you. So what do you see in my dream, O truthful one?" Yusuf said: "I advise that you gather food and sow abundant crops in these fruitful years, and build [storehouses] and treasuries, and place the grain in them with its stalk and ear, so that its stalk and ear become fodder for the animals. Command the people to set aside a fifth of their produce, and it will suffice you, from the food you have gathered, for the people of Egypt and those around it. People will come to you from all regions seeking grain, and treasures will gather with you that have not gathered for anyone before you."

The king said, "Who can do this for me, and who will gather it, [sell it] and take up the task of managing it?" Yusuf said: ﴿"Set me over the storehouses of the land"﴾. The figurative meaning of the verse is: over the storehouses of your land. "And dreams are not false."

﴿Indeed, I am a guardian, knowing.﴾ Meaning: a writer and reckoner. Qatāda: "Guardian of what I am entrusted with, knowing of its affairs." Ibn Isḥāq: "Guardian of what you have entrusted to me, knowing of what you have appointed me to." Shayba al-Ḍabbī: "Guardian of what you have entrusted to me, and knowing of the years of famine." It has also been said: "Guardian of what has reached me, knowing of its accounting of wealth."

The king said to him, "Who is more deserving of it than you?" So he appointed him to that office and said to him: ﴿"Indeed, today you are with us established and trusted,"﴾ possessing rank and standing, trustworthy over the treasuries.

Juwaybir narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "May God have mercy on my brother Yusuf. Had he not said, ﴿Set me over the storehouses of the land﴾, he would have employed him immediately. But he delayed that for a year, so he remained with him in his house for a year, with the king." [121] [[Zād al-Masīr: 4/185; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 9/211.]]

Sufyān narrated from Abū Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl, who said: The king said to Yusuf: "I want you to mix with me in everything, except that I disdain that you should eat with me." Yusuf (peace be upon him) said: "I have more right to disdain it. I am the son of Yaʿqūb, Isrāʾīl of God, son of Isḥāq, the sacrificed one of God, son of Ibrāhīm, the friend of God." So from then on he ate with him.

Ḥamza al-Rayyān narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Maysara, who said: When the ʿAzīz saw Yusuf's opinion and his refinement, he invited him, and he used to lunch and dine with him apart from his servants. When what happened between him and the woman happened, she said to him once, "Let him lunch with the servants." So he said, "Go and lunch with the servants." Yusuf said to him to his face: "Have you disdained to eat with me? I am, by God, Yusuf son of Yaʿqūb, the prophet of God, son of Isḥāq, the sacrificed one of God, son of Ibrāhīm, the friend of God."

Muqātil narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb offered Abū Hurayra the governorship, and he said: "I will not do it, nor do I want it. I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever seeks leadership will not act justly.'" [122] [[In Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ (12/94): "Whoever is eager for leadership will not act justly in it."]] ʿUmar said: "Indeed, one better than you sought leadership: Yusuf (peace be upon him), who said, ﴿Set me over the storehouses of the land﴾."

Ibn Isḥāq narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When a year had passed since the day he asked for the governorship, the king summoned him, crowned him, girded him with his sword, and placed for him a golden throne adorned with pearls and rubies, and draped over it a silk brocade. The throne was thirty cubits long and ten cubits wide, with thirty mattresses and ninety cushions on it. Then he ordered him to go out, and he went out crowned, his complexion like snow and his face like the moon, so that the beholder could see his face in the clarity of its colour. He went and sat on the throne, and the kings submitted to him. The king entered his house with his women and entrusted to him the affairs of Egypt, removing Qiṭfīr from what he had been over and placing Yusuf in his position.

Ibn Isḥāq said: Ibn Zayd said: Pharaoh, king of Egypt, had many treasuries besides the food, so he handed over all his authority to him and made his command and judgement binding. Then Qiṭfīr died during those nights, and the king married Yusuf to Rāḥīl, the wife of Qiṭfīr. When he entered upon her, he said, "Is this not better than what you used to desire?" She said: "O truthful one, do not blame me, for I was a beautiful, pampered woman, as you see, in wealth and luxury, and my husband did not come near women. I was as God made you in your beauty and form, and my self overcame me." Yusuf found her to be a virgin, and he had intercourse with her, and she bore him two sons: Ifrāʾīm son of Yusuf and Manashā son of Yusuf.

The rule of Egypt became settled for Yusuf, and he established justice among them, so men and women loved him. This is God's saying:

﴿And thus did We establish Yusuf in the land﴾, meaning the land of Egypt, that is, We gave him authority there, ﴿to settle therein wherever he willed﴾, and to act in it as he wished. "Tabawwu'" means to dwell; it is said "bawwa'tuhu" and "tabawwa'a." The reading of the people of Mecca is "nashāʾ" (we will) with a nūn, in response to His saying "makkannā" and what follows it: ﴿We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will﴾, that is, by Our favour.

﴿And We do not waste the reward of the good-doers.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbās and Wahb said: that is, the patient, like his patience in the well, his patience in prison, his patience in servitude, and his patience against what the woman invited him to. Mujāhid and others said: he continued to supplicate and to be gentle with him until the king and many people became Muslim. This is in this world. ﴿And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believed and were mindful of God.﴾ Al-Buḥturī said:

"Is there not in the Messenger of God, Yusuf, an example for one like you, imprisoned [....]"
[[An illegible word.]]

"He persisted in beautiful patience in confinement for a time, until beautiful patience brought him to the king."
[[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 9/220.]]

One of them wrote to a friend of his:

"Beyond the narrow passage of fear is the wide expanse of safety, and the first joy is followed by the last sorrow.
So do not despair, for God has granted Yusuf his treasuries after his release from prison."
[[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 9/220, where it reads "the end of sorrow" instead of "the last sorrow."]]

They said: When Joseph was firmly established in his rule, the years of abundance came, and then the years of drought came. Hunger afflicted the people, and those years came [.......] [[Unreadable word.]] The beginning of the famine was this: one night, while the king was in the middle of the night, hunger struck him, and the king cried out: "O Joseph, hunger! Hunger!" He said: "This is the first of the famine." When the first year of the lean years arrived, everything they had stored up during the years of plenty was destroyed. The people of Egypt began to buy food from Joseph. In the first year he sold it to them for money, until no dinar or dirham remained in Egypt that he had not taken. In the second year he sold it to them for jewelry and precious stones, until none of these remained in the people's hands. In the third year he sold it to them for livestock and beasts, until he had gathered all of them. In the fourth year he sold it to them for slaves, male and female, until no male or female slave remained in anyone's possession. Then in the fifth year he sold them lands, estates and houses, until he had taken possession of them. In the sixth year he sold them their children, until he had enslaved them. In the seventh year he sold them their very persons, until no free man or free woman remained in Egypt who had not become his slave. People said: "By God, we have never seen a king greater or more majestic than this." Then Joseph said to Pharaoh: "How do you see the handiwork of my Lord in what He has entrusted to me? What do you think I should do?" The king said: "The decision is yours, and we are only your followers." He said: "I call on you both to witness that I have freed the people of Egypt, all of them, and returned to them their wealth and their property."

It is narrated that Joseph (peace be upon him) would not eat his fill of food during those days. It was said to him: "You go hungry while the treasuries of the earth are in your hand?" He said: "I fear that if I am sated I will forget the hungry." Joseph also ordered the king's cooks to make the morning meal at midday, intending by this that the king should taste the experience of hunger and not forget the hungry, and that he would be kind to the needy. The cooks did so, and from that time kings have made their midday meal at noon.

They said: People came to Egypt from every far-off place to obtain provisions. Joseph would not allow anyone, even a great man, to take more than a camel's load, distributing among the people and making things easier for them, and the people crowded upon him.

They said: The land of Canaan and the lands of Syria were struck by the famine and hardship that struck all the other lands, and what had befallen the people also befell Jacob. So he sent his sons to Egypt to obtain provisions, and he kept back Benjamin, the full brother of Joseph. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿The brothers of Joseph came and they were ten﴾. Their dwelling was in the outskirts of the land of Palestine, the frontier regions of Syria, and they were people of the desert, with camels and sheep. ﴿They entered upon him, and Joseph recognized them﴾, but they did not recognize him, because God willed that Joseph should attain what He had willed.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Between the time they threw him into the well and the time they entered Egypt there were forty years, and therefore they did not recognize him. It was also said that he was dressed in the garb of the Pharaoh of Egypt, wearing silk garments, seated on his throne, with a gold collar around his neck and a crown on his head, and therefore they did not recognize him. There was also a curtain between him and them, and for this reason they did not recognize him.

Some of the wise said: Sin inherits arrogance. God Almighty said: ﴿He recognized them, but they were unaware of him﴾. When Joseph looked at them and they spoke to him in Hebrew, he said to them: "Tell me, who are you and what is your business? For I am observing your situation." They said: "We are a people from the Syrian region, shepherds, struck by hardship, so we have come to seek provisions." He said: "Perhaps you are spies, looking for the weak points of my land." They said: "By God, we are not spies. We are brothers, sons of one father, who is an aged, truthful man called Jacob, a prophet among the prophets of God." He said: "And how many are you?"

They said: "We were twelve. One of our brothers went out into the wilderness and perished there, and he was the dearest of us to our father." He said: "So how many of you are here?" They said: "Ten." He said: "Where is the other one?" They said: "He is with our father, for he is the full brother of the one who perished, and our father takes comfort in him." He said: "Who will know that what you say is true?" They said: "O King, we are in a land where no one knows us." Joseph said: "Then bring me your brother who is from your father, if you are truthful, for I am content with that."

They said: "Our father grieves at his separation from him, and we will try to persuade him to let him go, and we will surely do so." He said: "Then leave one of you with me as a pledge until you bring me your brother." They cast lots among themselves, and the lot fell upon Shimʿun, who was the best of them in judgment regarding Joseph and the most dutiful to him, so they left him with him. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿When he had provided them with their provisions﴾, that is, he gave each man a camel's load according to their number. ﴿He said: "Bring me a brother of yours from your father"﴾, that is, Benjamin. ﴿"Do you not see that I give full measure, and I am the best of hosts?"﴾ That is, I do not defraud people of anything, and I complete their measure for them, and I add a camel's load to your provision, and I honour your lodging and treat you well, and I am the best of those who host.

﴿"But if you do not bring him to me, there will be no measure for you with me, and you shall not come near me."﴾ That is, you will have no food from me to measure out for you, and you shall not come near my land after that. The verb here is in the jussive, which indicates a prohibition.

﴿They said: "We will seek to persuade our father about him"﴾, that is, we will seek him and ask him to send him with us. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "We will deceive him until we bring him out with us." ﴿"And we will surely do it."﴾ That is, what you have commanded.

﴿And Joseph said to his attendants﴾, that is, to his servants who worked with the provisions. al-Hasan, Humayd, Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi and Hafs read ﴿lifityānihi﴾ with alif and nūn, and this is the choice of Abu ʿUbayda, who said: it is written thus in the codex of ʿAbd Allah. The rest read ﴿lifitayatihi﴾ with the tāʾ and without alif. Both are dialectal forms, like al-ṣibyān and al-ṣibyah.

﴿Put their merchandise﴾, that is, their provisions. Qatada said: their silver. al-Ḍaḥḥak reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: it was leather and hides. ﴿into their saddlebags﴾, that is, into their containers. The word is the plural of raḥl, and the plural of paucity of it is ruḥayl. Ibn al-Anbari said: raḥl is used for a container, and also for a dwelling.

﴿So that they may recognize it when they return﴾, that is, when they go back ﴿to their family, so that they may come back to me﴾. The scholars differed concerning the reason for which Joseph did this. al-Kalbi said: Joseph feared that his father would not have silver, and then they would not return a second time. It was also said: he feared that taking it would harm them in their father's eyes, since it was a year of dearth and famine, so he wished to return it to them, intending that his father should be well provided for. It was also said: he saw that if he took the price of the food from his father and his brothers, despite their need for it, and then returned it to them without their knowing, it would be generosity and bounty. It was also said: he did this because he knew that their piety and trustworthiness would compel them to return the merchandise and not regard keeping it as lawful, and so they would come back for its sake. It was also said: he displayed his generosity in returning the merchandise and in guaranteeing their safe conduct, in goodness and kindness, so that they would be more inclined to return to him, hoping for his kindness.

When they returned to their father they said: "O our father, we have come before the best of men, who lodged us and honoured us with honour. Had he been a man from among the sons of Jacob, he would not have honoured us as he did." Jacob said to them: "When you come to the king in Egypt, convey my greetings to him and say: 'Our father sends blessings upon you and prays for you for what you have bestowed upon us.'" Then he said: "Where is Shimʿun?" They said: "He is with the king of Egypt." And they informed him of the story. He said: "And why did you inform him?" They said: "He seized us, and when we spoke to him in the language of the Hebrews he said: 'You are spies.'" And they related the story to him.

﴿They said: "O our father, the measure has been denied us, so send our brother Benjamin with us, and we shall receive measure"﴾. Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read ﴿yaktal﴾ with yāʾ, meaning he himself will receive measure, as we used to receive it. The others read it with nūn, meaning "we shall receive measure," and this is what Abu ʿUbayd chose. ﴿"And we will surely guard him."﴾

Jacob said: ﴿"Shall I trust you with him except as I trusted you with his brother Joseph before? God is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ al-Aʿmash, Ibn Muḥaysin, Yahya, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read ﴿ḥāfiẓan﴾ with alif, as a specification of explanation, as one says: "He is better as a man." The meaning of the verse is: "God is better than you as a guardian," so the kāf and mīm are omitted. What supports this is that it is written in the codex of ʿAbd Allah as: "God is the best of the guardians." The others read ﴿ḥifẓan﴾ without alif, as a verbal noun, meaning "God is better than you in guarding," and there is a difference of reading regarding this from ʿAsim.

When they opened their goods, which they had carried from Egypt, they found their merchandise, the price of the food, returned to them. They said: ﴿"O our father, what more could we desire? This is our merchandise, returned to us. We shall provide for our family, guard our brother Benjamin, and receive an extra camel's load, which is an easy measure."﴾ That is, ﴿"what more could we desire"﴾: what are we seeking, and what more do we want beyond this? The measure has been fulfilled for us and the price returned to us. They intended by this to console their father's heart. The word "mā" here is interrogative in a position of accusative, and its meaning is denial, as if they said: "We do not want dirhams from you."

﴿"This is our merchandise, returned to us"﴾. ﴿"We shall provide for our family"﴾ means we shall buy food for them and carry it to them. One says māra ahlahu yamīru mayran, and he is māʾir, if he brings them their provisions from another land. In the same sense: imtāra yamtāru imtiyāran. A poet said:

"I sent you as a provider, and you stayed a full year;
when will your help come, you who are sought for help?"

Another said:

"He came to a village whose food was plentiful,
like the dust of a fox, all things being measured out to it."

﴿"And we shall guard our brother Benjamin, and we shall receive an extra camel's load for us"﴾, that is, on account of him. ﴿"That is an easy measure"﴾: there is no burden in it and no hardship. Mujahid said: ﴿kayla baʿīr﴾ means a donkey's load, and he said: this is a dialect, in which a donkey is called baʿīr.

Jacob said: ﴿"I will never send him with you until you give me a solemn pledge in God's name, that you will certainly bring him back to me"﴾, that is, you swear to me by the right of Muhammad, the seal of the prophets and the lord of the messengers, that you will not betray your brother. The lām came into it because the sense of the statement is an oath. ﴿"Unless you are overwhelmed"﴾, that is, unless you all perish. Mujahid said this. Qatada said: "Unless they are overpowered, so that they cannot manage it."

﴿When they gave him their solemn pledge﴾, that is, they gave him their covenant. Juwaybir reported from al-Ḍaḥḥak from Ibn ʿAbbas: they swore to him by the right of Muhammad ﷺ and his station with his Lord. Jacob said: ﴿"God is witness to what we say"﴾, that is, a witness and a guardian of the fulfilment. al-Qutaybi said: "a guarantor." Kaʿb said: When Jacob said: ﴿"God is the best guardian,"﴾ God, mighty is His remembrance, said: "By My might, I will surely return both of them to you after you have put your trust in Me."

Jacob also said to them when they wished to depart: [this], ﴿"O my sons, do not enter Egypt by one gate, but enter by different gates."﴾ That was because he feared the evil eye for them, since they were people of beauty, fine bearing, handsome forms and tall statures, and they were the sons of one man. He commanded them to separate in entering it. Then he said: ﴿"I cannot avail you anything against God. Judgment belongs to God alone; in Him I have put my trust, and in Him let all who trust put their trust."﴾ He (peace be upon him) knew that what is decreed will come to pass, and that caution does not avail against destiny. ﴿"I cannot avail you anything against God"﴾. ﴿"Judgment belongs to God alone; in Him I have put my trust, and in Him let all who trust put their trust."﴾ And let those who entrust their affairs entrust them to God.

﴿When they entered from the gate their father had commanded them﴾. Egypt had four gates, and they entered it through all its gates. ﴿It did not avail them anything against God, except for a need in Jacob's soul that he fulfilled﴾: he was concerned about them with the concern of fathers for their sons. ﴿Truly he was a man of knowledge, by what We had taught him﴾, that is, through what We had taught him, meaning, for Our teaching him. Qatada said this. Sufyan reported from Ibn Abi ʿUrwa, who said: he is one who acts upon what he knows. Sufyan said: one who does not act is not a scholar. It was also said: he was truly one of fortune in what We had taught him.

﴿But most people do not know﴾, that is, what Jacob knows, meaning they do not recognize his rank in knowledge.

When they entered upon Joseph, they said: "This is our brother whom you ordered us to bring you. We have brought him to you." He said to them: "You have done well and you have been right, and you will find that with me." Then he lodged them, honoured their lodging, and gave them hospitality, seating every two of them at a table. Benjamin was left alone, so he wept and said: "If my brother Joseph were alive, he would have seated me with him." Joseph (peace be upon him) said to them: "This your brother has been left alone," so he seated him at his table, and he began to eat with him.

When night came, he ordered for them bedding, that is, mattresses, and said: "Let every two of you sleep together on one mattress." When only Benjamin was left, Joseph (peace be upon him) said: "This one will sleep with me on my bed." So he spent the night with him, and Joseph embraced him and smelled his cheek until morning. Ruwbil began to say: "We have never seen anything like this." When morning came, he said to them: "I see that this man whom you have brought has no companion. I will take him to myself, so that his lodging will be with me." Then he lodged them, provided them with food and drink, and lodged his full brother with himself. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿He took his brother to himself﴾.

When he was alone with him he said: "What is your name?" He said: "Benjamin." He said: "Son of whom, Benjamin?" He said: "The son of the bereaved, because when he was born his mother died." He said: "And what was her name?" He said: "Rahil, daughter of Lawi ibn Nahur." He said: "Do you have sons?" He said: "Yes, ten sons, and I have derived their names from the name of a brother of mine by my mother who perished." He said: "Great grief must have compelled you to that." He said: "And what did you name them?" He said: "Bala, Akhira, Athkal, Ahya, Kanar, Nuʿman, Adar, Arus, Haytam, and Maytham." He said: "What are these?" He said: "As for Bala, my brother was swallowed by the earth. As for Akhira, he was the firstborn of my mother's children. As for Athkal, he was my brother by father and mother and my age. As for Kathir, he was the dearest beloved of all. As for Nuʿman, he was pampered between his parents. As for Adar, he was like the rose in beauty. He said: As for Arus, he was like the head of the body. As for Haytam, he informed me that he is alive, and as for Maytham, if I were to see him my eye would be comforted."

Joseph said: "Would you like me to be your brother in place of your lost brother?" Benjamin said: "And who would find a brother like you? But Jacob did not bear you, nor Rahil." Joseph (peace be upon him) wept, rose to him, embraced him, and said to him: ﴿"I am your brother, Joseph, so do not grieve over what they used to do"﴾, that is, do not grieve over what they did to us in the past, for God has been good to us, and do not tell them anything of what you have come to know.

ʿAbd al-Samad ibn Maʿqil said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih, when he was asked about Joseph's saying to his brother: ﴿"I am your brother"﴾. It was asked of him: "How did he make him his brother, when he seized him with the drinking cup, and he had already informed him that he was his brother? And you claim that he remained disguised before them, deceiving them, until they returned?" He said: "He did not acknowledge to him the kinship, but he said: 'I am your brother in place of your lost brother.'" al-Shaʿbi said the same. He said: "He did not say to him: 'I am Joseph,' but he wished to console him." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/21.]]

The meaning of the verse: ﴿"I am your brother"﴾ in place of your missing brother. ﴿"So do not grieve over what they used to do"﴾, that is, do not complain and do not grieve over what your brothers did to you in the past, in yourself and regarding your brother from your mother, and what they used to do to you before today. Then Joseph gave his brothers their full measure, and he loaded a camel for them, and he loaded a camel in Benjamin's name as he loaded for them. Then he ordered that the king's drinking cup be put into Benjamin's saddlebag. al-Suddi said: ﴿He put the cup into his brother's saddlebag﴾, and the brother did not perceive it.

Kaʿb said: When he said to him: ﴿"I am your brother,"﴾ Benjamin said: "Then I will not leave you." Joseph (peace be upon him) said: "You know my father's attachment to me. If I detain you, his grief will increase, and I cannot do this unless I make you notorious by a matter, and attribute to you what is not becoming of you." He said: "I do not mind; do whatever you wish, for I will not leave you."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 12, verses 58–71 (part 2 of 2):

He said: "Indeed, I will put my cup (sa') in your saddlebag, then I will call out against you that you are thieves, so that it is arranged for me to bring you back after I have sent you off." He said: "Do it." That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when he had furnished them with their provisions﴾, i.e., when he had fulfilled their needs. ﴿He put the drinking-cup (al-siqayah) into his brother's saddlebag﴾. Al-siqayah is the drinking vessel with which the king used to drink. Ibn Zayd said: "It was, as they mention, a cup of gold." Ibn Ishaq said: "It was something made of silver." Ikrimah said: "It was a drinking vessel of silver set with jewels. Yusuf made it the measuring vessel so that grain would not be measured with anything else, and he used to drink from it." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "It was the [measure] whose two ends meet, and the non-Arabs used to drink from it, and al-'Abbas had one of them in the pre-Islamic period." Al-siqayah and al-sa' (al-sawa') are one and the same. ﴿In his brother's saddlebag﴾, among the belongings of Binyamin. Then they set off, and Yusuf gave them time until they had departed and gone on; then he ordered them to be pursued, and they were apprehended and detained.

﴿Then a caller called out⦆: a crier shouted. ﴿O caravan!﴾: this is the caravan which carried the loads. Al-Farra' said: "'Ir is used only for owners of camels." Mujahid said: "The 'ir were donkeys."

﴿Indeed, you are thieves!﴾: halt! So they halted. When the messenger reached them, he said to them: "Did we not honour your hospitality, treat your lodging well, give you full measure, and do for you what we did not do for others?" They said: "Yes. But what is it?" He said: "The cup of the king." He said: "It is not suspected of anyone but you." That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, turning towards them: "What is it that you are missing?"﴾ They turned towards the crier and his companions: "What is it that you are missing? What has gone astray from you?" Al-fiqdan is the opposite of al-wujud (finding), and al-mafqad means the search.

They said: When Joseph was firmly established in his rule, the years of abundance came, and then the years of drought came. Hunger afflicted the people, and those years came [.......] [[Unreadable word.]] The beginning of the famine was this: one night, while the king was in the middle of the night, hunger struck him, and the king cried out: "O Joseph, hunger! Hunger!" He said: "This is the first of the famine." When the first year of the lean years arrived, everything they had stored up during the years of plenty was destroyed. The people of Egypt began to buy food from Joseph. In the first year he sold it to them for money, until no dinar or dirham remained in Egypt that he had not taken. In the second year he sold it to them for jewelry and precious stones, until none of these remained in the people's hands. In the third year he sold it to them for livestock and beasts, until he had gathered all of them. In the fourth year he sold it to them for slaves, male and female, until no male or female slave remained in anyone's possession. Then in the fifth year he sold them lands, estates and houses, until he had taken possession of them. In the sixth year he sold them their children, until he had enslaved them. In the seventh year he sold them their very persons, until no free man or free woman remained in Egypt who had not become his slave. People said: "By God, we have never seen a king greater or more majestic than this." Then Joseph said to Pharaoh: "How do you see the handiwork of my Lord in what He has entrusted to me? What do you think I should do?" The king said: "The decision is yours, and we are only your followers." He said: "I call on you both to witness that I have freed the people of Egypt, all of them, and returned to them their wealth and their property."

It is narrated that Joseph (peace be upon him) would not eat his fill of food during those days. It was said to him: "You go hungry while the treasuries of the earth are in your hand?" He said: "I fear that if I am sated I will forget the hungry." Joseph also ordered the king's cooks to make the morning meal at midday, intending by this that the king should taste the experience of hunger and not forget the hungry, and that he would be kind to the needy. The cooks did so, and from that time kings have made their midday meal at noon.

They said: People came to Egypt from every far-off place to obtain provisions. Joseph would not allow anyone, even a great man, to take more than a camel's load, distributing among the people and making things easier for them, and the people crowded upon him.

They said: The land of Canaan and the lands of Syria were struck by the famine and hardship that struck all the other lands, and what had befallen the people also befell Jacob. So he sent his sons to Egypt to obtain provisions, and he kept back Benjamin, the full brother of Joseph. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿The brothers of Joseph came and they were ten﴾. Their dwelling was in the outskirts of the land of Palestine, the frontier regions of Syria, and they were people of the desert, with camels and sheep. ﴿They entered upon him, and Joseph recognized them﴾, but they did not recognize him, because God willed that Joseph should attain what He had willed.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Between the time they threw him into the well and the time they entered Egypt there were forty years, and therefore they did not recognize him. It was also said that he was dressed in the garb of the Pharaoh of Egypt, wearing silk garments, seated on his throne, with a gold collar around his neck and a crown on his head, and therefore they did not recognize him. There was also a curtain between him and them, and for this reason they did not recognize him.

Some of the wise said: Sin inherits arrogance. God Almighty said: ﴿He recognized them, but they were unaware of him﴾. When Joseph looked at them and they spoke to him in Hebrew, he said to them: "Tell me, who are you and what is your business? For I am observing your situation." They said: "We are a people from the Syrian region, shepherds, struck by hardship, so we have come to seek provisions." He said: "Perhaps you are spies, looking for the weak points of my land." They said: "By God, we are not spies. We are brothers, sons of one father, who is an aged, truthful man called Jacob, a prophet among the prophets of God." He said: "And how many are you?"

They said: "We were twelve. One of our brothers went out into the wilderness and perished there, and he was the dearest of us to our father." He said: "So how many of you are here?" They said: "Ten." He said: "Where is the other one?" They said: "He is with our father, for he is the full brother of the one who perished, and our father takes comfort in him." He said: "Who will know that what you say is true?" They said: "O King, we are in a land where no one knows us." Joseph said: "Then bring me your brother who is from your father, if you are truthful, for I am content with that."

They said: "Our father grieves at his separation from him, and we will try to persuade him to let him go, and we will surely do so." He said: "Then leave one of you with me as a pledge until you bring me your brother." They cast lots among themselves, and the lot fell upon Shimʿun, who was the best of them in judgment regarding Joseph and the most dutiful to him, so they left him with him. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿When he had provided them with their provisions﴾, that is, he gave each man a camel's load according to their number. ﴿He said: "Bring me a brother of yours from your father"﴾, that is, Benjamin. ﴿"Do you not see that I give full measure, and I am the best of hosts?"﴾ That is, I do not defraud people of anything, and I complete their measure for them, and I add a camel's load to your provision, and I honour your lodging and treat you well, and I am the best of those who host.

﴿"But if you do not bring him to me, there will be no measure for you with me, and you shall not come near me."﴾ That is, you will have no food from me to measure out for you, and you shall not come near my land after that. The verb here is in the jussive, which indicates a prohibition.

﴿They said: "We will seek to persuade our father about him"﴾, that is, we will seek him and ask him to send him with us. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "We will deceive him until we bring him out with us." ﴿"And we will surely do it."﴾ That is, what you have commanded.

﴿And Joseph said to his attendants﴾, that is, to his servants who worked with the provisions. al-Hasan, Humayd, Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi and Hafs read ﴿lifityānihi﴾ with alif and nūn, and this is the choice of Abu ʿUbayda, who said: it is written thus in the codex of ʿAbd Allah. The rest read ﴿lifitayatihi﴾ with the tāʾ and without alif. Both are dialectal forms, like al-ṣibyān and al-ṣibyah.

﴿Put their merchandise﴾, that is, their provisions. Qatada said: their silver. al-Ḍaḥḥak reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: it was leather and hides. ﴿into their saddlebags﴾, that is, into their containers. The word is the plural of raḥl, and the plural of paucity of it is ruḥayl. Ibn al-Anbari said: raḥl is used for a container, and also for a dwelling.

﴿So that they may recognize it when they return﴾, that is, when they go back ﴿to their family, so that they may come back to me﴾. The scholars differed concerning the reason for which Joseph did this. al-Kalbi said: Joseph feared that his father would not have silver, and then they would not return a second time. It was also said: he feared that taking it would harm them in their father's eyes, since it was a year of dearth and famine, so he wished to return it to them, intending that his father should be well provided for. It was also said: he saw that if he took the price of the food from his father and his brothers, despite their need for it, and then returned it to them without their knowing, it would be generosity and bounty. It was also said: he did this because he knew that their piety and trustworthiness would compel them to return the merchandise and not regard keeping it as lawful, and so they would come back for its sake. It was also said: he displayed his generosity in returning the merchandise and in guaranteeing their safe conduct, in goodness and kindness, so that they would be more inclined to return to him, hoping for his kindness.

When they returned to their father they said: "O our father, we have come before the best of men, who lodged us and honoured us with honour. Had he been a man from among the sons of Jacob, he would not have honoured us as he did." Jacob said to them: "When you come to the king in Egypt, convey my greetings to him and say: 'Our father sends blessings upon you and prays for you for what you have bestowed upon us.'" Then he said: "Where is Shimʿun?" They said: "He is with the king of Egypt." And they informed him of the story. He said: "And why did you inform him?" They said: "He seized us, and when we spoke to him in the language of the Hebrews he said: 'You are spies.'" And they related the story to him.

﴿They said: "O our father, the measure has been denied us, so send our brother Benjamin with us, and we shall receive measure"﴾. Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read ﴿yaktal﴾ with yāʾ, meaning he himself will receive measure, as we used to receive it. The others read it with nūn, meaning "we shall receive measure," and this is what Abu ʿUbayd chose. ﴿"And we will surely guard him."﴾

Jacob said: ﴿"Shall I trust you with him except as I trusted you with his brother Joseph before? God is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ al-Aʿmash, Ibn Muḥaysin, Yahya, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read ﴿ḥāfiẓan﴾ with alif, as a specification of explanation, as one says: "He is better as a man." The meaning of the verse is: "God is better than you as a guardian," so the kāf and mīm are omitted. What supports this is that it is written in the codex of ʿAbd Allah as: "God is the best of the guardians." The others read ﴿ḥifẓan﴾ without alif, as a verbal noun, meaning "God is better than you in guarding," and there is a difference of reading regarding this from ʿAsim.

When they opened their goods, which they had carried from Egypt, they found their merchandise, the price of the food, returned to them. They said: ﴿"O our father, what more could we desire? This is our merchandise, returned to us. We shall provide for our family, guard our brother Benjamin, and receive an extra camel's load, which is an easy measure."﴾ That is, ﴿"what more could we desire"﴾: what are we seeking, and what more do we want beyond this? The measure has been fulfilled for us and the price returned to us. They intended by this to console their father's heart. The word "mā" here is interrogative in a position of accusative, and its meaning is denial, as if they said: "We do not want dirhams from you."

﴿"This is our merchandise, returned to us"﴾. ﴿"We shall provide for our family"﴾ means we shall buy food for them and carry it to them. One says māra ahlahu yamīru mayran, and he is māʾir, if he brings them their provisions from another land. In the same sense: imtāra yamtāru imtiyāran. A poet said:

"I sent you as a provider, and you stayed a full year;
when will your help come, you who are sought for help?"

Another said:

"He came to a village whose food was plentiful,
like the dust of a fox, all things being measured out to it."

﴿"And we shall guard our brother Benjamin, and we shall receive an extra camel's load for us"﴾, that is, on account of him. ﴿"That is an easy measure"﴾: there is no burden in it and no hardship. Mujahid said: ﴿kayla baʿīr﴾ means a donkey's load, and he said: this is a dialect, in which a donkey is called baʿīr.

Jacob said: ﴿"I will never send him with you until you give me a solemn pledge in God's name, that you will certainly bring him back to me"﴾, that is, you swear to me by the right of Muhammad, the seal of the prophets and the lord of the messengers, that you will not betray your brother. The lām came into it because the sense of the statement is an oath. ﴿"Unless you are overwhelmed"﴾, that is, unless you all perish. Mujahid said this. Qatada said: "Unless they are overpowered, so that they cannot manage it."

﴿When they gave him their solemn pledge﴾, that is, they gave him their covenant. Juwaybir reported from al-Ḍaḥḥak from Ibn ʿAbbas: they swore to him by the right of Muhammad ﷺ and his station with his Lord. Jacob said: ﴿"God is witness to what we say"﴾, that is, a witness and a guardian of the fulfilment. al-Qutaybi said: "a guarantor." Kaʿb said: When Jacob said: ﴿"God is the best guardian,"﴾ God, mighty is His remembrance, said: "By My might, I will surely return both of them to you after you have put your trust in Me."

Jacob also said to them when they wished to depart: [this], ﴿"O my sons, do not enter Egypt by one gate, but enter by different gates."﴾ That was because he feared the evil eye for them, since they were people of beauty, fine bearing, handsome forms and tall statures, and they were the sons of one man. He commanded them to separate in entering it. Then he said: ﴿"I cannot avail you anything against God. Judgment belongs to God alone; in Him I have put my trust, and in Him let all who trust put their trust."﴾ He (peace be upon him) knew that what is decreed will come to pass, and that caution does not avail against destiny. ﴿"I cannot avail you anything against God"﴾. ﴿"Judgment belongs to God alone; in Him I have put my trust, and in Him let all who trust put their trust."﴾ And let those who entrust their affairs entrust them to God.

﴿When they entered from the gate their father had commanded them﴾. Egypt had four gates, and they entered it through all its gates. ﴿It did not avail them anything against God, except for a need in Jacob's soul that he fulfilled﴾: he was concerned about them with the concern of fathers for their sons. ﴿Truly he was a man of knowledge, by what We had taught him﴾, that is, through what We had taught him, meaning, for Our teaching him. Qatada said this. Sufyan reported from Ibn Abi ʿUrwa, who said: he is one who acts upon what he knows. Sufyan said: one who does not act is not a scholar. It was also said: he was truly one of fortune in what We had taught him.

﴿But most people do not know﴾, that is, what Jacob knows, meaning they do not recognize his rank in knowledge.

When they entered upon Joseph, they said: "This is our brother whom you ordered us to bring you. We have brought him to you." He said to them: "You have done well and you have been right, and you will find that with me." Then he lodged them, honoured their lodging, and gave them hospitality, seating every two of them at a table. Benjamin was left alone, so he wept and said: "If my brother Joseph were alive, he would have seated me with him." Joseph (peace be upon him) said to them: "This your brother has been left alone," so he seated him at his table, and he began to eat with him.

When night came, he ordered for them bedding, that is, mattresses, and said: "Let every two of you sleep together on one mattress." When only Benjamin was left, Joseph (peace be upon him) said: "This one will sleep with me on my bed." So he spent the night with him, and Joseph embraced him and smelled his cheek until morning. Ruwbil began to say: "We have never seen anything like this." When morning came, he said to them: "I see that this man whom you have brought has no companion. I will take him to myself, so that his lodging will be with me." Then he lodged them, provided them with food and drink, and lodged his full brother with himself. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿He took his brother to himself﴾.

When he was alone with him he said: "What is your name?" He said: "Benjamin." He said: "Son of whom, Benjamin?" He said: "The son of the bereaved, because when he was born his mother died." He said: "And what was her name?" He said: "Rahil, daughter of Lawi ibn Nahur." He said: "Do you have sons?" He said: "Yes, ten sons, and I have derived their names from the name of a brother of mine by my mother who perished." He said: "Great grief must have compelled you to that." He said: "And what did you name them?" He said: "Bala, Akhira, Athkal, Ahya, Kanar, Nuʿman, Adar, Arus, Haytam, and Maytham." He said: "What are these?" He said: "As for Bala, my brother was swallowed by the earth. As for Akhira, he was the firstborn of my mother's children. As for Athkal, he was my brother by father and mother and my age. As for Kathir, he was the dearest beloved of all. As for Nuʿman, he was pampered between his parents. As for Adar, he was like the rose in beauty. He said: As for Arus, he was like the head of the body. As for Haytam, he informed me that he is alive, and as for Maytham, if I were to see him my eye would be comforted."

Joseph said: "Would you like me to be your brother in place of your lost brother?" Benjamin said: "And who would find a brother like you? But Jacob did not bear you, nor Rahil." Joseph (peace be upon him) wept, rose to him, embraced him, and said to him: ﴿"I am your brother, Joseph, so do not grieve over what they used to do"﴾, that is, do not grieve over what they did to us in the past, for God has been good to us, and do not tell them anything of what you have come to know.

ʿAbd al-Samad ibn Maʿqil said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih, when he was asked about Joseph's saying to his brother: ﴿"I am your brother"﴾. It was asked of him: "How did he make him his brother, when he seized him with the drinking cup, and he had already informed him that he was his brother? And you claim that he remained disguised before them, deceiving them, until they returned?" He said: "He did not acknowledge to him the kinship, but he said: 'I am your brother in place of your lost brother.'" al-Shaʿbi said the same. He said: "He did not say to him: 'I am Joseph,' but he wished to console him." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/21.]]

The meaning of the verse: ﴿"I am your brother"﴾ in place of your missing brother. ﴿"So do not grieve over what they used to do"﴾, that is, do not complain and do not grieve over what your brothers did to you in the past, in yourself and regarding your brother from your mother, and what they used to do to you before today. Then Joseph gave his brothers their full measure, and he loaded a camel for them, and he loaded a camel in Benjamin's name as he loaded for them. Then he ordered that the king's drinking cup be put into Benjamin's saddlebag. al-Suddi said: ﴿He put the cup into his brother's saddlebag﴾, and the brother did not perceive it.

Kaʿb said: When he said to him: ﴿"I am your brother,"﴾ Benjamin said: "Then I will not leave you." Joseph (peace be upon him) said: "You know my father's attachment to me. If I detain you, his grief will increase, and I cannot do this unless I make you notorious by a matter, and attribute to you what is not becoming of you." He said: "I do not mind; do whatever you wish, for I will not leave you."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 12, verses 58–71 (part 2 of 2):

He said: "Indeed, I will put my cup (sa') in your saddlebag, then I will call out against you that you are thieves, so that it is arranged for me to bring you back after I have sent you off." He said: "Do it." That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when he had furnished them with their provisions﴾, i.e., when he had fulfilled their needs. ﴿He put the drinking-cup (al-siqayah) into his brother's saddlebag﴾. Al-siqayah is the drinking vessel with which the king used to drink. Ibn Zayd said: "It was, as they mention, a cup of gold." Ibn Ishaq said: "It was something made of silver." Ikrimah said: "It was a drinking vessel of silver set with jewels. Yusuf made it the measuring vessel so that grain would not be measured with anything else, and he used to drink from it." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "It was the [measure] whose two ends meet, and the non-Arabs used to drink from it, and al-'Abbas had one of them in the pre-Islamic period." Al-siqayah and al-sa' (al-sawa') are one and the same. ﴿In his brother's saddlebag﴾, among the belongings of Binyamin. Then they set off, and Yusuf gave them time until they had departed and gone on; then he ordered them to be pursued, and they were apprehended and detained.

﴿Then a caller called out⦆: a crier shouted. ﴿O caravan!﴾: this is the caravan which carried the loads. Al-Farra' said: "'Ir is used only for owners of camels." Mujahid said: "The 'ir were donkeys."

﴿Indeed, you are thieves!﴾: halt! So they halted. When the messenger reached them, he said to them: "Did we not honour your hospitality, treat your lodging well, give you full measure, and do for you what we did not do for others?" They said: "Yes. But what is it?" He said: "The cup of the king." He said: "It is not suspected of anyone but you." That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, turning towards them: "What is it that you are missing?"﴾ They turned towards the crier and his companions: "What is it that you are missing? What has gone astray from you?" Al-fiqdan is the opposite of al-wujud (finding), and al-mafqad means the search.

They said: When Joseph was firmly established in his rule, the years of abundance came, and then the years of drought came. Hunger afflicted the people, and those years came [.......] [[Unreadable word.]] The beginning of the famine was this: one night, while the king was in the middle of the night, hunger struck him, and the king cried out: "O Joseph, hunger! Hunger!" He said: "This is the first of the famine." When the first year of the lean years arrived, everything they had stored up during the years of plenty was destroyed. The people of Egypt began to buy food from Joseph. In the first year he sold it to them for money, until no dinar or dirham remained in Egypt that he had not taken. In the second year he sold it to them for jewelry and precious stones, until none of these remained in the people's hands. In the third year he sold it to them for livestock and beasts, until he had gathered all of them. In the fourth year he sold it to them for slaves, male and female, until no male or female slave remained in anyone's possession. Then in the fifth year he sold them lands, estates and houses, until he had taken possession of them. In the sixth year he sold them their children, until he had enslaved them. In the seventh year he sold them their very persons, until no free man or free woman remained in Egypt who had not become his slave. People said: "By God, we have never seen a king greater or more majestic than this." Then Joseph said to Pharaoh: "How do you see the handiwork of my Lord in what He has entrusted to me? What do you think I should do?" The king said: "The decision is yours, and we are only your followers." He said: "I call on you both to witness that I have freed the people of Egypt, all of them, and returned to them their wealth and their property."

It is narrated that Joseph (peace be upon him) would not eat his fill of food during those days. It was said to him: "You go hungry while the treasuries of the earth are in your hand?" He said: "I fear that if I am sated I will forget the hungry." Joseph also ordered the king's cooks to make the morning meal at midday, intending by this that the king should taste the experience of hunger and not forget the hungry, and that he would be kind to the needy. The cooks did so, and from that time kings have made their midday meal at noon.

They said: People came to Egypt from every far-off place to obtain provisions. Joseph would not allow anyone, even a great man, to take more than a camel's load, distributing among the people and making things easier for them, and the people crowded upon him.

They said: The land of Canaan and the lands of Syria were struck by the famine and hardship that struck all the other lands, and what had befallen the people also befell Jacob. So he sent his sons to Egypt to obtain provisions, and he kept back Benjamin, the full brother of Joseph. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿The brothers of Joseph came and they were ten﴾. Their dwelling was in the outskirts of the land of Palestine, the frontier regions of Syria, and they were people of the desert, with camels and sheep. ﴿They entered upon him, and Joseph recognized them﴾, but they did not recognize him, because God willed that Joseph should attain what He had willed.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Between the time they threw him into the well and the time they entered Egypt there were forty years, and therefore they did not recognize him. It was also said that he was dressed in the garb of the Pharaoh of Egypt, wearing silk garments, seated on his throne, with a gold collar around his neck and a crown on his head, and therefore they did not recognize him. There was also a curtain between him and them, and for this reason they did not recognize him.

Some of the wise said: Sin inherits arrogance. God Almighty said: ﴿He recognized them, but they were unaware of him﴾. When Joseph looked at them and they spoke to him in Hebrew, he said to them: "Tell me, who are you and what is your business? For I am observing your situation." They said: "We are a people from the Syrian region, shepherds, struck by hardship, so we have come to seek provisions." He said: "Perhaps you are spies, looking for the weak points of my land." They said: "By God, we are not spies. We are brothers, sons of one father, who is an aged, truthful man called Jacob, a prophet among the prophets of God." He said: "And how many are you?"

They said: "We were twelve. One of our brothers went out into the wilderness and perished there, and he was the dearest of us to our father." He said: "So how many of you are here?" They said: "Ten." He said: "Where is the other one?" They said: "He is with our father, for he is the full brother of the one who perished, and our father takes comfort in him." He said: "Who will know that what you say is true?" They said: "O King, we are in a land where no one knows us." Joseph said: "Then bring me your brother who is from your father, if you are truthful, for I am content with that."

They said: "Our father grieves at his separation from him, and we will try to persuade him to let him go, and we will surely do so." He said: "Then leave one of you with me as a pledge until you bring me your brother." They cast lots among themselves, and the lot fell upon Shimʿun, who was the best of them in judgment regarding Joseph and the most dutiful to him, so they left him with him. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿When he had provided them with their provisions﴾, that is, he gave each man a camel's load according to their number. ﴿He said: "Bring me a brother of yours from your father"﴾, that is, Benjamin. ﴿"Do you not see that I give full measure, and I am the best of hosts?"﴾ That is, I do not defraud people of anything, and I complete their measure for them, and I add a camel's load to your provision, and I honour your lodging and treat you well, and I am the best of those who host.

﴿"But if you do not bring him to me, there will be no measure for you with me, and you shall not come near me."﴾ That is, you will have no food from me to measure out for you, and you shall not come near my land after that. The verb here is in the jussive, which indicates a prohibition.

﴿They said: "We will seek to persuade our father about him"﴾, that is, we will seek him and ask him to send him with us. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "We will deceive him until we bring him out with us." ﴿"And we will surely do it."﴾ That is, what you have commanded.

﴿And Joseph said to his attendants﴾, that is, to his servants who worked with the provisions. al-Hasan, Humayd, Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi and Hafs read ﴿lifityānihi﴾ with alif and nūn, and this is the choice of Abu ʿUbayda, who said: it is written thus in the codex of ʿAbd Allah. The word is the plural of raḥl, and the plural of paucity of it is ruḥayl. Ibn al-Anbari said: raḥl is used for a container, and also for a dwelling.

﴿So that they may recognize it when they return﴾, that is, when they go back ﴿to their family, so that they may come back to me﴾. The scholars differed concerning the reason for which Joseph did this. al-Kalbi said: Joseph feared that his father would not have silver, and then they would not return a second time. It was also said: he feared that taking it would harm them in their father's eyes, since it was a year of dearth and famine, so he wished to return it to them, intending that his father should be well provided for. It was also said: he displayed his generosity in returning the merchandise and in guaranteeing their safe conduct, in goodness and kindness, so that they would be more inclined to return to him, hoping for his kindness.

When they returned to their father they said: "O our father, we have come before the best of men, who lodged us and honoured us with honour. Had he been a man from among the sons of Jacob, he would not have honoured us as he did." Jacob said to them: "When you come to the king in Egypt, convey my greetings to him and say: 'Our father sends blessings upon you and prays for you for what you have bestowed upon us.'" Then he said: "Where is Shimʿun?" They said: "He is with the king of Egypt." And they informed him of the story. He said: "And why did you inform him?" They said: "He seized us, and when we spoke to him in the language of the Hebrews he said: 'You are spies.'" And they related the story to him.

﴿They said: "O our father, the measure has been denied us, so send our brother Benjamin with us, and we shall receive measure"﴾. Yahya, al-Aʿmash, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read ﴿yaktal﴾ with yāʾ, meaning he himself will receive measure, as we used to receive it. The others read it with nūn, meaning "we shall receive measure," and this is what Abu ʿUbayd chose. ﴿"And we will surely guard him."﴾

Jacob said: ﴿"Shall I trust you with him except as I trusted you with his brother Joseph before? God is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."﴾ al-Aʿmash, Ibn Muḥaysin, Yahya, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read ﴿ḥāfiẓan﴾ with alif, as a specification of explanation, as one says: "He is better as a man."
