It was also said: "in" here means "when," like His saying: ﴿And leave what remains of usury, if you are believers﴾ [Sura al-Baqarah: 278], and His saying: ﴿You shall be the uppermost, if you are believers﴾ [Sura Al 'Imran: 139], and His saying: ﴿If they desire chastity﴾ [Sura al-Nur: 33].

Ibn 'Abbas said: He only said "in security" because in the past they had feared the kings of Egypt, and did not enter Egypt, for they had no permit. As for His saying "he took his parents to himself": Ibn Ishaq said: his father and his mother. Others said: his father and his maternal aunt, for Rachel, Joseph's mother, had died in childbirth, and Jacob afterward married her sister Liyya; so he called the aunt "mother," just as he called the paternal uncle "father" in His saying: ﴿We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac﴾.

Ishaq related from Bishr, from Sa'id, from al-Hasan, who said: God raised Rachel, Joseph's mother, from her grave until she prostrated, to fulfill the dream.

﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne﴾, on the couch; that is, he seated them upon it. Ibn Ishaq said: it means he raised their status. ﴿And they fell before him in prostration﴾: that is, Jacob, his aunt, and his brothers. At that time the greeting of people was prostration, and by prostration was not meant placing the forehead upon the ground, because that is not permitted except to God, Exalted; it is only bowing and humility as a form of greeting, honor, and salutation, except when it is done in the manner of worship and prayer. This is the saying of al-A'sha ibn Tha'labah:
"When he came to us after the sleep's absence, we prostrated to him and raised the turbans."
Another said:
"Its surplus reins prostrated, as Christians prostrate to their lords."
It was also said: prostration in language means submission, like the saying of al-Nabighah [in the source: Zayd al-Khayl instead of al-Nabighah]:
"With a host in whose lodges the spotted horses are lost; the hills in it are seen prostrating to the hooves."
That is, lowered and humbled.

[Tha'lab] said: "they fell" means "they passed by," and was not meant as falling down and dropping to the ground. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿They did not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾ [Sura al-Furqan: 73]; it only means they did not pass by in that manner. Mujahid: in the sense of passing. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that its meaning is: they fell down to God in prostration, so the "him" refers to God, Exalted.

Joseph then said, and his skin shivered: ﴿This is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true﴾, and that is His saying: ﴿Indeed I saw eleven stars﴾.

They differed about the length of Joseph's absence from Jacob. Al-Kalbi said: two hundred and twenty years. Salman al-Farisi: forty years. Abdullah ibn Shaddad: seventy years. It was also said: seventy-seven years. Al-Hasan said:
Joseph was thrown into the well at seventeen years of age, and was absent from his father eighty years, and lived after his reunion with Jacob twenty-three years, and died at the age of a hundred and twenty years. In the Torah: a hundred and sixteen years. According to Ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar: eighty-seven years. Ibn Abi Ishaq said: eighteen years. Joseph had from the wife of the Aziz: Ephraim, Menasseh, and Rahmah, wife of Job. Between Joseph and Moses were four hundred years.

﴿And He was good to me when He brought me out of the prison﴾; he did not say "out of the well," using courtesy, so as not to remind his brothers of their deed. It was also said: because God's blessing upon him in being saved from prison was greater than His blessing upon him in rescuing him from the well, for his falling into the well was due to his brothers' envy, while his imprisonment was a recompense from God for a slip that had come from him.

﴿And He brought you from the desert﴾, because Jacob and his sons were people of the desert and livestock. "Badw" is the verbal noun of your saying "badā, yabdū, badwan," when one becomes in the desert. ﴿After Satan had stirred discord between me and my brothers﴾. ﴿Indeed my Lord is Gentle, bestowing kindness on whom He wills﴾, knowing the subtleties of matters and their realities. ﴿Indeed He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾.

Abd al-Samad related from his father, from Wahb, who said: They—that is, Jacob and his sons—entered Egypt as seventy-two persons, men and women, and they left with Moses, and their number was six hundred and fifty-some thousand men, besides the offspring, the elderly, and the disabled; and the offspring were a million and two hundred thousand, besides the fighters.

The historians said: Jacob remained in Egypt after his family joined him for twenty-four years in the most pleasant condition and happiest life; then he died in Egypt. When death came to him, he bequeathed to his son Joseph that his body be carried until it was buried beside his father Isaac. Joseph did so, carried it, and buried him in Syria, then returned to Egypt.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he was transported in a chest of teak to Jerusalem, and that coincided with the day Esau died, and they were buried in one grave. Hence the Jews transport their dead to Jerusalem, those of them who do so. Jacob and Esau were born in one womb and buried in one grave, and their age together was a hundred and forty-seven years.

They said: When God gathered Joseph's family, fulfilled his vision, and cooled his eye, and had made his worldly kingdom and bliss expansive, he knew that this would not last for him and that he must part from it. He desired a bliss more enduring, and his soul longed for Paradise, so he wished for death and supplicated his Lord. No prophet before or after him wished for death, and he said: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom﴾, meaning the kingdom of Egypt, ﴿and taught me of the interpretation of events﴾, meaning the interpretation of dreams. ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their Creator and Maker.

﴿You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter﴾, my helper in this world and the Hereafter, managing my affairs. ﴿Cause me to die a Muslim, and join me with the righteous﴾, with my forefathers the prophets.

It was said: God took him in a good and pure state in Egypt, and he was buried in the Nile in a marble chest. When he died, people quarreled over him, each wanting to be buried in their own quarter, hoping for his blessing, until they gathered to fight. So they decided to bury him in the Nile at the place where the water divides in Egypt, so the water would flow over him and then reach all of Egypt, and they would all share in it equally. They did so.

Salih al-Murri related from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, gathered Jacob's family, his sons withdrew in private conversation. Some said to others: "Do you not know what you did, and what the old man suffered from you, and what Joseph suffered from you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then if they pardon you, but how will you face your Lord?" Their affair settled on coming to the old man, and they sat before him, with Joseph sitting beside his father.

They said: "O our father, we have come to you about a matter we have never come to you about before, and a calamity has befallen us the like of which has never befallen us," until they stirred him, and the prophets (upon them peace) are the most merciful of creatures. He said: "What is wrong with you, my sons?" They said: "Do you not know what we did to you, and what we did to our brother Joseph?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Have you not both pardoned?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Then your pardon will not avail us if God has not pardoned us." He said: "Then what do you want, my sons?" They said:

The sons said: "We want you to pray to God. When the revelation comes from God that He has pardoned them, we will have done it; our eyes will be comforted and our hearts will be at rest. Otherwise, there will never be any comfort for our eyes in this world." So the old man (al-Shaykh) faced the qibla and stood, and Yusuf stood behind his father, and they stood behind the two of them, humbled and submissive. Yaʿqub prayed, and Yusuf said "Amin," but He did not answer them for twenty years.

Salih al-Murri said: He kept them in fear. Then, when the twentieth year came, Jibril descended upon Yaʿqub and said:

"Indeed God, blessed and exalted, sent me to you to give you good news: He has answered your supplication concerning your sons, and He has pardoned what they did. For He has taken their covenants after you concerning prophethood. And that is what you mentioned and what you related to me."

When the caravan departed (that is, went out from the outskirts of Egypt heading toward Canaan), their father said: "Indeed, I sense the scent of Joseph" (it is narrated that the wind asked its Lord for permission to bring Jacob the scent of Joseph before the bearer of good news came to him; permission was granted, and it brought it to him). Ibn al-Suddi related from his father, from Mujahid, who said: Jacob caught the scent of Joseph from a distance of three days, because when the wind blew it stirred the shirt and carried the scent of the shirt to Jacob; he found the scent of Paradise, and knew that there is no scent of Paradise on earth except that it comes from that shirt. Therefore he said: "Indeed I sense the scent of Joseph," and he was eight nights' journey away from him.

Shu'bah related from Abu Sinan, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl say: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Jacob found the scent of Joseph while he was eight nights' journey away from him. Abu Sinan related from Abu Hudhayl, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Jacob found the scent of Joseph, and he was eight nights' journey away from him. Shu'bah related from Abu Sinan, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning this verse, say: He found its scent from a distance equal to that between Basra and Kufa. Al-Hasan said: It was mentioned to us that between them at that time there were eighty farsakhs.

﴿Unless you think me senile﴾ — Sufyan related from Husayf, from Mujahid, concerning "Unless you think me senile" (la wa-la an tufannidun), he said: "you consider the opinion foolish." From Ibn 'Abbas: "you consider me ignorant." Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid: "lest you say, 'your mind has gone.'" Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: "you deem me a liar," which is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "you think me senile," and similarly Israil related from Abu Yahya from Mujahid. Al-Rabi' said: "you consider me a fool." Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak: "you think me senile, so you say: 'an old man who has become senile and lost his mind.'" Ibn Yasar said: "you deem me weak." Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: "you find me repugnant." Al-Kisa'i said: "you deem me incapable." Al-Akhfash said: "you blame me." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "you deem me astray."

The root of tafnid (fannada) is corruption. Al-Nabighah said:
"Except Solomon, when the King said to him: 'Stand in the land and restrain it from tafnid.'"
That is, prevent it from corruption. Hence it is said that blame is tafnid. A poet said:
"O my two companions, leave off my blame and my tafnid; what has passed of a matter cannot be returned."
Jarir ibn 'Atiyyah said:
"O my blamers, leave off reproach and be brief; love has lasted long, and you have prolonged tafnid."
Another said:
"You destroyed me with blame and tafnid."
Al-fand is error in speech and opinion. It is said: afnada fulanan al-dahr, meaning when time corrupted him. From the words of Ibn Muqbil:
"Leave time to do what it wills, for when it charges the people with corruption, it corrupts them."

They said — that is, his grandchildren: ﴿By God, you are surely in your old error﴾, your ancient mistake of loving Joseph and not forgetting him.

﴿Then when the bearer of good news came﴾, the one who brought the message of Joseph. Ibn 'Abbas said: the messenger was Yahudha ibn Ya'qub. Ibn Mas'ud said: "the bearer of good news came from ahead of the caravan." Al-Suddi said: Yahudha said: "I was the one who took the shirt stained with blood to Jacob and told him that Joseph had been eaten by the wolf; today I will take the shirt and tell him he is alive, and gladden him as I saddened him." Ibn 'Abbas said: Yahudha carried it alone, apart from them; he went out bareheaded and barefoot and began to run until he reached his father. He had seven loaves with him, which he had not finished eating, and the distance was eighty farsakhs. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: the bearer of good news was Malik ibn Dhu'r from the people of Madyan.

﴿He cast it﴾, that is, the bearer of good news cast Joseph's shirt over Jacob's face, ﴿and he regained his sight﴾: he returned seeing after having been blind.

'Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related from Abu 'Abdullah al-Sulami, who said: I heard Yahya ibn Muslim, from someone he named, say: Jacob was the most honored of the people of the earth before the Angel of Death, and the Angel of Death asked his Lord for permission to come to Jacob, and was permitted. He came to him, and Jacob said: "O Angel of Death, I ask you by the One who created you: have you taken the soul of Joseph among those you have seized?" He said: "No." The Angel of Death said: "O Jacob, shall I teach you a supplication?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Say: O Possessor of the kindness that never ends and which no one but You can count." So Jacob supplicated with it that night, and the dawn had not risen before he cast the shirt over his face, and he regained his sight. Al-Dahhak said: his sight returned to him after blindness, strength after weakness, youth after decrepitude, and joy after sorrow.

He said: ﴿Did I not tell you that I know from God what you do not know﴾, concerning Joseph's life and that God would reunite us. They said, after that: ﴿O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins; indeed we have been sinners﴾, those who were at fault.

Jacob (upon him peace) said: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾ in the night prayer. Most exegetes said: he delayed it until the last part of the night, because supplication at the time of dawn is not veiled from God. When Jacob reached the appointed time, he advanced to prayer at dawn, and when he finished, he raised his hands to God, the Exalted: "O God, forgive me my grief over Joseph and my lack of patience concerning him, and forgive my sons what they did to Joseph." God revealed to him: "I have forgiven you and them all."

Muharib ibn Dithar said: a paternal uncle of mine used to go to the mosque, and he said: "I passed by the house of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and heard him say: 'O God, You called me and I answered, You commanded me and I obeyed; this is the dawn, so forgive me.'" I asked him about that, and he said: "Jacob delayed the seeking of forgiveness for his sons until the dawn, by his saying: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾."

Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "'I will ask my Lord to forgive you' means: until the coming of the day of Friday" [128]. Wahb said: he would ask forgiveness for them every Friday night for some twenty-odd years. Tawus said: he delayed it until the dawn of Friday night, and that coincided with the night of 'Ashura'.

From Abu Salamah, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, who said: "Seeking needs from a young man is easier than from the elderly. Do you not see Joseph's saying to his brothers: ﴿No reproach upon you today﴾, and Jacob's saying (upon him peace): ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾?"

Abu al-Hasan al-Mulani al-Sha'bi said: "'I will ask my Lord to forgive you': I will ask Joseph; if he pardons you, I will ask my Lord to forgive you." ﴿Indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾.

It is narrated that when the bearer of good news informed Jacob of Joseph's life, Jacob said: "How did you leave Joseph?" He said: "He is king of Egypt." Jacob said: "What do I want with kingship? On what religion did you leave him?" He said: "On the religion of Islam." Jacob said: "Now the blessing is complete."

Al-Thawri said: When Jacob and Joseph (upon them both peace) met, each embraced the other and they both wept. Joseph said: "O father, you wept for me until your sight was lost; did you not know that the Resurrection will gather us?" He said: "Yes, my son, but I feared that your religion would be stolen, and that I would be separated from you."

They said: Joseph had sent with the bearer of good news to Jacob provisions and two hundred riding-camels, and asked Jacob to come to him with all his family and children. Jacob prepared to leave for Egypt. When he drew near Egypt, the king who was above Joseph went out, and Joseph went out with the king among four thousand troops, and the people of Egypt rode with them to meet Jacob. Jacob was walking, leading his mount, with Yahudha. Jacob looked at the horses and people and said to Yahudha: "Is this the Pharaoh of Egypt?" He said: "No, this is your son."

When each drew near the other, Joseph went to begin with the greeting, but was prevented from doing so, since Jacob had more right to it and was more excellent. So Jacob began the greeting and said: "Peace be upon you, O you who removes sorrows." This is the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said: "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security."﴾

If it is said: how did Joseph say to them, "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security," after they had entered it, when God informed us that when they entered upon Joseph and he embraced his parents, he said this to them as he met them before entering Egypt, as we have mentioned?

Some said: in the verse there is inversion and reordering, and this exception is from the saying of Jacob when he said: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾, and the meaning is: "I will ask my Lord to forgive you, if God wills, indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Then when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself, and said: 'Enter Egypt... in security,' and he raised his parents upon the throne." This is the meaning of the saying of Abu Jarir. Others said: the exception falls on security, not on entering, like His saying: ﴿You shall enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in security﴾ [Sura al-Fath: 27].

And the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) upon entering the graves: "And we, if God wills, will be joining you" [129] [Sahih Muslim: 1/150]. So the exception falls on joining them, not on death. It was also said: "in" here means "when," like His saying: ﴿And leave what remains of usury, if you are believers﴾ [Sura al-Baqarah: 278], and His saying: ﴿You shall be the uppermost, if you are believers﴾ [Sura Al 'Imran: 139], and His saying: ﴿If they desire chastity﴾ [Sura al-Nur: 33].

Ibn 'Abbas said: He only said "in security" because in the past they had feared the kings of Egypt, and did not enter Egypt, for they had no permit. As for His saying "he took his parents to himself": Ibn Ishaq said: his father and his mother. Others said: his father and his maternal aunt, for Rachel, Joseph's mother, had died in childbirth, and Jacob afterward married her sister Liyya; so he called the aunt "mother," just as he called the paternal uncle "father" in His saying: ﴿We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac﴾.

Ishaq related from Bishr, from Sa'id, from al-Hasan, who said: God raised Rachel, Joseph's mother, from her grave until she prostrated, to fulfill the dream.

﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne﴾, on the couch; that is, he seated them upon it. Ibn Ishaq said: it means he raised their status. ﴿And they fell before him in prostration﴾: that is, Jacob, his aunt, and his brothers. At that time the greeting of people was prostration, and by prostration was not meant placing the forehead upon the ground, because that is not permitted except to God, Exalted; it is only bowing and humility as a form of greeting, honor, and salutation, except when it is done in the manner of worship and prayer. This is the saying of al-A'sha ibn Tha'labah:
"When he came to us after the sleep's absence, we prostrated to him and raised the turbans."
Another said:
"Its surplus reins prostrated, as Christians prostrate to their lords."
It was also said: prostration in language means submission, like the saying of al-Nabighah [in the source: Zayd al-Khayl instead of al-Nabighah]:
"With a host in whose lodges the spotted horses are lost; the hills in it are seen prostrating to the hooves."
That is, lowered and humbled.

[Tha'lab] said: "they fell" means "they passed by," and was not meant as falling down and dropping to the ground. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿They did not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾ [Sura al-Furqan: 73]; it only means they did not pass by in that manner. Mujahid: in the sense of passing. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that its meaning is: they fell down to God in prostration, so the "him" refers to God, Exalted.

Joseph then said, and his skin shivered: ﴿This is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true﴾, and that is His saying: ﴿Indeed I saw eleven stars﴾.

They differed about the length of Joseph's absence from Jacob. Al-Kalbi said: two hundred and twenty years. Salman al-Farisi: forty years. Abdullah ibn Shaddad: seventy years. It was also said: seventy-seven years. Al-Hasan said:
Joseph was thrown into the well at seventeen years of age, and was absent from his father eighty years, and lived after his reunion with Jacob twenty-three years, and died at the age of a hundred and twenty years. In the Torah: a hundred and sixteen years. According to Ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar: eighty-seven years. Ibn Abi Ishaq said: eighteen years. Joseph had from the wife of the Aziz: Ephraim, Menasseh, and Rahmah, wife of Job. Between Joseph and Moses were four hundred years.

﴿And He was good to me when He brought me out of the prison﴾; he did not say "out of the well," using courtesy, so as not to remind his brothers of their deed. It was also said: because God's blessing upon him in being saved from prison was greater than His blessing upon him in rescuing him from the well, for his falling into the well was due to his brothers' envy, while his imprisonment was a recompense from God for a slip that had come from him.

﴿And He brought you from the desert﴾, because Jacob and his sons were people of the desert and livestock. "Badw" is the verbal noun of your saying "badā, yabdū, badwan," when one becomes in the desert. ﴿After Satan had stirred discord between me and my brothers﴾. ﴿Indeed my Lord is Gentle, bestowing kindness on whom He wills﴾, knowing the subtleties of matters and their realities. ﴿Indeed He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾.

Abd al-Samad related from his father, from Wahb, who said: They—that is, Jacob and his sons—entered Egypt as seventy-two persons, men and women, and they left with Moses, and their number was six hundred and fifty-some thousand men, besides the offspring, the elderly, and the disabled; and the offspring were a million and two hundred thousand, besides the fighters.

The historians said: Jacob remained in Egypt after his family joined him for twenty-four years in the most pleasant condition and happiest life; then he died in Egypt. When death came to him, he bequeathed to his son Joseph that his body be carried until it was buried beside his father Isaac. Joseph did so, carried it, and buried him in Syria, then returned to Egypt.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he was transported in a chest of teak to Jerusalem, and that coincided with the day Esau died, and they were buried in one grave. Hence the Jews transport their dead to Jerusalem, those of them who do so. Jacob and Esau were born in one womb and buried in one grave, and their age together was a hundred and forty-seven years.

They said: When God gathered Joseph's family, fulfilled his vision, and cooled his eye, and had made his worldly kingdom and bliss expansive, he knew that this would not last for him and that he must part from it. He desired a bliss more enduring, and his soul longed for Paradise, so he wished for death and supplicated his Lord. No prophet before or after him wished for death, and he said: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom﴾, meaning the kingdom of Egypt, ﴿and taught me of the interpretation of events﴾, meaning the interpretation of dreams. ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their Creator and Maker.

﴿You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter﴾, my helper in this world and the Hereafter, managing my affairs. ﴿Cause me to die a Muslim, and join me with the righteous﴾, with my forefathers the prophets.

It was said: God took him in a good and pure state in Egypt, and he was buried in the Nile in a marble chest. When he died, people quarreled over him, each wanting to be buried in their own quarter, hoping for his blessing, until they gathered to fight. So they decided to bury him in the Nile at the place where the water divides in Egypt, so the water would flow over him and then reach all of Egypt, and they would all share in it equally. They did so.

Salih al-Murri related from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, gathered Jacob's family, his sons withdrew in private conversation. Some said to others: "Do you not know what you did, and what the old man suffered from you, and what Joseph suffered from you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then if they pardon you, but how will you face your Lord?" Their affair settled on coming to the old man, and they sat before him, with Joseph sitting beside his father.

They said: "O our father, we have come to you about a matter we have never come to you about before, and a calamity has befallen us the like of which has never befallen us," until they stirred him, and the prophets (upon them peace) are the most merciful of creatures. He said: "What is wrong with you, my sons?" They said: "Do you not know what we did to you, and what we did to our brother Joseph?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Have you not both pardoned?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Then your pardon will not avail us if God has not pardoned us." He said: "Then what do you want, my sons?" They said:

The sons said: "We want you to pray to God. When the revelation comes from God that He has pardoned them, we will have done it; our eyes will be comforted and our hearts will be at rest. Otherwise, there will never be any comfort for our eyes in this world." So the old man (al-Shaykh) faced the qibla and stood, and Yusuf stood behind his father, and they stood behind the two of them, humbled and submissive. Yaʿqub prayed, and Yusuf said "Amin," but He did not answer them for twenty years.

Salih al-Murri said: He kept them in fear. Then, when the twentieth year came, Jibril descended upon Yaʿqub and said:

"Indeed God, blessed and exalted, sent me to you to give you good news: He has answered your supplication concerning your sons, and He has pardoned what they did. For He has taken their covenants after you concerning prophethood. And that is what you mentioned and what you related to me."

When the caravan departed (that is, went out from the outskirts of Egypt heading toward Canaan), their father said: "Indeed, I sense the scent of Joseph" (it is narrated that the wind asked its Lord for permission to bring Jacob the scent of Joseph before the bearer of good news came to him; permission was granted, and it brought it to him). Ibn al-Suddi related from his father, from Mujahid, who said: Jacob caught the scent of Joseph from a distance of three days, because when the wind blew it stirred the shirt and carried the scent of the shirt to Jacob; he found the scent of Paradise, and knew that there is no scent of Paradise on earth except that it comes from that shirt. Therefore he said: "Indeed I sense the scent of Joseph," and he was eight nights' journey away from him.

Shu'bah related from Abu Sinan, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl say: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Jacob found the scent of Joseph while he was eight nights' journey away from him. Abu Sinan related from Abu Hudhayl, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Jacob found the scent of Joseph, and he was eight nights' journey away from him. Shu'bah related from Abu Sinan, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning this verse, say: He found its scent from a distance equal to that between Basra and Kufa. Al-Hasan said: It was mentioned to us that between them at that time there were eighty farsakhs.

﴿Unless you think me senile﴾ — Sufyan related from Husayf, from Mujahid, concerning "Unless you think me senile" (la wa-la an tufannidun), he said: "you consider the opinion foolish." From Ibn 'Abbas: "you consider me ignorant." Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid: "lest you say, 'your mind has gone.'" Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: "you deem me a liar," which is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "you think me senile," and similarly Israil related from Abu Yahya from Mujahid. Al-Rabi' said: "you consider me a fool." Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak: "you think me senile, so you say: 'an old man who has become senile and lost his mind.'" Ibn Yasar said: "you deem me weak." Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: "you find me repugnant." Al-Kisa'i said: "you deem me incapable." Al-Akhfash said: "you blame me." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "you deem me astray."

The root of tafnid (fannada) is corruption. Al-Nabighah said:
"Except Solomon, when the King said to him: 'Stand in the land and restrain it from tafnid.'"
That is, prevent it from corruption. Hence it is said that blame is tafnid. A poet said:
"O my two companions, leave off my blame and my tafnid; what has passed of a matter cannot be returned."
Jarir ibn 'Atiyyah said:
"O my blamers, leave off reproach and be brief; love has lasted long, and you have prolonged tafnid."
Another said:
"You destroyed me with blame and tafnid."
Al-fand is error in speech and opinion. It is said: afnada fulanan al-dahr, meaning when time corrupted him. From the words of Ibn Muqbil:
"Leave time to do what it wills, for when it charges the people with corruption, it corrupts them."

They said — that is, his grandchildren: ﴿By God, you are surely in your old error﴾, your ancient mistake of loving Joseph and not forgetting him.

﴿Then when the bearer of good news came﴾, the one who brought the message of Joseph. Ibn 'Abbas said: the messenger was Yahudha ibn Ya'qub. Ibn Mas'ud said: "the bearer of good news came from ahead of the caravan." Al-Suddi said: Yahudha said: "I was the one who took the shirt stained with blood to Jacob and told him that Joseph had been eaten by the wolf; today I will take the shirt and tell him he is alive, and gladden him as I saddened him." Ibn 'Abbas said: Yahudha carried it alone, apart from them; he went out bareheaded and barefoot and began to run until he reached his father. He had seven loaves with him, which he had not finished eating, and the distance was eighty farsakhs. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: the bearer of good news was Malik ibn Dhu'r from the people of Madyan.

﴿He cast it﴾, that is, the bearer of good news cast Joseph's shirt over Jacob's face, ﴿and he regained his sight﴾: he returned seeing after having been blind.

'Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related from Abu 'Abdullah al-Sulami, who said: I heard Yahya ibn Muslim, from someone he named, say: Jacob was the most honored of the people of the earth before the Angel of Death, and the Angel of Death asked his Lord for permission to come to Jacob, and was permitted. He came to him, and Jacob said: "O Angel of Death, I ask you by the One who created you: have you taken the soul of Joseph among those you have seized?" He said: "No." The Angel of Death said: "O Jacob, shall I teach you a supplication?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Say: O Possessor of the kindness that never ends and which no one but You can count." So Jacob supplicated with it that night, and the dawn had not risen before he cast the shirt over his face, and he regained his sight. Al-Dahhak said: his sight returned to him after blindness, strength after weakness, youth after decrepitude, and joy after sorrow.

He said: ﴿Did I not tell you that I know from God what you do not know﴾, concerning Joseph's life and that God would reunite us. They said, after that: ﴿O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins; indeed we have been sinners﴾, those who were at fault.

Jacob (upon him peace) said: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾ in the night prayer. Most exegetes said: he delayed it until the last part of the night, because supplication at the time of dawn is not veiled from God. When Jacob reached the appointed time, he advanced to prayer at dawn, and when he finished, he raised his hands to God, the Exalted: "O God, forgive me my grief over Joseph and my lack of patience concerning him, and forgive my sons what they did to Joseph." God revealed to him: "I have forgiven you and them all."

Muharib ibn Dithar said: a paternal uncle of mine used to go to the mosque, and he said: "I passed by the house of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and heard him say: 'O God, You called me and I answered, You commanded me and I obeyed; this is the dawn, so forgive me.'" I asked him about that, and he said: "Jacob delayed the seeking of forgiveness for his sons until the dawn, by his saying: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾."

Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "'I will ask my Lord to forgive you' means: until the coming of the day of Friday" [128]. Wahb said: he would ask forgiveness for them every Friday night for some twenty-odd years. Tawus said: he delayed it until the dawn of Friday night, and that coincided with the night of 'Ashura'.

From Abu Salamah, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, who said: "Seeking needs from a young man is easier than from the elderly. Do you not see Joseph's saying to his brothers: ﴿No reproach upon you today﴾, and Jacob's saying (upon him peace): ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾?"

Abu al-Hasan al-Mulani al-Sha'bi said: "'I will ask my Lord to forgive you': I will ask Joseph; if he pardons you, I will ask my Lord to forgive you." ﴿Indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾.

It is narrated that when the bearer of good news informed Jacob of Joseph's life, Jacob said: "How did you leave Joseph?" He said: "He is king of Egypt." Jacob said: "What do I want with kingship? On what religion did you leave him?" He said: "On the religion of Islam." Jacob said: "Now the blessing is complete."

Al-Thawri said: When Jacob and Joseph (upon them both peace) met, each embraced the other and they both wept. Joseph said: "O father, you wept for me until your sight was lost; did you not know that the Resurrection will gather us?" He said: "Yes, my son, but I feared that your religion would be stolen, and that I would be separated from you."

They said: Joseph had sent with the bearer of good news to Jacob provisions and two hundred riding-camels, and asked Jacob to come to him with all his family and children. Jacob prepared to leave for Egypt. When he drew near Egypt, the king who was above Joseph went out, and Joseph went out with the king among four thousand troops, and the people of Egypt rode with them to meet Jacob. Jacob was walking, leading his mount, with Yahudha. Jacob looked at the horses and people and said to Yahudha: "Is this the Pharaoh of Egypt?" He said: "No, this is your son."

When each drew near the other, Joseph went to begin with the greeting, but was prevented from doing so, since Jacob had more right to it and was more excellent. So Jacob began the greeting and said: "Peace be upon you, O you who removes sorrows." This is the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said: "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security."﴾

If it is said: how did Joseph say to them, "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security," after they had entered it, when God informed us that when they entered upon Joseph and he embraced his parents, he said this to them as he met them before entering Egypt, as we have mentioned?

Some said: in the verse there is inversion and reordering, and this exception is from the saying of Jacob when he said: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾, and the meaning is: "I will ask my Lord to forgive you, if God wills, indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Then when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself, and said: 'Enter Egypt... in security,' and he raised his parents upon the throne." This is the meaning of the saying of Abu Jarir. Others said: the exception falls on security, not on entering, like His saying: ﴿You shall enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in security﴾ [Sura al-Fath: 27].

And the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) upon entering the graves: "And we, if God wills, will be joining you" [129] [Sahih Muslim: 1/150]. So the exception falls on joining them, not on death. It was also said: "in" here means "when," like His saying: ﴿And leave what remains of usury, if you are believers﴾ [Sura al-Baqarah: 278], and His saying: ﴿You shall be the uppermost, if you are believers﴾ [Sura Al 'Imran: 139], and His saying: ﴿If they desire chastity﴾ [Sura al-Nur: 33].

Ibn 'Abbas said: He only said "in security" because in the past they had feared the kings of Egypt, and did not enter Egypt, for they had no permit. As for His saying "he took his parents to himself": Ibn Ishaq said: his father and his mother. Others said: his father and his maternal aunt, for Rachel, Joseph's mother, had died in childbirth, and Jacob afterward married her sister Liyya; so he called the aunt "mother," just as he called the paternal uncle "father" in His saying: ﴿We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac﴾.

Ishaq related from Bishr, from Sa'id, from al-Hasan, who said: God raised Rachel, Joseph's mother, from her grave until she prostrated, to fulfill the dream.

﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne﴾, on the couch; that is, he seated them upon it. Ibn Ishaq said: it means he raised their status. ﴿And they fell before him in prostration﴾: that is, Jacob, his aunt, and his brothers. At that time the greeting of people was prostration, and by prostration was not meant placing the forehead upon the ground, because that is not permitted except to God, Exalted; it is only bowing and humility as a form of greeting, honor, and salutation, except when it is done in the manner of worship and prayer. This is the saying of al-A'sha ibn Tha'labah:
"When he came to us after the sleep's absence, we prostrated to him and raised the turbans."
Another said:
"Its surplus reins prostrated, as Christians prostrate to their lords."
It was also said: prostration in language means submission, like the saying of al-Nabighah [in the source: Zayd al-Khayl instead of al-Nabighah]:
"With a host in whose lodges the spotted horses are lost; the hills in it are seen prostrating to the hooves."
That is, lowered and humbled.

[Tha'lab] said: "they fell" means "they passed by," and was not meant as falling down and dropping to the ground. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿They did not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾ [Sura al-Furqan: 73]; it only means they did not pass by in that manner. Mujahid: in the sense of passing. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that its meaning is: they fell down to God in prostration, so the "him" refers to God, Exalted.

Joseph then said, and his skin shivered: ﴿This is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true﴾, and that is His saying: ﴿Indeed I saw eleven stars﴾.

They differed about the length of Joseph's absence from Jacob. Al-Kalbi said: two hundred and twenty years. Salman al-Farisi: forty years. Abdullah ibn Shaddad: seventy years. It was also said: seventy-seven years. Al-Hasan said:
Joseph was thrown into the well at seventeen years of age, and was absent from his father eighty years, and lived after his reunion with Jacob twenty-three years, and died at the age of a hundred and twenty years. In the Torah: a hundred and sixteen years. According to Ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar: eighty-seven years. Ibn Abi Ishaq said: eighteen years. Joseph had from the wife of the Aziz: Ephraim, Menasseh, and Rahmah, wife of Job. Between Joseph and Moses were four hundred years.

﴿And He was good to me when He brought me out of the prison﴾; he did not say "out of the well," using courtesy, so as not to remind his brothers of their deed. It was also said: because God's blessing upon him in being saved from prison was greater than His blessing upon him in rescuing him from the well, for his falling into the well was due to his brothers' envy, while his imprisonment was a recompense from God for a slip that had come from him.

﴿And He brought you from the desert﴾, because Jacob and his sons were people of the desert and livestock. "Badw" is the verbal noun of your saying "badā, yabdū, badwan," when one becomes in the desert. ﴿After Satan had stirred discord between me and my brothers﴾. ﴿Indeed my Lord is Gentle, bestowing kindness on whom He wills﴾, knowing the subtleties of matters and their realities. ﴿Indeed He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾.

Abd al-Samad related from his father, from Wahb, who said: They—that is, Jacob and his sons—entered Egypt as seventy-two persons, men and women, and they left with Moses, and their number was six hundred and fifty-some thousand men, besides the offspring, the elderly, and the disabled; and the offspring were a million and two hundred thousand, besides the fighters.

The historians said: Jacob remained in Egypt after his family joined him for twenty-four years in the most pleasant condition and happiest life; then he died in Egypt. When death came to him, he bequeathed to his son Joseph that his body be carried until it was buried beside his father Isaac. Joseph did so, carried it, and buried him in Syria, then returned to Egypt.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he was transported in a chest of teak to Jerusalem, and that coincided with the day Esau died, and they were buried in one grave. Hence the Jews transport their dead to Jerusalem, those of them who do so. Jacob and Esau were born in one womb and buried in one grave, and their age together was a hundred and forty-seven years.

They said: When God gathered Joseph's family, fulfilled his vision, and cooled his eye, and had made his worldly kingdom and bliss expansive, he knew that this would not last for him and that he must part from it. He desired a bliss more enduring, and his soul longed for Paradise, so he wished for death and supplicated his Lord. No prophet before or after him wished for death, and he said: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom﴾, meaning the kingdom of Egypt, ﴿and taught me of the interpretation of events﴾, meaning the interpretation of dreams. ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their Creator and Maker.

﴿You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter﴾, my helper in this world and the Hereafter, managing my affairs. ﴿Cause me to die a Muslim, and join me with the righteous﴾, with my forefathers the prophets.

It was said: God took him in a good and pure state in Egypt, and he was buried in the Nile in a marble chest. When he died, people quarreled over him, each wanting to be buried in their own quarter, hoping for his blessing, until they gathered to fight. So they decided to bury him in the Nile at the place where the water divides in Egypt, so the water would flow over him and then reach all of Egypt, and they would all share in it equally. They did so.

Salih al-Murri related from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, gathered Jacob's family, his sons withdrew in private conversation. Some said to others: "Do you not know what you did, and what the old man suffered from you, and what Joseph suffered from you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then if they pardon you, but how will you face your Lord?" Their affair settled on coming to the old man, and they sat before him, with Joseph sitting beside his father.

They said: "O our father, we have come to you about a matter we have never come to you about before, and a calamity has befallen us the like of which has never befallen us," until they stirred him, and the prophets (upon them peace) are the most merciful of creatures. He said: "What is wrong with you, my sons?" They said: "Do you not know what we did to you, and what we did to our brother Joseph?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Have you not both pardoned?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Then your pardon will not avail us if God has not pardoned us." He said: "Then what do you want, my sons?" They said:

The sons said: "We want you to pray to God. When the revelation comes from God that He has pardoned them, we will have done it; our eyes will be comforted and our hearts will be at rest. Otherwise, there will never be any comfort for our eyes in this world." So the old man (al-Shaykh) faced the qibla and stood, and Yusuf stood behind his father, and they stood behind the two of them, humbled and submissive. Yaʿqub prayed, and Yusuf said "Amin," but He did not answer them for twenty years.

Salih al-Murri said: He kept them in fear. Then, when the twentieth year came, Jibril descended upon Yaʿqub and said:

"Indeed God, blessed and exalted, sent me to you to give you good news: He has answered your supplication concerning your sons, and He has pardoned what they did. For He has taken their covenants after you concerning prophethood. And that is what you mentioned and what you related to me."

When the caravan departed (that is, went out from the outskirts of Egypt heading toward Canaan), their father said: "Indeed, I sense the scent of Joseph" (it is narrated that the wind asked its Lord for permission to bring Jacob the scent of Joseph before the bearer of good news came to him; permission was granted, and it brought it to him). Ibn al-Suddi related from his father, from Mujahid, who said: Jacob caught the scent of Joseph from a distance of three days, because when the wind blew it stirred the shirt and carried the scent of the shirt to Jacob; he found the scent of Paradise, and knew that there is no scent of Paradise on earth except that it comes from that shirt. Therefore he said: "Indeed I sense the scent of Joseph," and he was eight nights' journey away from him.

Shu'bah related from Abu Sinan, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl say: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Jacob found the scent of Joseph while he was eight nights' journey away from him. Abu Sinan related from Abu Hudhayl, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Jacob found the scent of Joseph, and he was eight nights' journey away from him. Shu'bah related from Abu Sinan, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning this verse, say: He found its scent from a distance equal to that between Basra and Kufa. Al-Hasan said: It was mentioned to us that between them at that time there were eighty farsakhs.

﴿Unless you think me senile﴾ — Sufyan related from Husayf, from Mujahid, concerning "Unless you think me senile" (la wa-la an tufannidun), he said: "you consider the opinion foolish." From Ibn 'Abbas: "you consider me ignorant." Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid: "lest you say, 'your mind has gone.'" Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: "you deem me a liar," which is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "you think me senile," and similarly Israil related from Abu Yahya from Mujahid. Al-Rabi' said: "you consider me a fool." Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak: "you think me senile, so you say: 'an old man who has become senile and lost his mind.'" Ibn Yasar said: "you deem me weak." Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: "you find me repugnant." Al-Kisa'i said: "you deem me incapable." Al-Akhfash said: "you blame me." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "you deem me astray."

The root of tafnid (fannada) is corruption. Al-Nabighah said:
"Except Solomon, when the King said to him: 'Stand in the land and restrain it from tafnid.'"
That is, prevent it from corruption. Hence it is said that blame is tafnid. A poet said:
"O my two companions, leave off my blame and my tafnid; what has passed of a matter cannot be returned."
Jarir ibn 'Atiyyah said:
"O my blamers, leave off reproach and be brief; love has lasted long, and you have prolonged tafnid."
Another said:
"You destroyed me with blame and tafnid."
Al-fand is error in speech and opinion. It is said: afnada fulanan al-dahr, meaning when time corrupted him. From the words of Ibn Muqbil:
"Leave time to do what it wills, for when it charges the people with corruption, it corrupts them."

They said — that is, his grandchildren: ﴿By God, you are surely in your old error﴾, your ancient mistake of loving Joseph and not forgetting him.

﴿Then when the bearer of good news came﴾, the one who brought the message of Joseph. Ibn 'Abbas said: the messenger was Yahudha ibn Ya'qub. Ibn Mas'ud said: "the bearer of good news came from ahead of the caravan." Al-Suddi said: Yahudha said: "I was the one who took the shirt stained with blood to Jacob and told him that Joseph had been eaten by the wolf; today I will take the shirt and tell him he is alive, and gladden him as I saddened him." Ibn 'Abbas said: Yahudha carried it alone, apart from them; he went out bareheaded and barefoot and began to run until he reached his father. He had seven loaves with him, which he had not finished eating, and the distance was eighty farsakhs. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: the bearer of good news was Malik ibn Dhu'r from the people of Madyan.

﴿He cast it﴾, that is, the bearer of good news cast Joseph's shirt over Jacob's face, ﴿and he regained his sight﴾: he returned seeing after having been blind.

'Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related from Abu 'Abdullah al-Sulami, who said: I heard Yahya ibn Muslim, from someone he named, say: Jacob was the most honored of the people of the earth before the Angel of Death, and the Angel of Death asked his Lord for permission to come to Jacob, and was permitted. He came to him, and Jacob said: "O Angel of Death, I ask you by the One who created you: have you taken the soul of Joseph among those you have seized?" He said: "No." The Angel of Death said: "O Jacob, shall I teach you a supplication?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Say: O Possessor of the kindness that never ends and which no one but You can count." So Jacob supplicated with it that night, and the dawn had not risen before he cast the shirt over his face, and he regained his sight. Al-Dahhak said: his sight returned to him after blindness, strength after weakness, youth after decrepitude, and joy after sorrow.

He said: ﴿Did I not tell you that I know from God what you do not know﴾, concerning Joseph's life and that God would reunite us. They said, after that: ﴿O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins; indeed we have been sinners﴾, those who were at fault.

Jacob (upon him peace) said: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾ in the night prayer. Most exegetes said: he delayed it until the last part of the night, because supplication at the time of dawn is not veiled from God. When Jacob reached the appointed time, he advanced to prayer at dawn, and when he finished, he raised his hands to God, the Exalted: "O God, forgive me my grief over Joseph and my lack of patience concerning him, and forgive my sons what they did to Joseph." God revealed to him: "I have forgiven you and them all."

Muharib ibn Dithar said: a paternal uncle of mine used to go to the mosque, and he said: "I passed by the house of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and heard him say: 'O God, You called me and I answered, You commanded me and I obeyed; this is the dawn, so forgive me.'" I asked him about that, and he said: "Jacob delayed the seeking of forgiveness for his sons until the dawn, by his saying: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾."

Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "'I will ask my Lord to forgive you' means: until the coming of the day of Friday" [128]. Wahb said: he would ask forgiveness for them every Friday night for some twenty-odd years. Tawus said: he delayed it until the dawn of Friday night, and that coincided with the night of 'Ashura'.

From Abu Salamah, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, who said: "Seeking needs from a young man is easier than from the elderly. Do you not see Joseph's saying to his brothers: ﴿No reproach upon you today﴾, and Jacob's saying (upon him peace): ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾?"

Abu al-Hasan al-Mulani al-Sha'bi said: "'I will ask my Lord to forgive you': I will ask Joseph; if he pardons you, I will ask my Lord to forgive you." ﴿Indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾.

It is narrated that when the bearer of good news informed Jacob of Joseph's life, Jacob said: "How did you leave Joseph?" He said: "He is king of Egypt." Jacob said: "What do I want with kingship? On what religion did you leave him?" He said: "On the religion of Islam." Jacob said: "Now the blessing is complete."

Al-Thawri said: When Jacob and Joseph (upon them both peace) met, each embraced the other and they both wept. Joseph said: "O father, you wept for me until your sight was lost; did you not know that the Resurrection will gather us?" He said: "Yes, my son, but I feared that your religion would be stolen, and that I would be separated from you."

They said: Joseph had sent with the bearer of good news to Jacob provisions and two hundred riding-camels, and asked Jacob to come to him with all his family and children. Jacob prepared to leave for Egypt. When he drew near Egypt, the king who was above Joseph went out, and Joseph went out with the king among four thousand troops, and the people of Egypt rode with them to meet Jacob. Jacob was walking, leading his mount, with Yahudha. Jacob looked at the horses and people and said to Yahudha: "Is this the Pharaoh of Egypt?" He said: "No, this is your son."

When each drew near the other, Joseph went to begin with the greeting, but was prevented from doing so, since Jacob had more right to it and was more excellent. So Jacob began the greeting and said: "Peace be upon you, O you who removes sorrows." This is the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said: "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security."﴾

If it is said: how did Joseph say to them, "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security," after they had entered it, when God informed us that when they entered upon Joseph and he embraced his parents, he said this to them as he met them before entering Egypt, as we have mentioned?

Some said: in the verse there is inversion and reordering, and this exception is from the saying of Jacob when he said: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾, and the meaning is: "I will ask my Lord to forgive you, if God wills, indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Then when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself, and said: 'Enter Egypt... in security,' and he raised his parents upon the throne." This is the meaning of the saying of Abu Jarir. Others said: the exception falls on security, not on entering, like His saying: ﴿You shall enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in security﴾ [Sura al-Fath: 27].

And the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) upon entering the graves: "And we, if God wills, will be joining you" [129] [Sahih Muslim: 1/150]. So the exception falls on joining them, not on death. It was also said: "in" here means "when," like His saying: ﴿And leave what remains of usury, if you are believers﴾ [Sura al-Baqarah: 278], and His saying: ﴿You shall be the uppermost, if you are believers﴾ [Sura Al 'Imran: 139], and His saying: ﴿If they desire chastity﴾ [Sura al-Nur: 33].

Ibn 'Abbas said: He only said "in security" because in the past they had feared the kings of Egypt, and did not enter Egypt, for they had no permit. As for His saying "he took his parents to himself": Ibn Ishaq said: his father and his mother. Others said: his father and his maternal aunt, for Rachel, Joseph's mother, had died in childbirth, and Jacob afterward married her sister Liyya; so he called the aunt "mother," just as he called the paternal uncle "father" in His saying: ﴿We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac﴾.

Ishaq related from Bishr, from Sa'id, from al-Hasan, who said: God raised Rachel, Joseph's mother, from her grave until she prostrated, to fulfill the dream.

﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne﴾, on the couch; that is, he seated them upon it. Ibn Ishaq said: it means he raised their status. ﴿And they fell before him in prostration﴾: that is, Jacob, his aunt, and his brothers. At that time the greeting of people was prostration, and by prostration was not meant placing the forehead upon the ground, because that is not permitted except to God, Exalted; it is only bowing and humility as a form of greeting, honor, and salutation, except when it is done in the manner of worship and prayer. This is the saying of al-A'sha ibn Tha'labah:
"When he came to us after the sleep's absence, we prostrated to him and raised the turbans."
Another said:
"Its surplus reins prostrated, as Christians prostrate to their lords."
It was also said: prostration in language means submission, like the saying of al-Nabighah [in the source: Zayd al-Khayl instead of al-Nabighah]:
"With a host in whose lodges the spotted horses are lost; the hills in it are seen prostrating to the hooves."
That is, lowered and humbled.

[Tha'lab] said: "they fell" means "they passed by," and was not meant as falling down and dropping to the ground. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿They did not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾ [Sura al-Furqan: 73]; it only means they did not pass by in that manner. Mujahid: in the sense of passing. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that its meaning is: they fell down to God in prostration, so the "him" refers to God, Exalted.

Joseph then said, and his skin shivered: ﴿This is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true﴾, and that is His saying: ﴿Indeed I saw eleven stars﴾.

They differed about the length of Joseph's absence from Jacob. Al-Kalbi said: two hundred and twenty years. Salman al-Farisi: forty years. Abdullah ibn Shaddad: seventy years. It was also said: seventy-seven years. Al-Hasan said:
Joseph was thrown into the well at seventeen years of age, and was absent from his father eighty years, and lived after his reunion with Jacob twenty-three years, and died at the age of a hundred and twenty years. In the Torah: a hundred and sixteen years. According to Ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar: eighty-seven years. Ibn Abi Ishaq said: eighteen years. Joseph had from the wife of the Aziz: Ephraim, Menasseh, and Rahmah, wife of Job. Between Joseph and Moses were four hundred years.

﴿And He was good to me when He brought me out of the prison﴾; he did not say "out of the well," using courtesy, so as not to remind his brothers of their deed. It was also said: because God's blessing upon him in being saved from prison was greater than His blessing upon him in rescuing him from the well, for his falling into the well was due to his brothers' envy, while his imprisonment was a recompense from God for a slip that had come from him.

﴿And He brought you from the desert﴾, because Jacob and his sons were people of the desert and livestock. "Badw" is the verbal noun of your saying "badā, yabdū, badwan," when one becomes in the desert. ﴿After Satan had stirred discord between me and my brothers﴾. ﴿Indeed my Lord is Gentle, bestowing kindness on whom He wills﴾, knowing the subtleties of matters and their realities. ﴿Indeed He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾.

Abd al-Samad related from his father, from Wahb, who said: They—that is, Jacob and his sons—entered Egypt as seventy-two persons, men and women, and they left with Moses, and their number was six hundred and fifty-some thousand men, besides the offspring, the elderly, and the disabled; and the offspring were a million and two hundred thousand, besides the fighters.

The historians said: Jacob remained in Egypt after his family joined him for twenty-four years in the most pleasant condition and happiest life; then he died in Egypt. When death came to him, he bequeathed to his son Joseph that his body be carried until it was buried beside his father Isaac. Joseph did so, carried it, and buried him in Syria, then returned to Egypt.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he was transported in a chest of teak to Jerusalem, and that coincided with the day Esau died, and they were buried in one grave. Hence the Jews transport their dead to Jerusalem, those of them who do so. Jacob and Esau were born in one womb and buried in one grave, and their age together was a hundred and forty-seven years.

They said: When God gathered Joseph's family, fulfilled his vision, and cooled his eye, and had made his worldly kingdom and bliss expansive, he knew that this would not last for him and that he must part from it. He desired a bliss more enduring, and his soul longed for Paradise, so he wished for death and supplicated his Lord. No prophet before or after him wished for death, and he said: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom﴾, meaning the kingdom of Egypt, ﴿and taught me of the interpretation of events﴾, meaning the interpretation of dreams. ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their Creator and Maker.

﴿You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter﴾, my helper in this world and the Hereafter, managing my affairs. ﴿Cause me to die a Muslim, and join me with the righteous﴾, with my forefathers the prophets.

It was said: God took him in a good and pure state in Egypt, and he was buried in the Nile in a marble chest. When he died, people quarreled over him, each wanting to be buried in their own quarter, hoping for his blessing, until they gathered to fight. So they decided to bury him in the Nile at the place where the water divides in Egypt, so the water would flow over him and then reach all of Egypt, and they would all share in it equally. They did so.

Salih al-Murri related from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, gathered Jacob's family, his sons withdrew in private conversation. Some said to others: "Do you not know what you did, and what the old man suffered from you, and what Joseph suffered from you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then if they pardon you, but how will you face your Lord?" Their affair settled on coming to the old man, and they sat before him, with Joseph sitting beside his father.

They said: "O our father, we have come to you about a matter we have never come to you about before, and a calamity has befallen us the like of which has never befallen us," until they stirred him, and the prophets (upon them peace) are the most merciful of creatures. He said: "What is wrong with you, my sons?" They said: "Do you not know what we did to you, and what we did to our brother Joseph?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Have you not both pardoned?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Then your pardon will not avail us if God has not pardoned us." He said: "Then what do you want, my sons?" They said:

The sons said: "We want you to pray to God. When the revelation comes from God that He has pardoned them, we will have done it; our eyes will be comforted and our hearts will be at rest. Otherwise, there will never be any comfort for our eyes in this world." So the old man (al-Shaykh) faced the qibla and stood, and Yusuf stood behind his father, and they stood behind the two of them, humbled and submissive. Yaʿqub prayed, and Yusuf said "Amin," but He did not answer them for twenty years.

Salih al-Murri said: He kept them in fear. Then, when the twentieth year came, Jibril descended upon Yaʿqub and said:

"Indeed God, blessed and exalted, sent me to you to give you good news: He has answered your supplication concerning your sons, and He has pardoned what they did. For He has taken their covenants after you concerning prophethood. And that is what you mentioned and what you related to me."

When the caravan departed (that is, went out from the outskirts of Egypt heading toward Canaan), their father said: "Indeed, I sense the scent of Joseph" (it is narrated that the wind asked its Lord for permission to bring Jacob the scent of Joseph before the bearer of good news came to him; permission was granted, and it brought it to him). Ibn al-Suddi related from his father, from Mujahid, who said: Jacob caught the scent of Joseph from a distance of three days, because when the wind blew it stirred the shirt and carried the scent of the shirt to Jacob; he found the scent of Paradise, and knew that there is no scent of Paradise on earth except that it comes from that shirt. Therefore he said: "Indeed I sense the scent of Joseph," and he was eight nights' journey away from him.

Shu'bah related from Abu Sinan, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl say: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Jacob found the scent of Joseph while he was eight nights' journey away from him. Abu Sinan related from Abu Hudhayl, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Jacob found the scent of Joseph, and he was eight nights' journey away from him. Shu'bah related from Abu Sinan, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning this verse, say: He found its scent from a distance equal to that between Basra and Kufa. Al-Hasan said: It was mentioned to us that between them at that time there were eighty farsakhs.

﴿Unless you think me senile﴾ — Sufyan related from Husayf, from Mujahid, concerning "Unless you think me senile" (la wa-la an tufannidun), he said: "you consider the opinion foolish." From Ibn 'Abbas: "you consider me ignorant." Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid: "lest you say, 'your mind has gone.'" Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: "you deem me a liar," which is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "you think me senile," and similarly Israil related from Abu Yahya from Mujahid. Al-Rabi' said: "you consider me a fool." Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak: "you think me senile, so you say: 'an old man who has become senile and lost his mind.'" Ibn Yasar said: "you deem me weak." Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: "you find me repugnant." Al-Kisa'i said: "you deem me incapable." Al-Akhfash said: "you blame me." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "you deem me astray."

The root of tafnid (fannada) is corruption. Al-Nabighah said:
"Except Solomon, when the King said to him: 'Stand in the land and restrain it from tafnid.'"
That is, prevent it from corruption. Hence it is said that blame is tafnid. A poet said:
"O my two companions, leave off my blame and my tafnid; what has passed of a matter cannot be returned."
Jarir ibn 'Atiyyah said:
"O my blamers, leave off reproach and be brief; love has lasted long, and you have prolonged tafnid."
Another said:
"You destroyed me with blame and tafnid."
Al-fand is error in speech and opinion. It is said: afnada fulanan al-dahr, meaning when time corrupted him. From the words of Ibn Muqbil:
"Leave time to do what it wills, for when it charges the people with corruption, it corrupts them."

They said — that is, his grandchildren: ﴿By God, you are surely in your old error﴾, your ancient mistake of loving Joseph and not forgetting him.

﴿Then when the bearer of good news came﴾, the one who brought the message of Joseph. Ibn 'Abbas said: the messenger was Yahudha ibn Ya'qub. Ibn Mas'ud said: "the bearer of good news came from ahead of the caravan." Al-Suddi said: Yahudha said: "I was the one who took the shirt stained with blood to Jacob and told him that Joseph had been eaten by the wolf; today I will take the shirt and tell him he is alive, and gladden him as I saddened him." Ibn 'Abbas said: Yahudha carried it alone, apart from them; he went out bareheaded and barefoot and began to run until he reached his father. He had seven loaves with him, which he had not finished eating, and the distance was eighty farsakhs. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: the bearer of good news was Malik ibn Dhu'r from the people of Madyan.

﴿He cast it﴾, that is, the bearer of good news cast Joseph's shirt over Jacob's face, ﴿and he regained his sight﴾: he returned seeing after having been blind.

'Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related from Abu 'Abdullah al-Sulami, who said: I heard Yahya ibn Muslim, from someone he named, say: Jacob was the most honored of the people of the earth before the Angel of Death, and the Angel of Death asked his Lord for permission to come to Jacob, and was permitted. He came to him, and Jacob said: "O Angel of Death, I ask you by the One who created you: have you taken the soul of Joseph among those you have seized?" He said: "No." The Angel of Death said: "O Jacob, shall I teach you a supplication?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Say: O Possessor of the kindness that never ends and which no one but You can count." So Jacob supplicated with it that night, and the dawn had not risen before he cast the shirt over his face, and he regained his sight. Al-Dahhak said: his sight returned to him after blindness, strength after weakness, youth after decrepitude, and joy after sorrow.

He said: ﴿Did I not tell you that I know from God what you do not know﴾, concerning Joseph's life and that God would reunite us. They said, after that: ﴿O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins; indeed we have been sinners﴾, those who were at fault.

Jacob (upon him peace) said: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾ in the night prayer. Most exegetes said: he delayed it until the last part of the night, because supplication at the time of dawn is not veiled from God. When Jacob reached the appointed time, he advanced to prayer at dawn, and when he finished, he raised his hands to God, the Exalted: "O God, forgive me my grief over Joseph and my lack of patience concerning him, and forgive my sons what they did to Joseph." God revealed to him: "I have forgiven you and them all."

Muharib ibn Dithar said: a paternal uncle of mine used to go to the mosque, and he said: "I passed by the house of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and heard him say: 'O God, You called me and I answered, You commanded me and I obeyed; this is the dawn, so forgive me.'" I asked him about that, and he said: "Jacob delayed the seeking of forgiveness for his sons until the dawn, by his saying: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾."

Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "'I will ask my Lord to forgive you' means: until the coming of the day of Friday" [128]. Wahb said: he would ask forgiveness for them every Friday night for some twenty-odd years. Tawus said: he delayed it until the dawn of Friday night, and that coincided with the night of 'Ashura'.

From Abu Salamah, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, who said: "Seeking needs from a young man is easier than from the elderly. Do you not see Joseph's saying to his brothers: ﴿No reproach upon you today﴾, and Jacob's saying (upon him peace): ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾?"

Abu al-Hasan al-Mulani al-Sha'bi said: "'I will ask my Lord to forgive you': I will ask Joseph; if he pardons you, I will ask my Lord to forgive you." ﴿Indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾.

It is narrated that when the bearer of good news informed Jacob of Joseph's life, Jacob said: "How did you leave Joseph?" He said: "He is king of Egypt." Jacob said: "What do I want with kingship? On what religion did you leave him?" He said: "On the religion of Islam." Jacob said: "Now the blessing is complete."

Al-Thawri said: When Jacob and Joseph (upon them both peace) met, each embraced the other and they both wept. Joseph said: "O father, you wept for me until your sight was lost; did you not know that the Resurrection will gather us?" He said: "Yes, my son, but I feared that your religion would be stolen, and that I would be separated from you."

They said: Joseph had sent with the bearer of good news to Jacob provisions and two hundred riding-camels, and asked Jacob to come to him with all his family and children. Jacob prepared to leave for Egypt. When he drew near Egypt, the king who was above Joseph went out, and Joseph went out with the king among four thousand troops, and the people of Egypt rode with them to meet Jacob. Jacob was walking, leading his mount, with Yahudha. Jacob looked at the horses and people and said to Yahudha: "Is this the Pharaoh of Egypt?" He said: "No, this is your son."

When each drew near the other, Joseph went to begin with the greeting, but was prevented from doing so, since Jacob had more right to it and was more excellent. So Jacob began the greeting and said: "Peace be upon you, O you who removes sorrows." This is the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said: "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security."﴾

If it is said: how did Joseph say to them, "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security," after they had entered it, when God informed us that when they entered upon Joseph and he embraced his parents, he said this to them as he met them before entering Egypt, as we have mentioned?

Some said: in the verse there is inversion and reordering, and this exception is from the saying of Jacob when he said: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾, and the meaning is: "I will ask my Lord to forgive you, if God wills, indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Then when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself, and said: 'Enter Egypt... in security,' and he raised his parents upon the throne." This is the meaning of the saying of Abu Jarir. Others said: the exception falls on security, not on entering, like His saying: ﴿You shall enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in security﴾ [Sura al-Fath: 27].

And the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) upon entering the graves: "And we, if God wills, will be joining you" [129] [Sahih Muslim: 1/150]. So the exception falls on joining them, not on death. It was also said: "in" here means "when," like His saying: ﴿And leave what remains of usury, if you are believers﴾ [Sura al-Baqarah: 278], and His saying: ﴿You shall be the uppermost, if you are believers﴾ [Sura Al 'Imran: 139], and His saying: ﴿If they desire chastity﴾ [Sura al-Nur: 33].

Ibn 'Abbas said: He only said "in security" because in the past they had feared the kings of Egypt, and did not enter Egypt, for they had no permit. As for His saying "he took his parents to himself": Ibn Ishaq said: his father and his mother. Others said: his father and his maternal aunt, for Rachel, Joseph's mother, had died in childbirth, and Jacob afterward married her sister Liyya; so he called the aunt "mother," just as he called the paternal uncle "father" in His saying: ﴿We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac﴾.

Ishaq related from Bishr, from Sa'id, from al-Hasan, who said: God raised Rachel, Joseph's mother, from her grave until she prostrated, to fulfill the dream.

﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne﴾, on the couch; that is, he seated them upon it. Ibn Ishaq said: it means he raised their status. ﴿And they fell before him in prostration﴾: that is, Jacob, his aunt, and his brothers. At that time the greeting of people was prostration, and by prostration was not meant placing the forehead upon the ground, because that is not permitted except to God, Exalted; it is only bowing and humility as a form of greeting, honor, and salutation, except when it is done in the manner of worship and prayer. This is the saying of al-A'sha ibn Tha'labah:
"When he came to us after the sleep's absence, we prostrated to him and raised the turbans."
Another said:
"Its surplus reins prostrated, as Christians prostrate to their lords."
It was also said: prostration in language means submission, like the saying of al-Nabighah [in the source: Zayd al-Khayl instead of al-Nabighah]:
"With a host in whose lodges the spotted horses are lost; the hills in it are seen prostrating to the hooves."
That is, lowered and humbled.

[Tha'lab] said: "they fell" means "they passed by," and was not meant as falling down and dropping to the ground. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿They did not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾ [Sura al-Furqan: 73]; it only means they did not pass by in that manner. Mujahid: in the sense of passing. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that its meaning is: they fell down to God in prostration, so the "him" refers to God, Exalted.

Joseph then said, and his skin shivered: ﴿This is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true﴾, and that is His saying: ﴿Indeed I saw eleven stars﴾.

They differed about the length of Joseph's absence from Jacob. Al-Kalbi said: two hundred and twenty years. Salman al-Farisi: forty years. Abdullah ibn Shaddad: seventy years. It was also said: seventy-seven years. Al-Hasan said:
Joseph was thrown into the well at seventeen years of age, and was absent from his father eighty years, and lived after his reunion with Jacob twenty-three years, and died at the age of a hundred and twenty years. In the Torah: a hundred and sixteen years. According to Ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar: eighty-seven years. Ibn Abi Ishaq said: eighteen years. Joseph had from the wife of the Aziz: Ephraim, Menasseh, and Rahmah, wife of Job. Between Joseph and Moses were four hundred years.

﴿And He was good to me when He brought me out of the prison﴾; he did not say "out of the well," using courtesy, so as not to remind his brothers of their deed. It was also said: because God's blessing upon him in being saved from prison was greater than His blessing upon him in rescuing him from the well, for his falling into the well was due to his brothers' envy, while his imprisonment was a recompense from God for a slip that had come from him.

﴿And He brought you from the desert﴾, because Jacob and his sons were people of the desert and livestock. "Badw" is the verbal noun of your saying "badā, yabdū, badwan," when one becomes in the desert. ﴿After Satan had stirred discord between me and my brothers﴾. ﴿Indeed my Lord is Gentle, bestowing kindness on whom He wills﴾, knowing the subtleties of matters and their realities. ﴿Indeed He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾.

Abd al-Samad related from his father, from Wahb, who said: They—that is, Jacob and his sons—entered Egypt as seventy-two persons, men and women, and they left with Moses, and their number was six hundred and fifty-some thousand men, besides the offspring, the elderly, and the disabled; and the offspring were a million and two hundred thousand, besides the fighters.

The historians said: Jacob remained in Egypt after his family joined him for twenty-four years in the most pleasant condition and happiest life; then he died in Egypt. When death came to him, he bequeathed to his son Joseph that his body be carried until it was buried beside his father Isaac. Joseph did so, carried it, and buried him in Syria, then returned to Egypt.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he was transported in a chest of teak to Jerusalem, and that coincided with the day Esau died, and they were buried in one grave. Hence the Jews transport their dead to Jerusalem, those of them who do so. Jacob and Esau were born in one womb and buried in one grave, and their age together was a hundred and forty-seven years.
