They said: When God gathered Joseph's family, fulfilled his vision, and cooled his eye, and had made his worldly kingdom and bliss expansive, he knew that this would not last for him and that he must part from it. He desired a bliss more enduring, and his soul longed for Paradise, so he wished for death and supplicated his Lord. No prophet before or after him wished for death, and he said: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom﴾, meaning the kingdom of Egypt, ﴿and taught me of the interpretation of events﴾, meaning the interpretation of dreams. ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their Creator and Maker.

﴿You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter﴾, my helper in this world and the Hereafter, managing my affairs. ﴿Cause me to die a Muslim, and join me with the righteous﴾, with my forefathers the prophets.

It was said: God took him in a good and pure state in Egypt, and he was buried in the Nile in a marble chest. When he died, people quarreled over him, each wanting to be buried in their own quarter, hoping for his blessing, until they gathered to fight. So they decided to bury him in the Nile at the place where the water divides in Egypt, so the water would flow over him and then reach all of Egypt, and they would all share in it equally. They did so.

Salih al-Murri related from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, gathered Jacob's family, his sons withdrew in private conversation. Some said to others: "Do you not know what you did, and what the old man suffered from you, and what Joseph suffered from you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then if they pardon you, but how will you face your Lord?" Their affair settled on coming to the old man, and they sat before him, with Joseph sitting beside his father.

They said: "O our father, we have come to you about a matter we have never come to you about before, and a calamity has befallen us the like of which has never befallen us," until they stirred him, and the prophets (upon them peace) are the most merciful of creatures. He said: "What is wrong with you, my sons?" They said: "Do you not know what we did to you, and what we did to our brother Joseph?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Have you not both pardoned?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Then your pardon will not avail us if God has not pardoned us." He said: "Then what do you want, my sons?" They said:

The sons said: "We want you to pray to God. When the revelation comes from God that He has pardoned them, we will have done it; our eyes will be comforted and our hearts will be at rest. Otherwise, there will never be any comfort for our eyes in this world." So the old man (al-Shaykh) faced the qibla and stood, and Yusuf stood behind his father, and they stood behind the two of them, humbled and submissive. Yaʿqub prayed, and Yusuf said "Amin," but He did not answer them for twenty years.

Salih al-Murri said: He kept them in fear. Then, when the twentieth year came, Jibril descended upon Yaʿqub and said:

"Indeed God, blessed and exalted, sent me to you to give you good news: He has answered your supplication concerning your sons, and He has pardoned what they did. For He has taken their covenants after you concerning prophethood. And that is what you mentioned and what you related to me."

When the caravan departed (that is, went out from the outskirts of Egypt heading toward Canaan), their father said: "Indeed, I sense the scent of Joseph" (it is narrated that the wind asked its Lord for permission to bring Jacob the scent of Joseph before the bearer of good news came to him; permission was granted, and it brought it to him). Ibn al-Suddi related from his father, from Mujahid, who said: Jacob caught the scent of Joseph from a distance of three days, because when the wind blew it stirred the shirt and carried the scent of the shirt to Jacob; he found the scent of Paradise, and knew that there is no scent of Paradise on earth except that it comes from that shirt. Therefore he said: "Indeed I sense the scent of Joseph," and he was eight nights' journey away from him.

Shu'bah related from Abu Sinan, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl say: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Jacob found the scent of Joseph while he was eight nights' journey away from him. Abu Sinan related from Abu Hudhayl, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Jacob found the scent of Joseph, and he was eight nights' journey away from him. Shu'bah related from Abu Sinan, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning this verse, say: He found its scent from a distance equal to that between Basra and Kufa. Al-Hasan said: It was mentioned to us that between them at that time there were eighty farsakhs.

﴿Unless you think me senile﴾ — Sufyan related from Husayf, from Mujahid, concerning "Unless you think me senile" (la wa-la an tufannidun), he said: "you consider the opinion foolish." From Ibn 'Abbas: "you consider me ignorant." Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid: "lest you say, 'your mind has gone.'" Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: "you deem me a liar," which is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "you think me senile," and similarly Israil related from Abu Yahya from Mujahid. Al-Rabi' said: "you consider me a fool." Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak: "you think me senile, so you say: 'an old man who has become senile and lost his mind.'" Ibn Yasar said: "you deem me weak." Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: "you find me repugnant." Al-Kisa'i said: "you deem me incapable." Al-Akhfash said: "you blame me." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "you deem me astray."

The root of tafnid (fannada) is corruption. Al-Nabighah said:
"Except Solomon, when the King said to him: 'Stand in the land and restrain it from tafnid.'"
That is, prevent it from corruption. Hence it is said that blame is tafnid. A poet said:
"O my two companions, leave off my blame and my tafnid; what has passed of a matter cannot be returned."
Jarir ibn 'Atiyyah said:
"O my blamers, leave off reproach and be brief; love has lasted long, and you have prolonged tafnid."
Another said:
"You destroyed me with blame and tafnid."
Al-fand is error in speech and opinion. It is said: afnada fulanan al-dahr, meaning when time corrupted him. From the words of Ibn Muqbil:
"Leave time to do what it wills, for when it charges the people with corruption, it corrupts them."

They said — that is, his grandchildren: ﴿By God, you are surely in your old error﴾, your ancient mistake of loving Joseph and not forgetting him.

﴿Then when the bearer of good news came﴾, the one who brought the message of Joseph. Ibn 'Abbas said: the messenger was Yahudha ibn Ya'qub. Ibn Mas'ud said: "the bearer of good news came from ahead of the caravan." Al-Suddi said: Yahudha said: "I was the one who took the shirt stained with blood to Jacob and told him that Joseph had been eaten by the wolf; today I will take the shirt and tell him he is alive, and gladden him as I saddened him." Ibn 'Abbas said: Yahudha carried it alone, apart from them; he went out bareheaded and barefoot and began to run until he reached his father. He had seven loaves with him, which he had not finished eating, and the distance was eighty farsakhs. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: the bearer of good news was Malik ibn Dhu'r from the people of Madyan.

﴿He cast it﴾, that is, the bearer of good news cast Joseph's shirt over Jacob's face, ﴿and he regained his sight﴾: he returned seeing after having been blind.

'Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related from Abu 'Abdullah al-Sulami, who said: I heard Yahya ibn Muslim, from someone he named, say: Jacob was the most honored of the people of the earth before the Angel of Death, and the Angel of Death asked his Lord for permission to come to Jacob, and was permitted. He came to him, and Jacob said: "O Angel of Death, I ask you by the One who created you: have you taken the soul of Joseph among those you have seized?" He said: "No." The Angel of Death said: "O Jacob, shall I teach you a supplication?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Say: O Possessor of the kindness that never ends and which no one but You can count." So Jacob supplicated with it that night, and the dawn had not risen before he cast the shirt over his face, and he regained his sight. Al-Dahhak said: his sight returned to him after blindness, strength after weakness, youth after decrepitude, and joy after sorrow.

He said: ﴿Did I not tell you that I know from God what you do not know﴾, concerning Joseph's life and that God would reunite us. They said, after that: ﴿O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins; indeed we have been sinners﴾, those who were at fault.

Jacob (upon him peace) said: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾ in the night prayer. Most exegetes said: he delayed it until the last part of the night, because supplication at the time of dawn is not veiled from God. When Jacob reached the appointed time, he advanced to prayer at dawn, and when he finished, he raised his hands to God, the Exalted: "O God, forgive me my grief over Joseph and my lack of patience concerning him, and forgive my sons what they did to Joseph." God revealed to him: "I have forgiven you and them all."

Muharib ibn Dithar said: a paternal uncle of mine used to go to the mosque, and he said: "I passed by the house of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and heard him say: 'O God, You called me and I answered, You commanded me and I obeyed; this is the dawn, so forgive me.'" I asked him about that, and he said: "Jacob delayed the seeking of forgiveness for his sons until the dawn, by his saying: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾."

Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "'I will ask my Lord to forgive you' means: until the coming of the day of Friday" [128]. Wahb said: he would ask forgiveness for them every Friday night for some twenty-odd years. Tawus said: he delayed it until the dawn of Friday night, and that coincided with the night of 'Ashura'.

From Abu Salamah, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, who said: "Seeking needs from a young man is easier than from the elderly. Do you not see Joseph's saying to his brothers: ﴿No reproach upon you today﴾, and Jacob's saying (upon him peace): ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾?"

Abu al-Hasan al-Mulani al-Sha'bi said: "'I will ask my Lord to forgive you': I will ask Joseph; if he pardons you, I will ask my Lord to forgive you." ﴿Indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾.

It is narrated that when the bearer of good news informed Jacob of Joseph's life, Jacob said: "How did you leave Joseph?" He said: "He is king of Egypt." Jacob said: "What do I want with kingship? On what religion did you leave him?" He said: "On the religion of Islam." Jacob said: "Now the blessing is complete."

Al-Thawri said: When Jacob and Joseph (upon them both peace) met, each embraced the other and they both wept. Joseph said: "O father, you wept for me until your sight was lost; did you not know that the Resurrection will gather us?" He said: "Yes, my son, but I feared that your religion would be stolen, and that I would be separated from you."

They said: Joseph had sent with the bearer of good news to Jacob provisions and two hundred riding-camels, and asked Jacob to come to him with all his family and children. Jacob prepared to leave for Egypt. When he drew near Egypt, the king who was above Joseph went out, and Joseph went out with the king among four thousand troops, and the people of Egypt rode with them to meet Jacob. Jacob was walking, leading his mount, with Yahudha. Jacob looked at the horses and people and said to Yahudha: "Is this the Pharaoh of Egypt?" He said: "No, this is your son."

When each drew near the other, Joseph went to begin with the greeting, but was prevented from doing so, since Jacob had more right to it and was more excellent. So Jacob began the greeting and said: "Peace be upon you, O you who removes sorrows." This is the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said: "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security."﴾

If it is said: how did Joseph say to them, "Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security," after they had entered it, when God informed us that when they entered upon Joseph and he embraced his parents, he said this to them as he met them before entering Egypt, as we have mentioned?

Some said: in the verse there is inversion and reordering, and this exception is from the saying of Jacob when he said: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾, and the meaning is: "I will ask my Lord to forgive you, if God wills, indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. Then when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself, and said: 'Enter Egypt... in security,' and he raised his parents upon the throne." This is the meaning of the saying of Abu Jarir. Others said: the exception falls on security, not on entering, like His saying: ﴿You shall enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in security﴾ [Sura al-Fath: 27].

And the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) upon entering the graves: "And we, if God wills, will be joining you" [129] [Sahih Muslim: 1/150]. So the exception falls on joining them, not on death. It was also said: "in" here means "when," like His saying: ﴿And leave what remains of usury, if you are believers﴾ [Sura al-Baqarah: 278], and His saying: ﴿You shall be the uppermost, if you are believers﴾ [Sura Al 'Imran: 139], and His saying: ﴿If they desire chastity﴾ [Sura al-Nur: 33].

Ibn 'Abbas said: He only said "in security" because in the past they had feared the kings of Egypt, and did not enter Egypt, for they had no permit. As for His saying "he took his parents to himself": Ibn Ishaq said: his father and his mother. Others said: his father and his maternal aunt, for Rachel, Joseph's mother, had died in childbirth, and Jacob afterward married her sister Liyya; so he called the aunt "mother," just as he called the paternal uncle "father" in His saying: ﴿We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac﴾.

Ishaq related from Bishr, from Sa'id, from al-Hasan, who said: God raised Rachel, Joseph's mother, from her grave until she prostrated, to fulfill the dream.

﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne﴾, on the couch; that is, he seated them upon it. Ibn Ishaq said: it means he raised their status. ﴿And they fell before him in prostration﴾: that is, Jacob, his aunt, and his brothers. At that time the greeting of people was prostration, and by prostration was not meant placing the forehead upon the ground, because that is not permitted except to God, Exalted; it is only bowing and humility as a form of greeting, honor, and salutation, except when it is done in the manner of worship and prayer. This is the saying of al-A'sha ibn Tha'labah:
"When he came to us after the sleep's absence, we prostrated to him and raised the turbans."
Another said:
"Its surplus reins prostrated, as Christians prostrate to their lords."
It was also said: prostration in language means submission, like the saying of al-Nabighah [in the source: Zayd al-Khayl instead of al-Nabighah]:
"With a host in whose lodges the spotted horses are lost; the hills in it are seen prostrating to the hooves."
That is, lowered and humbled.

[Tha'lab] said: "they fell" means "they passed by," and was not meant as falling down and dropping to the ground. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿They did not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾ [Sura al-Furqan: 73]; it only means they did not pass by in that manner. Mujahid: in the sense of passing. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that its meaning is: they fell down to God in prostration, so the "him" refers to God, Exalted.

Joseph then said, and his skin shivered: ﴿This is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true﴾, and that is His saying: ﴿Indeed I saw eleven stars﴾.

They differed about the length of Joseph's absence from Jacob. Al-Kalbi said: two hundred and twenty years. Salman al-Farisi: forty years. Abdullah ibn Shaddad: seventy years. It was also said: seventy-seven years. Al-Hasan said:
Joseph was thrown into the well at seventeen years of age, and was absent from his father eighty years, and lived after his reunion with Jacob twenty-three years, and died at the age of a hundred and twenty years. In the Torah: a hundred and sixteen years. According to Ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar: eighty-seven years. Ibn Abi Ishaq said: eighteen years. Joseph had from the wife of the Aziz: Ephraim, Menasseh, and Rahmah, wife of Job. Between Joseph and Moses were four hundred years.

﴿And He was good to me when He brought me out of the prison﴾; he did not say "out of the well," using courtesy, so as not to remind his brothers of their deed. It was also said: because God's blessing upon him in being saved from prison was greater than His blessing upon him in rescuing him from the well, for his falling into the well was due to his brothers' envy, while his imprisonment was a recompense from God for a slip that had come from him.

﴿And He brought you from the desert﴾, because Jacob and his sons were people of the desert and livestock. "Badw" is the verbal noun of your saying "badā, yabdū, badwan," when one becomes in the desert. ﴿After Satan had stirred discord between me and my brothers﴾. ﴿Indeed my Lord is Gentle, bestowing kindness on whom He wills﴾, knowing the subtleties of matters and their realities. ﴿Indeed He is the Knowing, the Wise﴾.

Abd al-Samad related from his father, from Wahb, who said: They—that is, Jacob and his sons—entered Egypt as seventy-two persons, men and women, and they left with Moses, and their number was six hundred and fifty-some thousand men, besides the offspring, the elderly, and the disabled; and the offspring were a million and two hundred thousand, besides the fighters.

The historians said: Jacob remained in Egypt after his family joined him for twenty-four years in the most pleasant condition and happiest life; then he died in Egypt. When death came to him, he bequeathed to his son Joseph that his body be carried until it was buried beside his father Isaac. Joseph did so, carried it, and buried him in Syria, then returned to Egypt.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he was transported in a chest of teak to Jerusalem, and that coincided with the day Esau died, and they were buried in one grave. Hence the Jews transport their dead to Jerusalem, those of them who do so. Jacob and Esau were born in one womb and buried in one grave, and their age together was a hundred and forty-seven years.

They said: When God gathered Joseph's family, fulfilled his vision, and cooled his eye, and had made his worldly kingdom and bliss expansive, he knew that this would not last for him and that he must part from it. He desired a bliss more enduring, and his soul longed for Paradise, so he wished for death and supplicated his Lord. No prophet before or after him wished for death, and he said: ﴿My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom﴾, meaning the kingdom of Egypt, ﴿and taught me of the interpretation of events﴾, meaning the interpretation of dreams. ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their Creator and Maker.

﴿You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter﴾, my helper in this world and the Hereafter, managing my affairs. ﴿Cause me to die a Muslim, and join me with the righteous﴾, with my forefathers the prophets.

It was said: God took him in a good and pure state in Egypt, and he was buried in the Nile in a marble chest. When he died, people quarreled over him, each wanting to be buried in their own quarter, hoping for his blessing, until they gathered to fight. So they decided to bury him in the Nile at the place where the water divides in Egypt, so the water would flow over him and then reach all of Egypt, and they would all share in it equally. They did so.

Salih al-Murri related from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, gathered Jacob's family, his sons withdrew in private conversation. Some said to others: "Do you not know what you did, and what the old man suffered from you, and what Joseph suffered from you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then if they pardon you, but how will you face your Lord?" Their affair settled on coming to the old man, and they sat before him, with Joseph sitting beside his father.

They said: "O our father, we have come to you about a matter we have never come to you about before, and a calamity has befallen us the like of which has never befallen us," until they stirred him, and the prophets (upon them peace) are the most merciful of creatures. He said: "What is wrong with you, my sons?" They said: "Do you not know what we did to you, and what we did to our brother Joseph?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Have you not both pardoned?" The two said: "Yes." They said: "Then your pardon will not avail us if God has not pardoned us." He said: "Then what do you want, my sons?" They said:

The sons said: "We want you to pray to God. When the revelation comes from God that He has pardoned them, we will have done it; our eyes will be comforted and our hearts will be at rest. Otherwise, there will never be any comfort for our eyes in this world." So the old man (al-Shaykh) faced the qibla and stood, and Yusuf stood behind his father, and they stood behind the two of them, humbled and submissive. Yaʿqub prayed, and Yusuf said "Amin," but He did not answer them for twenty years.

Salih al-Murri said: He kept them in fear. Then, when the twentieth year came, Jibril descended upon Yaʿqub and said:

"Indeed God, blessed and exalted, sent me to you to give you good news: He has answered your supplication concerning your sons, and He has pardoned what they did. For He has taken their covenants after you concerning prophethood. And that is what you mentioned and what you related to me."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 12, verses 102–111:**

﴿That is among the news of the unseen which We reveal to you.﴾ The address is to the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

﴿And you were not with them﴾, meaning: O Muhammad, you were not with the sons of Ya'qub ﴿when they resolved upon their plan﴾, that is, when they agreed to cast Yusuf into the depths of the well, ﴿while they were scheming﴾ against Yusuf.

﴿And most of the people, even if you should strive, will not be believers.﴾

﴿And you do not ask them for any payment for it﴾, that is, for conveying the message and calling to God, ﴿any reward﴾, meaning any wage or recompense. ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the revelation are nothing but admonition and reminder for all the worlds.

﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning how many a statement containing admonition, lesson and indication, ﴿they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾, meaning they do not reflect upon it and do not take heed from it.

Al-Harith ibn Qudama reported from Ikrima that he recited ﴿wal-ard yamurrūna ʿalayhā﴾ with the ending in the nominative (ar-ard, raf'), i.e. the reading ﴿and the earth﴾ as a nominative. From Muhammad ibn Umar, who said: I heard ʿAmr ibn Wa'il recite ﴿wa-kaʾayyin min āyatin fī s-samāwāti﴾ with the word āyah in the unmarked (qat') form, and ﴿wal-arḍu yamurrūna ʿalayhā﴾ in the nominative. Abu Hamza al-Thumali reported from al-Suddi that he recited ﴿wal-arḍa yamurrūna ʿalayhā﴾ in the accusative (nasb), and he recited ﴿yamurrūna ʿala l-arḍ﴾ ("they pass over the earth"). It is also reported from Ibn Mujahid, who said: Ishaq al-Harbi Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: And ʿAbdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) recited: ﴿wa-kaʾayyin min āyatin fī s-samāwāti wal-arḍi yamshūna ʿalayhā﴾ ("they walk upon it").

﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him.﴾ Ikrima, regarding the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him﴾, said: Their belief is that when they are asked, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they say, "God," and when they are asked, "Who sends down the rain?" they say, "God," yet they still associate others with Him. Jabir reported from Ikrima and ʿAmir regarding the same verse that they both said: They believe in God, that He is their Lord and their Creator, yet they associate others with Him. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Ibn Jubayr reported from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the talbiyah (the invocation recited in pilgrimage) of the idolaters of the Arabs. They would say in their talbiyah: "Here I am, O God, You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You; You own him and what he owns." In their talbiyah there was also a verse mocking the one who recites it: "O God, answer, unless Bakr, besides you, the Banu Ghatafan, and they are beside you, descend upon the people and humiliate you, and the Ghanij of us has not ceased to come to you." The talbiyah of the people of the sacred precinct (Hurum) was: "We have come out as your servants, the people of a valley, and they are your dependents (taladuk). They built your lands in ancient times, and they have turned hostile to whoever opposes you." The talbiyah of Quraysh was: [O God, here I am; You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You; You own him and what he owns.] [Addition from Akhbar Makka of al-Azraqi: 194, and Tarikh Dimashq: 19/501; the phrase is illegible in the manuscript.] The talbiyah of Hamdan, Ghassan, Qudaʿa, Judham, Talqin and Bahra was: "We are your servants, Yemen; we come to you twice on the path of deliverance; we oppose ..., we have come to you as a guide." [al-Yaʿqubi recorded the talbiyah of each Arab tribe in detail; see his Tarikh 1/255, where there are differences from what the author mentions here.] Then God revealed: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him﴾, meaning in the talbiyah.

And it is said: When the idolaters heard what preceded this verse of verses, they said: "We believe in God who created these things, but we claim that He has a partner." So God the Exalted revealed this verse.

ʿAta: This refers to supplication (duʿaʾ). The disbelievers associated others with their Lord in ease, but when calamity befell them they became sincere in supplication. Its proof is the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And they thought that they were encompassed, [then] they called upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:22], and His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shade, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Surah Luqman 31:32], and His saying: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:12], and His saying: ﴿And when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication﴾ [Surah Fussilat 41:51].

Some of the people of meaning (ahl al-maʿani) said: Its meaning is: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him﴾ before their belief. Its parallel is the saying of God: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them, who were greater than them in strength﴾ [Surah Qaf 50:36], meaning they had been greater than them in might.

Wahb said: This refers to the event of the smoke (wiqʿat ad-dukhan). When the people of Makka were covered by the smoke in the years of drought, they said: ﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers﴾ [Surah ad-Dukhan 44:12]. That was their "belief" and their gratitude, then they returned to disbelief after the punishment was lifted. Its proof is His saying: ﴿Indeed, you will return [to disbelief]﴾ [Surah ad-Dukhan 44:15]. And return (ʿawd) cannot occur except after a beginning. God knows best.

﴿Then do they feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming (ghashiyah) punishment from God?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: ghashiyah means something that envelops (mujallalah). Mujahid said: a punishment that covers them. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿The day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ [Surah al-ʿAnkabut 29:55]. Qatada said: a calamity (waqʿah). Al-Dahhak said: it means thunderbolts and crashing blows (al-sawaʿiq wal-qawariʿ).

﴿Or that the Hour will come upon them suddenly while they perceive not﴾, meaning the Resurrection, while they do not feel its approach. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Cry will be sounded among the people while they are in their markets.

Say to them, O Muhammad: ﴿This is my way﴾, that is, this call which I make and this path upon which I am, ﴿my sunnah and my manhaj (method)﴾. Ibn Zayd said this. Al-Rabiʿ said: my call (daʿwati). Al-Dahhak said: my supplication (duʿaʾi). Muqatil said: my religion (dini). Its parallel is the saying of God: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:125], meaning His religion.

﴿I invite to God with insight (ʿala basirah)﴾, that is, upon certainty. It is said: So-and-so is mustabsir in such-and-such, meaning certain of it. ﴿I and whoever follows me﴾, meaning whoever believed in me and affirmed me, ﴿also invites to God.﴾ This is the saying of al-Kalbi. Ibn Zayd said: By God, whoever follows him is most deserving that he call to what he called to, mentioning the Qur'an and good instruction, and forbidding the disobedience of God.

It is said: Its meaning is: I and whoever follows me are upon insight. The meaning is that just as I am upon insight, so too whoever believed in me and followed me is upon insight. Ibn ʿAbbas said: That refers to the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), who were upon the best path and the most direct guidance, the source of knowledge, the treasure of faith, and the army of the Most Merciful.

﴿And glory be to God﴾, meaning: and say, "Glory be to God," exalting Him above what they associate with Him. ﴿And I am not of those who associate others with God.﴾

﴿And We did not send before you [O Muhammad] except men﴾, not angels, ﴿to whom We revealed, from among the people of the cities﴾, meaning from among the people of the settled towns, not the people of the desert, because the people of the towns are more intelligent, more virtuous, more knowledgeable and more forbearing.

﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾ That is, these idolaters who deny your prophethood. He informs of the affair of the earlier disbelieving nations so that they might take heed. ﴿And the Home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God.﴾ God, glorified is His praise, says: This is what We did in this world to the people of Our guardianship and obedience, that We delivered them at the descent of the punishment; and what is in the Home of the Hereafter is better for them. So the previously mentioned element was omitted because the context indicates it. The "home" is attributed to "the Hereafter" without any disagreement, for its glorification, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is the truth of certainty﴾ [Surah al-Waqiʿah 56:95], and the expressions "the first year" (ʿam al-awwal), "the last night" (barihat al-ula), and "Thursday" and "Rabiʿ al-akhir" (where the adjective is attached to the noun in a similar manner). The poet said:

Even if the dwellings of ʿAbs were to be effaced upon you,
You would recognize humiliation with the recognition of certainty.

Meaning: recognition (ʿirfanan).

﴿Will they not reason?﴾, meaning, will they not believe?

﴿Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our victory came to them.﴾ The reciters differed regarding His saying: ﴿kudhibū﴾ (they had been denied).

A group read it with light vocalization (takhfif) [Refer to Tafsir al-Qurtubi 9/275 and Zad al-Masir; there is difference in the names, so consider carefully]. This is the reading of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (ʿalayhi s-salam), Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Masʿud, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, ʿIkrima, al-Dahhak, ʿAlqama, Masruq, al-Nakhaʿi, Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, al-Aʿmash, ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar al-Hamdani, Abu Ishaq al-Subaʿi, Ibn Abi Layla, ʿAsim, Hamza, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn and his son Muhammad ibn ʿAli and his son Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, ʿAbdullah ibn Muslim, and Ibn Yasar. Al-Kisa'i and Abu ʿUbayda chose it.

It is reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he recited ﴿wa-ẓannū annahum qad kudhibū﴾ with light vocalization. This is also the reading of ʿAʾisha, [Hurqul] al-Aʿraj, Nafiʿ, al-Zuhri, ʿAta ibn Abi Rabah, ʿAbdullah ibn Kathir, ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith, Abu Rajaʾ and al-Hasan. Also of Qatada, Abu ʿAmr, ʿIsa, Salam, ʿAmr ibn Maymun, and Yaʿqub; and it is also reported from the Prophet (ﷺ).

As for one who reads with light vocalization, its meaning is: until, when the messengers despaired of the faith of their people, and their people thought that the messengers had lied to them regarding the existence of the punishment.

Shuʿayb ibn al-Hajjaj reported from Ibrahim from Abu Hamza al-Jazari, who said: I prepared food and invited some of our companions, including Saʿid ibn Jubayr. I sent to al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, but he refused to come to me, so I went to him and did not leave him until he came. He said: A young man from Quraysh asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr, saying: "O Abu ʿAbd Allah, how do you read this word? When I reach it I wish I did not read this surah: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought they had been denied﴾." He said: Yes, [it means] until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing them, and the ones they were sent to thought the messengers had lied to them.

He said: Al-Dahhak said: I have never seen a man today who is called to knowledge and hesitates. If I had traveled to Yemen for this alone, it would have been little.

Some said: The meaning of the verse according to this reading is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾ of the faith of their people, and the messengers thought that they had been denied in what they found of victory. This is the report of Ibn Abi Mulayka from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: They had called, and they became weak and despaired, and thought they had been let down. Then the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him say, "When is the victory of God?"﴾ and so on.

As for one who reads with heavy vocalization (tashdid), its meaning is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing in them, and the messengers became certain (istayqanat) that their nations had denied them, Our victory came to them.﴾ According to this interpretation, ẓann (thought) carries the meaning of ʿilm (knowledge) and yaqin (certainty), like the saying of the poet:

So I said to them, "Be certain (ẓannū) of two thousand armored men,
their nobles in the woven Persian mail."

That is: be certain. This is the meaning of the statement of Qatada.

Some said: The meaning of the verse according to this reading is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of those among their people who denied them from believing them, and the messengers thought that those who had believed in them and affirmed them had denied them and apostatized from their religion because of their slowness in victory, Our victory came to them.﴾ This is the meaning of the statement of ʿAʾisha.

Mujahid read ﴿kudhibū﴾ with a fatha on the kaf and the dhal, lightened, and it has two interpretations. One: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired that their people would be punished, and their people thought that the messengers had lied, the messengers came, Our victory came.﴾ The second: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of their people's faith, and the messengers thought that their people had lied against God through their disbelief.﴾ On this interpretation, ẓann means certainty. God knows best.

﴿So whom We willed was delivered﴾, at the descent of the punishment, and they are the obedient and the believers. ﴿And Our punishment is not repelled from the criminal people﴾, meaning the idolaters.

The reciters differed regarding His saying: ﴿fa-nujjiya﴾ (so whom We willed was delivered). The majority of reciters read it as ﴿fa-nunajjī﴾ with two nuns, meaning: So We do this to them. Al-Kisa'i assimilated one of the two nuns into the other and read ﴿fa-nujjiya﴾ with one nun and a shadda on the jim. ʿAsim read it with a damma on the nun, a shadda on the jim, and a fatha on the ya, in the passive form (madhhab ma lam yusammi fa'iluhu). Abu ʿUbayd chose this reading because it is in the codex of ʿUthman, and the codices of the other regions have one nun. Ibn Muhaysin read ﴿fa-najā man nashāʾ﴾ with a fatha on the nun and light vocalization, as a past verb. Its grammatical position (mahalluhu) is nominative in the reading of ʿAsim and Ibn Muhaysin, and accusative in the reading of the rest.

﴿Certainly there was in their stories a lesson for those of understanding.﴾ That is, in the account of Yusuf and his brothers there is admonition for the people of understanding. ﴿It was not a narration invented (yuftara)﴾, meaning the Qur'an is not something fabricated, ﴿but a confirmation of what was before it﴾, meaning the scriptures that came before it, ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things﴾ needed by the servants, ﴿and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.﴾

﴿Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our victory came to them.﴾ The reciters differed regarding His saying: ﴿kudhibū﴾ (they had been denied).

A group read it with light vocalization (takhfif) [Refer to Tafsir al-Qurtubi 9/275 and Zad al-Masir; there is difference in the names, so consider carefully]. This is the reading of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (ʿalayhi s-salam), Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Masʿud, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, ʿIkrima, al-Dahhak, ʿAlqama, Masruq, al-Nakhaʿi, Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, al-Aʿmash, ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar al-Hamdani, Abu Ishaq al-Subaʿi, Ibn Abi Layla, ʿAsim, Hamza, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn and his son Muhammad ibn ʿAli and his son Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, ʿAbdullah ibn Muslim, and Ibn Yasar. Al-Kisa'i and Abu ʿUbayda chose it.

This is also the reading of ʿAʾisha, [Hurqul] al-Aʿraj, Nafiʿ, al-Zuhri, ʿAta ibn Abi Rabah, ʿAbdullah ibn Kathir, ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith, Abu Rajaʾ and al-Hasan. I sent to al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, but he refused to come to me, so I went to him and did not leave him until he came. He said: A young man from Quraysh asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr, saying: "O Abu ʿAbd Allah, how do you read this word? When I reach it I wish I did not read this surah: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought they had been denied﴾." He said: Yes, [it means] until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing them, and the ones they were sent to thought the messengers had lied to them.

He said: Al-Dahhak said: I have never seen a man today who is called to knowledge and hesitates. If I had traveled to Yemen for this alone, it would have been little.

This is the report of Ibn Abi Mulayka from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: They had called, and they became weak and despaired, and thought they had been let down. That is: be certain. This is the meaning of the statement of Qatada.

﴿So whom We willed was delivered﴾, at the descent of the punishment, and they are the obedient and the believers. ﴿And Our punishment is not repelled from the criminal people﴾, meaning the idolaters.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 12, verses 102–111:**

﴿That is among the news of the unseen which We reveal to you.﴾ The address is to the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

﴿And most of the people, even if you should strive, will not be believers.﴾

﴿And you do not ask them for any payment for it﴾, that is, for conveying the message and calling to God, ﴿any reward﴾, meaning any wage or recompense. ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the revelation are nothing but admonition and reminder for all the worlds.

Al-Harith ibn Qudama reported from Ikrima that he recited ﴿wal-ard yamurrūna ʿalayhā﴾ with the ending in the nominative (ar-ard, raf'), i.e. the reading ﴿and the earth﴾ as a nominative. Abu Hamza al-Thumali reported from al-Suddi that he recited ﴿wal-arḍa yamurrūna ʿalayhā﴾ in the accusative (nasb), and he recited ﴿yamurrūna ʿala l-arḍ﴾ ("they pass over the earth"). It is also reported from Ibn Mujahid, who said: Ishaq al-Harbi Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: And ʿAbdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) recited: ﴿wa-kaʾayyin min āyatin fī s-samāwāti wal-arḍi yamshūna ʿalayhā﴾ ("they walk upon it").

﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him.﴾ Ikrima, regarding the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him﴾, said: Their belief is that when they are asked, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they say, "God," and when they are asked, "Who sends down the rain?" they say, "God," yet they still associate others with Him. Jabir reported from Ikrima and ʿAmir regarding the same verse that they both said: They believe in God, that He is their Lord and their Creator, yet they associate others with Him. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Ibn Jubayr reported from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the talbiyah (the invocation recited in pilgrimage) of the idolaters of the Arabs. They would say in their talbiyah: "Here I am, O God, You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You; You own him and what he owns." In their talbiyah there was also a verse mocking the one who recites it: "O God, answer, unless Bakr, besides you, the Banu Ghatafan, and they are beside you, descend upon the people and humiliate you, and the Ghanij of us has not ceased to come to you." The talbiyah of the people of the sacred precinct (Hurum) was: "We have come out as your servants, the people of a valley, and they are your dependents (taladuk). They built your lands in ancient times, and they have turned hostile to whoever opposes you." The talbiyah of Quraysh was: [O God, here I am; You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You; You own him and what he owns.] [Addition from Akhbar Makka of al-Azraqi: 194, and Tarikh Dimashq: 19/501; the phrase is illegible in the manuscript.] The talbiyah of Hamdan, Ghassan, Qudaʿa, Judham, Talqin and Bahra was: "We are your servants, Yemen; we come to you twice on the path of deliverance; we oppose ..., we have come to you as a guide." [al-Yaʿqubi recorded the talbiyah of each Arab tribe in detail; see his Tarikh 1/255, where there are differences from what the author mentions here.] Then God revealed: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him﴾, meaning in the talbiyah.

And it is said: When the idolaters heard what preceded this verse of verses, they said: "We believe in God who created these things, but we claim that He has a partner." So God the Exalted revealed this verse.

Its proof is the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And they thought that they were encompassed, [then] they called upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:22], and His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shade, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Surah Luqman 31:32], and His saying: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:12], and His saying: ﴿And when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication﴾ [Surah Fussilat 41:51].

Some of the people of meaning (ahl al-maʿani) said: Its meaning is: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him﴾ before their belief. Its parallel is the saying of God: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them, who were greater than them in strength﴾ [Surah Qaf 50:36], meaning they had been greater than them in might.

Wahb said: This refers to the event of the smoke (wiqʿat ad-dukhan). When the people of Makka were covered by the smoke in the years of drought, they said: ﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers﴾ [Surah ad-Dukhan 44:12]. That was their "belief" and their gratitude, then they returned to disbelief after the punishment was lifted. Its proof is His saying: ﴿Indeed, you will return [to disbelief]﴾ [Surah ad-Dukhan 44:15]. And return (ʿawd) cannot occur except after a beginning. God knows best.

﴿Then do they feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming (ghashiyah) punishment from God?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: ghashiyah means something that envelops (mujallalah). Mujahid said: a punishment that covers them. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿The day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ [Surah al-ʿAnkabut 29:55]. Qatada said: a calamity (waqʿah). Al-Dahhak said: it means thunderbolts and crashing blows (al-sawaʿiq wal-qawariʿ).

﴿Or that the Hour will come upon them suddenly while they perceive not﴾, meaning the Resurrection, while they do not feel its approach. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Cry will be sounded among the people while they are in their markets.

﴿I invite to God with insight (ʿala basirah)﴾, that is, upon certainty. It is said: So-and-so is mustabsir in such-and-such, meaning certain of it. ﴿I and whoever follows me﴾, meaning whoever believed in me and affirmed me, ﴿also invites to God.﴾ This is the saying of al-Kalbi. Ibn ʿAbbas said: That refers to the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), who were upon the best path and the most direct guidance, the source of knowledge, the treasure of faith, and the army of the Most Merciful.

﴿And glory be to God﴾, meaning: and say, "Glory be to God," exalting Him above what they associate with Him. ﴿And I am not of those who associate others with God.﴾

﴿And We did not send before you [O Muhammad] except men﴾, not angels, ﴿to whom We revealed, from among the people of the cities﴾, meaning from among the people of the settled towns, not the people of the desert, because the people of the towns are more intelligent, more virtuous, more knowledgeable and more forbearing.

﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾ That is, these idolaters who deny your prophethood. He informs of the affair of the earlier disbelieving nations so that they might take heed. ﴿And the Home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God.﴾ God, glorified is His praise, says: This is what We did in this world to the people of Our guardianship and obedience, that We delivered them at the descent of the punishment; and what is in the Home of the Hereafter is better for them. So the previously mentioned element was omitted because the context indicates it. The "home" is attributed to "the Hereafter" without any disagreement, for its glorification, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is the truth of certainty﴾ [Surah al-Waqiʿah 56:95], and the expressions "the first year" (ʿam al-awwal), "the last night" (barihat al-ula), and "Thursday" and "Rabiʿ al-akhir" (where the adjective is attached to the noun in a similar manner). The poet said:

Even if the dwellings of ʿAbs were to be effaced upon you,
You would recognize humiliation with the recognition of certainty.

Meaning: recognition (ʿirfanan).

﴿Will they not reason?﴾, meaning, will they not believe?

Its proof is the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And they thought that they were encompassed, [then] they called upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:22], and His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shade, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Surah Luqman 31:32], and His saying: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:12], and His saying: ﴿And when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication﴾ [Surah Fussilat 41:51].

Some of the people of meaning (ahl al-maʿani) said: Its meaning is: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him﴾ before their belief. Its parallel is the saying of God: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them, who were greater than them in strength﴾ [Surah Qaf 50:36], meaning they had been greater than them in might.

Wahb said: This refers to the event of the smoke (wiqʿat ad-dukhan). When the people of Makka were covered by the smoke in the years of drought, they said: ﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers﴾ [Surah ad-Dukhan 44:12]. That was their "belief" and their gratitude, then they returned to disbelief after the punishment was lifted. Its proof is His saying: ﴿Indeed, you will return [to disbelief]﴾ [Surah ad-Dukhan 44:15]. And return (ʿawd) cannot occur except after a beginning. God knows best.

﴿Then do they feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming (ghashiyah) punishment from God?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: ghashiyah means something that envelops (mujallalah). Mujahid said: a punishment that covers them. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿The day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ [Surah al-ʿAnkabut 29:55]. Qatada said: a calamity (waqʿah). Al-Dahhak said: it means thunderbolts and crashing blows (al-sawaʿiq wal-qawariʿ).

﴿Or that the Hour will come upon them suddenly while they perceive not﴾, meaning the Resurrection, while they do not feel its approach. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Cry will be sounded among the people while they are in their markets.

Say to them, O Muhammad: ﴿This is my way﴾, that is, this call which I make and this path upon which I am, ﴿my sunnah and my manhaj (method)﴾. Ibn Zayd said this. Al-Rabiʿ said: my call (daʿwati). Al-Dahhak said: my supplication (duʿaʾi). Muqatil said: my religion (dini). Its parallel is the saying of God: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:125], meaning His religion.

﴿I invite to God with insight (ʿala basirah)﴾, that is, upon certainty. It is said: So-and-so is mustabsir in such-and-such, meaning certain of it. ﴿I and whoever follows me﴾, meaning whoever believed in me and affirmed me, ﴿also invites to God.﴾ This is the saying of al-Kalbi. Ibn Zayd said: By God, whoever follows him is most deserving that he call to what he called to, mentioning the Qur'an and good instruction, and forbidding the disobedience of God.

It is said: Its meaning is: I and whoever follows me are upon insight. The meaning is that just as I am upon insight, so too whoever believed in me and followed me is upon insight. Ibn ʿAbbas said: That refers to the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), who were upon the best path and the most direct guidance, the source of knowledge, the treasure of faith, and the army of the Most Merciful.

﴿And glory be to God﴾, meaning: and say, "Glory be to God," exalting Him above what they associate with Him. ﴿And I am not of those who associate others with God.﴾

﴿And We did not send before you [O Muhammad] except men﴾, not angels, ﴿to whom We revealed, from among the people of the cities﴾, meaning from among the people of the settled towns, not the people of the desert, because the people of the towns are more intelligent, more virtuous, more knowledgeable and more forbearing.

﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾ That is, these idolaters who deny your prophethood. He informs of the affair of the earlier disbelieving nations so that they might take heed. ﴿And the Home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God.﴾ God, glorified is His praise, says: This is what We did in this world to the people of Our guardianship and obedience, that We delivered them at the descent of the punishment; and what is in the Home of the Hereafter is better for them. So the previously mentioned element was omitted because the context indicates it. The "home" is attributed to "the Hereafter" without any disagreement, for its glorification, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is the truth of certainty﴾ [Surah al-Waqiʿah 56:95], and the expressions "the first year" (ʿam al-awwal), "the last night" (barihat al-ula), and "Thursday" and "Rabiʿ al-akhir" (where the adjective is attached to the noun in a similar manner). The poet said:

Even if the dwellings of ʿAbs were to be effaced upon you,
You would recognize humiliation with the recognition of certainty.

Meaning: recognition (ʿirfanan).

﴿Will they not reason?﴾, meaning, will they not believe?

﴿Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our victory came to them.﴾ The reciters differed regarding His saying: ﴿kudhibū﴾ (they had been denied).

A group read it with light vocalization (takhfif) [Refer to Tafsir al-Qurtubi 9/275 and Zad al-Masir; there is difference in the names, so consider carefully]. This is the reading of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (ʿalayhi s-salam), Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Masʿud, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, ʿIkrima, al-Dahhak, ʿAlqama, Masruq, al-Nakhaʿi, Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, al-Aʿmash, ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar al-Hamdani, Abu Ishaq al-Subaʿi, Ibn Abi Layla, ʿAsim, Hamza, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn and his son Muhammad ibn ʿAli and his son Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, ʿAbdullah ibn Muslim, and Ibn Yasar. Al-Kisa'i and Abu ʿUbayda chose it.

It is reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he recited ﴿wa-ẓannū annahum qad kudhibū﴾ with light vocalization. This is also the reading of ʿAʾisha, [Hurqul] al-Aʿraj, Nafiʿ, al-Zuhri, ʿAta ibn Abi Rabah, ʿAbdullah ibn Kathir, ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith, Abu Rajaʾ and al-Hasan. Also of Qatada, Abu ʿAmr, ʿIsa, Salam, ʿAmr ibn Maymun, and Yaʿqub; and it is also reported from the Prophet (ﷺ).

As for one who reads with light vocalization, its meaning is: until, when the messengers despaired of the faith of their people, and their people thought that the messengers had lied to them regarding the existence of the punishment.

Shuʿayb ibn al-Hajjaj reported from Ibrahim from Abu Hamza al-Jazari, who said: I prepared food and invited some of our companions, including Saʿid ibn Jubayr. I sent to al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, but he refused to come to me, so I went to him and did not leave him until he came. He said: A young man from Quraysh asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr, saying: "O Abu ʿAbd Allah, how do you read this word? When I reach it I wish I did not read this surah: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought they had been denied﴾." He said: Yes, [it means] until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing them, and the ones they were sent to thought the messengers had lied to them.

He said: Al-Dahhak said: I have never seen a man today who is called to knowledge and hesitates. If I had traveled to Yemen for this alone, it would have been little.

Some said: The meaning of the verse according to this reading is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾ of the faith of their people, and the messengers thought that they had been denied in what they found of victory. This is the report of Ibn Abi Mulayka from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: They had called, and they became weak and despaired, and thought they had been let down. Then the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him say, "When is the victory of God?"﴾ and so on.

As for one who reads with heavy vocalization (tashdid), its meaning is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing in them, and the messengers became certain (istayqanat) that their nations had denied them, Our victory came to them.﴾ According to this interpretation, ẓann (thought) carries the meaning of ʿilm (knowledge) and yaqin (certainty), like the saying of the poet:

So I said to them, "Be certain (ẓannū) of two thousand armored men,
their nobles in the woven Persian mail."

That is: be certain. This is the meaning of the statement of Qatada.

Some said: The meaning of the verse according to this reading is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of those among their people who denied them from believing them, and the messengers thought that those who had believed in them and affirmed them had denied them and apostatized from their religion because of their slowness in victory, Our victory came to them.﴾ This is the meaning of the statement of ʿAʾisha.

Mujahid read ﴿kudhibū﴾ with a fatha on the kaf and the dhal, lightened, and it has two interpretations. One: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired that their people would be punished, and their people thought that the messengers had lied, the messengers came, Our victory came.﴾ The second: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of their people's faith, and the messengers thought that their people had lied against God through their disbelief.﴾ On this interpretation, ẓann means certainty. God knows best.

﴿So whom We willed was delivered﴾, at the descent of the punishment, and they are the obedient and the believers. ﴿And Our punishment is not repelled from the criminal people﴾, meaning the idolaters.

The reciters differed regarding His saying: ﴿fa-nujjiya﴾ (so whom We willed was delivered). The majority of reciters read it as ﴿fa-nunajjī﴾ with two nuns, meaning: So We do this to them. Al-Kisa'i assimilated one of the two nuns into the other and read ﴿fa-nujjiya﴾ with one nun and a shadda on the jim. ʿAsim read it with a damma on the nun, a shadda on the jim, and a fatha on the ya, in the passive form (madhhab ma lam yusammi fa'iluhu). Ibn Muhaysin read ﴿fa-najā man nashāʾ﴾ with a fatha on the nun and light vocalization, as a past verb. Its grammatical position (mahalluhu) is nominative in the reading of ʿAsim and Ibn Muhaysin, and accusative in the reading of the rest.

﴿Certainly there was in their stories a lesson for those of understanding.﴾ That is, in the account of Yusuf and his brothers there is admonition for the people of understanding. ﴿It was not a narration invented (yuftara)﴾, meaning the Qur'an is not something fabricated, ﴿but a confirmation of what was before it﴾, meaning the scriptures that came before it, ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things﴾ needed by the servants, ﴿and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 12, verses 102–111:**

﴿And most of the people, even if you should strive, will not be believers.﴾

﴿And you do not ask them for any payment for it﴾, that is, for conveying the message and calling to God, ﴿any reward﴾, meaning any wage or recompense. ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the revelation are nothing but admonition and reminder for all the worlds.

﴿Certainly there was in their stories a lesson for those of understanding.﴾ That is, in the account of Yusuf and his brothers there is admonition for the people of understanding. ﴿It was not a narration invented (yuftara)﴾, meaning the Qur'an is not something fabricated, ﴿but a confirmation of what was before it﴾, meaning the scriptures that came before it, ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things﴾ needed by the servants, ﴿and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 12, verses 102–111:**

﴿That is among the news of the unseen which We reveal to you.﴾ The address is to the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

﴿And you were not with them﴾, meaning: O Muhammad, you were not with the sons of Ya'qub ﴿when they resolved upon their plan﴾, that is, when they agreed to cast Yusuf into the depths of the well, ﴿while they were scheming﴾ against Yusuf.

﴿And most of the people, even if you should strive, will not be believers.﴾

﴿And you do not ask them for any payment for it﴾, that is, for conveying the message and calling to God, ﴿any reward﴾, meaning any wage or recompense. ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the revelation are nothing but admonition and reminder for all the worlds.

﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning how many a statement containing admonition, lesson and indication, ﴿they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾, meaning they do not reflect upon it and do not take heed from it.

Al-Harith ibn Qudama reported from Ikrima that he recited ﴿wal-ard yamurrūna ʿalayhā﴾ with the ending in the nominative (ar-ard, raf'), i.e. the reading ﴿and the earth﴾ as a nominative. From Muhammad ibn Umar, who said: I heard ʿAmr ibn Wa'il recite ﴿wa-kaʾayyin min āyatin fī s-samāwāti﴾ with the word āyah in the unmarked (qat') form, and ﴿wal-arḍu yamurrūna ʿalayhā﴾ in the nominative. Abu Hamza al-Thumali reported from al-Suddi that he recited ﴿wal-arḍa yamurrūna ʿalayhā﴾ in the accusative (nasb), and he recited ﴿yamurrūna ʿala l-arḍ﴾ ("they pass over the earth"). It is also reported from Ibn Mujahid, who said: Ishaq al-Harbi Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: And ʿAbdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) recited: ﴿wa-kaʾayyin min āyatin fī s-samāwāti wal-arḍi yamshūna ʿalayhā﴾ ("they walk upon it").

﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him.﴾ Ikrima, regarding the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him﴾, said: Their belief is that when they are asked, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they say, "God," and when they are asked, "Who sends down the rain?" they say, "God," yet they still associate others with Him. Jabir reported from Ikrima and ʿAmir regarding the same verse that they both said: They believe in God, that He is their Lord and their Creator, yet they associate others with Him. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Ibn Jubayr reported from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the talbiyah (the invocation recited in pilgrimage) of the idolaters of the Arabs. They would say in their talbiyah: "Here I am, O God, You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You; You own him and what he owns." In their talbiyah there was also a verse mocking the one who recites it: "O God, answer, unless Bakr, besides you, the Banu Ghatafan, and they are beside you, descend upon the people and humiliate you, and the Ghanij of us has not ceased to come to you." The talbiyah of the people of the sacred precinct (Hurum) was: "We have come out as your servants, the people of a valley, and they are your dependents (taladuk). They built your lands in ancient times, and they have turned hostile to whoever opposes you." The talbiyah of Quraysh was: [O God, here I am; You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You; You own him and what he owns.] [Addition from Akhbar Makka of al-Azraqi: 194, and Tarikh Dimashq: 19/501; the phrase is illegible in the manuscript.] The talbiyah of Hamdan, Ghassan, Qudaʿa, Judham, Talqin and Bahra was: "We are your servants, Yemen; we come to you twice on the path of deliverance; we oppose ..., we have come to you as a guide." [al-Yaʿqubi recorded the talbiyah of each Arab tribe in detail; see his Tarikh 1/255, where there are differences from what the author mentions here.] Then God revealed: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him﴾, meaning in the talbiyah.

And it is said: When the idolaters heard what preceded this verse of verses, they said: "We believe in God who created these things, but we claim that He has a partner." So God the Exalted revealed this verse.

ʿAta: This refers to supplication (duʿaʾ). The disbelievers associated others with their Lord in ease, but when calamity befell them they became sincere in supplication. Its proof is the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And they thought that they were encompassed, [then] they called upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:22], and His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shade, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Surah Luqman 31:32], and His saying: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:12], and His saying: ﴿And when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication﴾ [Surah Fussilat 41:51].

Some of the people of meaning (ahl al-maʿani) said: Its meaning is: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they are associating others with Him﴾ before their belief. Its parallel is the saying of God: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them, who were greater than them in strength﴾ [Surah Qaf 50:36], meaning they had been greater than them in might.

Wahb said: This refers to the event of the smoke (wiqʿat ad-dukhan). When the people of Makka were covered by the smoke in the years of drought, they said: ﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers﴾ [Surah ad-Dukhan 44:12]. That was their "belief" and their gratitude, then they returned to disbelief after the punishment was lifted. Its proof is His saying: ﴿Indeed, you will return [to disbelief]﴾ [Surah ad-Dukhan 44:15]. And return (ʿawd) cannot occur except after a beginning. God knows best.

﴿Then do they feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming (ghashiyah) punishment from God?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: ghashiyah means something that envelops (mujallalah). Mujahid said: a punishment that covers them. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿The day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ [Surah al-ʿAnkabut 29:55]. Qatada said: a calamity (waqʿah). Al-Dahhak said: it means thunderbolts and crashing blows (al-sawaʿiq wal-qawariʿ).

﴿Or that the Hour will come upon them suddenly while they perceive not﴾, meaning the Resurrection, while they do not feel its approach. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Cry will be sounded among the people while they are in their markets.

Say to them, O Muhammad: ﴿This is my way﴾, that is, this call which I make and this path upon which I am, ﴿my sunnah and my manhaj (method)﴾. Ibn Zayd said this. Al-Rabiʿ said: my call (daʿwati). Al-Dahhak said: my supplication (duʿaʾi). Muqatil said: my religion (dini). Its parallel is the saying of God: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:125], meaning His religion.

﴿I invite to God with insight (ʿala basirah)﴾, that is, upon certainty. It is said: So-and-so is mustabsir in such-and-such, meaning certain of it. ﴿I and whoever follows me﴾, meaning whoever believed in me and affirmed me, ﴿also invites to God.﴾ This is the saying of al-Kalbi. Ibn Zayd said: By God, whoever follows him is most deserving that he call to what he called to, mentioning the Qur'an and good instruction, and forbidding the disobedience of God.

It is said: Its meaning is: I and whoever follows me are upon insight. The meaning is that just as I am upon insight, so too whoever believed in me and followed me is upon insight. Ibn ʿAbbas said: That refers to the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), who were upon the best path and the most direct guidance, the source of knowledge, the treasure of faith, and the army of the Most Merciful.

﴿And glory be to God﴾, meaning: and say, "Glory be to God," exalting Him above what they associate with Him. ﴿And I am not of those who associate others with God.﴾

﴿And We did not send before you [O Muhammad] except men﴾, not angels, ﴿to whom We revealed, from among the people of the cities﴾, meaning from among the people of the settled towns, not the people of the desert, because the people of the towns are more intelligent, more virtuous, more knowledgeable and more forbearing.

﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾ That is, these idolaters who deny your prophethood. He informs of the affair of the earlier disbelieving nations so that they might take heed. ﴿And the Home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God.﴾ God, glorified is His praise, says: This is what We did in this world to the people of Our guardianship and obedience, that We delivered them at the descent of the punishment; and what is in the Home of the Hereafter is better for them. So the previously mentioned element was omitted because the context indicates it. The "home" is attributed to "the Hereafter" without any disagreement, for its glorification, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is the truth of certainty﴾ [Surah al-Waqiʿah 56:95], and the expressions "the first year" (ʿam al-awwal), "the last night" (barihat al-ula), and "Thursday" and "Rabiʿ al-akhir" (where the adjective is attached to the noun in a similar manner). The poet said:

Even if the dwellings of ʿAbs were to be effaced upon you,
You would recognize humiliation with the recognition of certainty.

Meaning: recognition (ʿirfanan).

﴿Will they not reason?﴾, meaning, will they not believe?

﴿Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our victory came to them.﴾ The reciters differed regarding His saying: ﴿kudhibū﴾ (they had been denied).

A group read it with light vocalization (takhfif) [Refer to Tafsir al-Qurtubi 9/275 and Zad al-Masir; there is difference in the names, so consider carefully]. This is the reading of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (ʿalayhi s-salam), Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Masʿud, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, ʿIkrima, al-Dahhak, ʿAlqama, Masruq, al-Nakhaʿi, Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, al-Aʿmash, ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar al-Hamdani, Abu Ishaq al-Subaʿi, Ibn Abi Layla, ʿAsim, Hamza, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn and his son Muhammad ibn ʿAli and his son Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, ʿAbdullah ibn Muslim, and Ibn Yasar. Al-Kisa'i and Abu ʿUbayda chose it.

It is reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he recited ﴿wa-ẓannū annahum qad kudhibū﴾ with light vocalization. This is also the reading of ʿAʾisha, [Hurqul] al-Aʿraj, Nafiʿ, al-Zuhri, ʿAta ibn Abi Rabah, ʿAbdullah ibn Kathir, ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith, Abu Rajaʾ and al-Hasan. Also of Qatada, Abu ʿAmr, ʿIsa, Salam, ʿAmr ibn Maymun, and Yaʿqub; and it is also reported from the Prophet (ﷺ).

As for one who reads with light vocalization, its meaning is: until, when the messengers despaired of the faith of their people, and their people thought that the messengers had lied to them regarding the existence of the punishment.

Shuʿayb ibn al-Hajjaj reported from Ibrahim from Abu Hamza al-Jazari, who said: I prepared food and invited some of our companions, including Saʿid ibn Jubayr. I sent to al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, but he refused to come to me, so I went to him and did not leave him until he came. He said: A young man from Quraysh asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr, saying: "O Abu ʿAbd Allah, how do you read this word? When I reach it I wish I did not read this surah: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought they had been denied﴾." He said: Yes, [it means] until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing them, and the ones they were sent to thought the messengers had lied to them.

He said: Al-Dahhak said: I have never seen a man today who is called to knowledge and hesitates. If I had traveled to Yemen for this alone, it would have been little.

Some said: The meaning of the verse according to this reading is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾ of the faith of their people, and the messengers thought that they had been denied in what they found of victory. This is the report of Ibn Abi Mulayka from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: They had called, and they became weak and despaired, and thought they had been let down. Then the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him say, "When is the victory of God?"﴾ and so on.

As for one who reads with heavy vocalization (tashdid), its meaning is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing in them, and the messengers became certain (istayqanat) that their nations had denied them, Our victory came to them.﴾ According to this interpretation, ẓann (thought) carries the meaning of ʿilm (knowledge) and yaqin (certainty), like the saying of the poet:

So I said to them, "Be certain (ẓannū) of two thousand armored men,
their nobles in the woven Persian mail."

That is: be certain. This is the meaning of the statement of Qatada.

Some said: The meaning of the verse according to this reading is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of those among their people who denied them from believing them, and the messengers thought that those who had believed in them and affirmed them had denied them and apostatized from their religion because of their slowness in victory, Our victory came to them.﴾ This is the meaning of the statement of ʿAʾisha.

Mujahid read ﴿kudhibū﴾ with a fatha on the kaf and the dhal, lightened, and it has two interpretations. One: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired that their people would be punished, and their people thought that the messengers had lied, the messengers came, Our victory came.﴾ The second: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of their people's faith, and the messengers thought that their people had lied against God through their disbelief.﴾ On this interpretation, ẓann means certainty. God knows best.

﴿So whom We willed was delivered﴾, at the descent of the punishment, and they are the obedient and the believers. ﴿And Our punishment is not repelled from the criminal people﴾, meaning the idolaters.

The reciters differed regarding His saying: ﴿fa-nujjiya﴾ (so whom We willed was delivered). The majority of reciters read it as ﴿fa-nunajjī﴾ with two nuns, meaning: So We do this to them. Al-Kisa'i assimilated one of the two nuns into the other and read ﴿fa-nujjiya﴾ with one nun and a shadda on the jim. ʿAsim read it with a damma on the nun, a shadda on the jim, and a fatha on the ya, in the passive form (madhhab ma lam yusammi fa'iluhu). Abu ʿUbayd chose this reading because it is in the codex of ʿUthman, and the codices of the other regions have one nun. Ibn Muhaysin read ﴿fa-najā man nashāʾ﴾ with a fatha on the nun and light vocalization, as a past verb. Its grammatical position (mahalluhu) is nominative in the reading of ʿAsim and Ibn Muhaysin, and accusative in the reading of the rest.

This is the reading of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (ʿalayhi s-salam), Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Masʿud, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, ʿIkrima, al-Dahhak, ʿAlqama, Masruq, al-Nakhaʿi, Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, al-Aʿmash, ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar al-Hamdani, Abu Ishaq al-Subaʿi, Ibn Abi Layla, ʿAsim, Hamza, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn and his son Muhammad ibn ʿAli and his son Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, ʿAbdullah ibn Muslim, and Ibn Yasar. Al-Kisa'i and Abu ʿUbayda chose it.

It is reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he recited ﴿wa-ẓannū annahum qad kudhibū﴾ with light vocalization. This is also the reading of ʿAʾisha, [Hurqul] al-Aʿraj, Nafiʿ, al-Zuhri, ʿAta ibn Abi Rabah, ʿAbdullah ibn Kathir, ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith, Abu Rajaʾ and al-Hasan. Also of Qatada, Abu ʿAmr, ʿIsa, Salam, ʿAmr ibn Maymun, and Yaʿqub; and it is also reported from the Prophet (ﷺ).

As for one who reads with light vocalization, its meaning is: until, when the messengers despaired of the faith of their people, and their people thought that the messengers had lied to them regarding the existence of the punishment.

Shuʿayb ibn al-Hajjaj reported from Ibrahim from Abu Hamza al-Jazari, who said: I prepared food and invited some of our companions, including Saʿid ibn Jubayr. I sent to al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, but he refused to come to me, so I went to him and did not leave him until he came. He said: A young man from Quraysh asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr, saying: "O Abu ʿAbd Allah, how do you read this word? When I reach it I wish I did not read this surah: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought they had been denied﴾." He said: Yes, [it means] until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing them, and the ones they were sent to thought the messengers had lied to them.

He said: Al-Dahhak said: I have never seen a man today who is called to knowledge and hesitates. If I had traveled to Yemen for this alone, it would have been little.

Some said: The meaning of the verse according to this reading is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired﴾ of the faith of their people, and the messengers thought that they had been denied in what they found of victory. This is the report of Ibn Abi Mulayka from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: They had called, and they became weak and despaired, and thought they had been let down. Then the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him say, "When is the victory of God?"﴾ and so on.

As for one who reads with heavy vocalization (tashdid), its meaning is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing in them, and the messengers became certain (istayqanat) that their nations had denied them, Our victory came to them.﴾ According to this interpretation, ẓann (thought) carries the meaning of ʿilm (knowledge) and yaqin (certainty), like the saying of the poet:

So I said to them, "Be certain (ẓannū) of two thousand armored men,
their nobles in the woven Persian mail."

That is: be certain. This is the meaning of the statement of Qatada.

Some said: The meaning of the verse according to this reading is: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of those among their people who denied them from believing them, and the messengers thought that those who had believed in them and affirmed them had denied them and apostatized from their religion because of their slowness in victory, Our victory came to them.﴾ This is the meaning of the statement of ʿAʾisha.

Mujahid read ﴿kudhibū﴾ with a fatha on the kaf and the dhal, lightened, and it has two interpretations. One: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired that their people would be punished, and their people thought that the messengers had lied, the messengers came, Our victory came.﴾ The second: ﴿until, when the messengers despaired of their people's faith, and the messengers thought that their people had lied against God through their disbelief.﴾ On this interpretation, ẓann means certainty. God knows best.

﴿So whom We willed was delivered﴾, at the descent of the punishment, and they are the obedient and the believers. ﴿And Our punishment is not repelled from the criminal people﴾, meaning the idolaters.

The reciters differed regarding His saying: ﴿fa-nujjiya﴾ (so whom We willed was delivered). The majority of reciters read it as ﴿fa-nunajjī﴾ with two nuns, meaning: So We do this to them. Al-Kisa'i assimilated one of the two nuns into the other and read ﴿fa-nujjiya﴾ with one nun and a shadda on the jim. ʿAsim read it with a damma on the nun, a shadda on the jim, and a fatha on the ya, in the passive form (madhhab ma lam yusammi fa'iluhu).
